Derive and implement radix-2 FFT algorithms and analyse their computational cost.
Design FIR filters by windowing, frequency sampling and equiripple methods, and IIR filters from analogue prototypes, to meet a specification.
Realise filters in direct, cascade, parallel and lattice structures and assess finite word-length effects.
Design decimators, interpolators and polyphase filter banks for multirate systems.
Apply DSP techniques to speech, audio and image processing problems and evaluate the results quantitatively.

syllabus.title: Discrete-time signals, sampling and quantisation
topics: Review of discrete-time signals, LTI systems, convolution, the DTFT and the z-transform
Analogue-to-digital and digital-to-analogue conversion; sampling and reconstruction in practice
Uniform quantisation, quantisation noise and SNR per bit; dithering
Fixed-point and floating-point number formats for DSP

syllabus.title: The discrete Fourier transform
topics: The discrete Fourier series and the DFT as samples of the DTFT; the DFT matrix
DFT properties: linearity, circular shift, symmetry, Parseval's theorem
Circular convolution and computing linear convolution with the DFT; zero padding
Block convolution for long signals: overlap-add and overlap-save
The discrete cosine transform and energy compaction

syllabus.title: The fast Fourier transform
topics: Computational cost of the direct DFT; the divide-and-conquer idea
Radix-2 decimation-in-time and decimation-in-frequency FFTs; butterflies, bit reversal and in-place computation
Mixed-radix and real-input FFTs; the inverse FFT
The Goertzel algorithm and detecting DTMF keypresses on a phone line
Implementing an FFT from scratch and validating it against a library routine

syllabus.title: FIR filter design
topics: Filter specifications: passband, stopband, ripple, transition width; linear phase and the four FIR types
Window method: rectangular, Hann, Hamming, Blackman and Kaiser windows
Frequency-sampling design
Optimal equiripple design with the Parks-McClellan algorithm
FIR structures: direct form, transposed form, cascade and lattice
Removing 50 Hz mains interference and baseline wander from an ECG recording

syllabus.title: IIR filter design
topics: Analogue prototypes: Butterworth, Chebyshev types I and II, and elliptic filters
Impulse invariance and the bilinear transform with frequency prewarping
Frequency transformations to high-pass, band-pass and band-stop filters
IIR structures: direct forms I and II, transposed forms, cascade of second-order sections, parallel form
Finite word-length effects: coefficient quantisation, round-off noise, overflow, scaling and limit cycles
Choosing between FIR and IIR: phase, cost, stability and latency

syllabus.title: Multirate processing
topics: Downsampling and upsampling in time and frequency
Decimation and interpolation filters; rational sampling-rate conversion
Polyphase decomposition and efficient multirate implementations
Two-channel filter banks, quadrature mirror filters and perfect reconstruction
Oversampling and sigma-delta converters

syllabus.title: Spectral analysis
topics: Spectral analysis with the DFT: leakage, resolution, windowing and zero padding
The short-time Fourier transform and spectrograms; time-frequency trade-offs
Random signals: autocorrelation and power spectral density
Non-parametric estimation: periodogram, Bartlett and Welch methods
Parametric estimation: autoregressive models and the Yule-Walker equations
Analysing grid frequency fluctuations and vibration from a cocoa-processing motor

syllabus.title: Optimal and adaptive filtering
topics: Linear prediction and the Levinson-Durbin recursion
The Wiener filter and the mean-square error criterion
Adaptive filters: LMS and normalised LMS; convergence and step size
Noise and echo cancellation for voice calls

syllabus.title: Audio and image processing applications
topics: Speech analysis: pitch detection, linear predictive coding and MFCC features for recognising Twi and Ewe keywords
Audio effects and equalisers; perceptual audio coding principles
Two-dimensional signals: the 2-D DFT and 2-D convolution
Image filtering: smoothing, sharpening, edge detection and median filtering
DCT-based image compression and JPEG for low-bandwidth delivery
Real-time constraints: latency, buffering and DSP processor architectures

courses.title: Embedded Systems

GPIO, timers and PWM
Interrupts
ADC and sensors
Serial communication: UART, I2C, SPI
Real-time scheduling basics
Low-power design

Valvano, Embedded Systems: Introduction to ARM Cortex-M Microcontrollers
White, Making Embedded Systems

Write bare-metal C for GPIO, timers, PWM, interrupts and ADC on an ARM Cortex-M or AVR board.
Design interrupt-driven and polled drivers and reason about latency and shared-data hazards.
Communicate with sensors and other devices over UART, I2C and SPI and decode the traffic on a logic analyser.

Estimate and reduce energy consumption with sleep modes, clock gating and duty cycling.

syllabus.title: Embedded systems and microcontroller architecture
topics: What makes a system embedded: constraints on cost, power, size, timing and reliability
Microcontroller anatomy: core, flash, SRAM, peripherals, buses, clock tree, reset
ARM Cortex-M and AVR compared; the memory map and memory-mapped registers
Toolchain: cross-compiler, linker script, startup code, flashing, debugging with a probe; simulators
Reading a datasheet and reference manual; writing the first blink in bare-metal C

syllabus.title: GPIO, timers and PWM

Driving LEDs, relays, seven-segment displays, keypads, character LCDs
Timer peripherals: prescalers, counters, compare and capture, overflow
Measuring time, generating delays and periodic events without blocking

syllabus.title: Interrupts

Watchdog timers and fault handlers

DAC and PWM-based analog output; driving a speaker
Digital sensors with pulse outputs: ultrasonic distance, DHT humidity

syllabus.title: Serial communication: UART, I2C, SPI

Other links: CAN, USB and wireless modules (Bluetooth, LoRa, GSM) in brief

syllabus.title: Real-time scheduling basics
topics: Timing requirements: hard and soft real time, deadlines, jitter

Pre-emptive multitasking: tasks, context switch, stacks; a tiny RTOS (FreeRTOS)
Rate-monotonic and earliest-deadline-first scheduling; utilisation bounds; priority inversion and inheritance
Inter-task communication: queues, semaphores, mutexes

syllabus.title: Low-power design
topics: Where energy goes: active, sleep, peripherals, radios; measuring current
Sleep modes, wake-up sources, clock scaling, peripheral gating
Duty cycling and event-driven design; battery and solar budgeting for a field sensor
Energy-aware firmware design for devices in rural Ghana

syllabus.title: Embedded software engineering and project
topics: Driver layering, hardware abstraction, configuration, code organisation
Testing embedded code: unit tests on the host, hardware-in-the-loop, logging
Robustness: brown-out, EMI, input validation, firmware update
Project: a complete device such as a weather station, irrigation controller or prepaid meter prototype

courses.title: Enterprise Resource Planning
topics: What ERP systems do
Finance and accounting modules
Supply chain and inventory
Human resources and payroll
ERP data models
Selecting and implementing ERP
ERP for small and medium enterprises
courses.description: How integrated enterprise systems run a business on one shared database: the purpose of ERP, finance and accounting, procurement, inventory and supply chain, sales, human resources and payroll, the master and transaction data models underneath, and how ERP is selected, implemented and adapted for small and medium enterprises. Students run complete order-to-cash, procure-to-pay and hire-to-retire cycles on a simulated company in the browser and trace every document to its journal entries and tables.
modelledOn: Monk and Wagner, Concepts in Enterprise Resource Planning
Magal and Word, Integrated Business Processes with ERP Systems
Sumner, Enterprise Resource Planning
ASCM (APICS), Certified in Planning and Inventory Management (CPIM)
outcomes: Explain what ERP systems do, how integration on a shared database differs from isolated departmental systems, and where their value comes from.
Execute and explain the finance, procurement, inventory, sales and HR processes in an ERP system and the postings each step creates.
Analyse ERP data models, distinguishing organisational structures, master data and transaction data.
Plan inventory and supply using reorder points, economic order quantity and material requirements planning.
Evaluate ERP options and plan an implementation covering selection, fit-gap analysis, data migration, testing and change management.
Recommend an appropriate ERP approach for a small or medium enterprise with limited budget and connectivity.

syllabus.title: What ERP systems do
topics: From isolated departmental systems to integrated enterprise systems; the single source of truth
ERP history: MRP, MRP II, ERP and cloud ERP; the major commercial and open-source products
Modules and how they share data; end-to-end business processes across departments
Benefits, costs and well-known ERP failures

syllabus.title: ERP data models
topics: Organisational structures: company, plant, warehouse, sales and purchasing organisations
Master data: customers, suppliers, materials, chart of accounts, employees; ownership and quality
Transaction data and document flow: orders, deliveries, invoices and payments linked by reference
The relational schema behind an ERP; header and line tables; tracing a document to its tables
Configuration versus customisation; extensions and APIs

syllabus.title: Finance and accounting modules
topics: General ledger, chart of accounts and automatic postings from operational modules
Accounts receivable and accounts payable; subledgers and reconciliation
Asset accounting and depreciation runs; bank reconciliation and mobile money settlements
Controlling: cost centres, profit centres and internal orders
Period-end closing and financial statements; multi-currency transactions in cedis and dollars
Taxes in the ERP: VAT and levies configured for Ghana

syllabus.title: Supply chain and inventory
topics: Procure-to-pay: purchase requisition, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice verification and three-way match
Order-to-cash: quotation, sales order, availability check, delivery, billing and payment
Inventory management: stock types, movements, valuation methods and cycle counting
Inventory planning: reorder points, safety stock, economic order quantity and ABC analysis
Production planning and material requirements planning; bills of materials and routings
A shea butter cooperative's supply chain from collection centres to export

syllabus.title: Human resources and payroll
topics: Organisational management: positions, jobs and reporting lines
Hire-to-retire: recruitment, onboarding, time and attendance, leave and exit
Payroll processing: gross pay, deductions, PAYE and SSNIT contributions, and posting payroll to the ledger
Employee self-service and access to sensitive personal data

syllabus.title: Reporting, integration and controls
topics: Operational reports, embedded analytics and links to a data warehouse
Integration with e-commerce, banks, mobile money and tax authority systems through APIs and files
Authorisations, roles and segregation of duties within the ERP
Audit trails and internal controls built into ERP processes

syllabus.title: Selecting and implementing ERP
topics: Business case and total cost of ownership; on-premise, hosted and SaaS deployment
Vendor selection: requirements, request for proposal, scoring, demonstrations and references
Fit-gap analysis and the choice between changing the process and modifying the software
Implementation approaches: big bang, phased and parallel; implementation methodologies
Data migration, testing, training, cutover and post go-live support
Change management, critical success factors and lessons from failed implementations

syllabus.title: ERP for small and medium enterprises
topics: SME needs and constraints: budget, skills, informal processes and cash-based trading
Open-source and cloud options such as Odoo and ERPNext; accounting packages as a first step
Working with intermittent power and connectivity: offline modes and mobile front ends
Implementing ERP for a pharmacy chain or an agro-processing firm in Ghana

syllabus.title: Trends and capstone
topics: Cloud ERP, two-tier ERP and composable architectures
Analytics, automation and machine learning embedded in ERP
ERP security and data protection obligations
Capstone: configuring and running the full business cycle of a simulated Ghanaian company with an implementation plan

courses.title: Epidemiology and Public Health Data
topics: Measures of disease frequency
Study designs in epidemiology
Surveillance systems
Outbreak investigation
Disease modelling: SIR models
Spatial epidemiology
Communicating public health data
courses.description: The quantitative methods of epidemiology and the data systems behind public health: measures of disease frequency and association, study designs and bias, surveillance systems, outbreak investigation, compartmental SIR models, spatial epidemiology and the communication of public health data. Practised with browser-based simulations and public datasets, working through African cases such as malaria incidence, cholera and meningitis outbreaks and district surveillance reports.
modelledOn: Rothman, Epidemiology: An Introduction
Gordis, Epidemiology
Vynnycky and White, An Introduction to Infectious Disease Modelling
WHO and Africa CDC, Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) Technical Guidelines
outcomes: Calculate and interpret incidence, prevalence, mortality rates and standardised rates and measures of association such as relative risk and odds ratios.
Choose an appropriate study design for a public health question and identify confounding, selection bias and information bias.
Describe how surveillance systems collect, analyse and act on data and evaluate a system's sensitivity, timeliness and representativeness.
Investigate an outbreak from case definition and line list through epidemic curves to control measures and a written report.
Build, simulate and fit SIR-type models and use them to estimate reproduction numbers and compare interventions.
Analyse and map spatial health data and communicate findings clearly and honestly to decision makers and the public.

syllabus.title: Epidemiology and measures of disease frequency
topics: The epidemiological approach: person, place and time; the epidemiological triangle; natural history of disease
Counts, proportions, ratios and rates; incidence (risk and rate), prevalence and their relationship
Mortality and morbidity measures: crude, specific and case fatality rates; maternal and under-five mortality
Direct and indirect standardisation; population pyramids and denominators from census data
Burden of disease: DALYs and YLLs; malaria, HIV and TB burden in sub-Saharan Africa
Confidence intervals for rates and proportions

syllabus.title: Measures of association and causation
topics: Risk difference, relative risk, odds ratio, attributable fraction
Two-by-two tables, chi-squared tests and confidence intervals
Causal inference: Bradford Hill considerations, counterfactuals, directed acyclic graphs
Screening and diagnostic tests: sensitivity, specificity, predictive values; rapid diagnostic tests for malaria

syllabus.title: Study designs in epidemiology
topics: Descriptive studies: case reports, case series, ecological and cross-sectional studies; demographic and health surveys
Cohort studies: prospective and retrospective, follow-up, person-time
Case-control studies: selecting controls, matching, why the odds ratio is used
Randomised controlled trials: randomisation, blinding, intention to treat; community and cluster trials such as bed net trials
Bias and confounding: selection, information, recall; stratification, adjustment and effect modification
Sample size and power in outline; ethics of research with human participants

syllabus.title: Surveillance systems
topics: Purposes and types of surveillance: passive, active, sentinel, syndromic, event-based, laboratory-based
Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response: priority diseases, case definitions, thresholds and weekly reporting
Notifiable diseases and the flow of reports from community to district to national level; DHIS2 for surveillance
Alert and epidemic thresholds; detecting aberrations with moving averages and statistical methods
Evaluating surveillance: sensitivity, positive predictive value, timeliness, completeness, representativeness
Community-based surveillance by community health volunteers; One Health and zoonotic surveillance

syllabus.title: Outbreak investigation
topics: The steps of an outbreak investigation from verifying the outbreak to communicating findings
Case definitions (suspected, probable, confirmed), line lists and case finding
Epidemic curves: point source, continuing and propagated outbreaks; incubation periods
Analytical studies in an outbreak: attack rates and food-specific risk tables
Control measures, contact tracing and declaring an outbreak over
Simulated investigations: a cholera outbreak in a coastal community, a meningitis season in the northern belt, a Lassa fever cluster

syllabus.title: Disease modelling: SIR models
topics: Compartmental models: SIR and SEIR differential equations; solving them numerically
The basic and effective reproduction numbers; herd immunity thresholds and vaccination coverage
Fitting models to incidence data; estimating growth rates and the reproduction number in real time
Stochastic models and early extinction; age structure and contact matrices
Modelling interventions: vaccination, isolation, treatment, vector control; malaria transmission in outline
Uncertainty and the limits of models; scenarios versus forecasts

syllabus.title: Spatial epidemiology
topics: Spatial data: points, polygons, rasters, coordinate systems; geocoding health facilities and cases
Choropleth maps, rates by district, small-number problems and smoothing
Clusters and hotspots: Snow's cholera map, spatial autocorrelation, scan statistics
Access to care and catchment areas; mapping malaria risk with environmental data

syllabus.title: Communicating public health data
topics: Choosing charts and tables for epidemiological data; honest axes, rates versus counts, uncertainty
Situation reports and epidemiological bulletins for district and national audiences
Risk communication with communities and the media; countering misinformation
Privacy and ethics in publishing health data; small-area disclosure risk and Data Protection Act 843
Project: an outbreak or surveillance analysis with a model, a map and a situation report

courses.title: Game Engine Programming
topics: The game loop
Rendering sprites and scenes
Input handling
Entity and component systems
Collision detection
Audio
Performance on low-end phones
courses.description: How a game engine works inside and how to build one: the game loop and timing, rendering sprites and scenes, input handling, entity and component systems, collision detection, audio, resource management and performance on low-end phones. Students write a small engine in JavaScript on the HTML canvas and WebGL piece by piece, profile it in the browser and ship a complete game on it.
modelledOn: Gregory, Game Engine Architecture
Nystrom, Game Programming Patterns
Ericson, Real-Time Collision Detection
McShaffry and Graham, Game Coding Complete
outcomes: Explain the architecture of a game engine and the responsibilities of its runtime subsystems.
Implement a game loop with fixed and variable time steps, frame pacing and interpolation.
Render sprites, tile maps and scenes efficiently with the canvas and WebGL, using batching, atlases and cameras.
Design entity and component systems and apply game programming patterns to organise game code.
Implement collision detection with bounding volumes and spatial partitioning, and integrate input and audio subsystems.
Profile and optimise a game to run smoothly on low-end Android phones with limited memory, CPU and battery.

syllabus.title: Engine architecture and the game loop
topics: What an engine is: runtime layers (platform, core systems, resources, rendering, physics, gameplay) and the tools pipeline
The game loop: process input, update, render; requestAnimationFrame and the browser event loop
Time: delta time, fixed time step with accumulator, interpolation between states, spiral of death
Frame rate, vertical sync, frame pacing and measuring frame time
Engine start-up and shut-down, configuration, logging and a debug overlay

syllabus.title: Rendering sprites and scenes
topics: 2D rendering with the canvas: sprites, transforms, layering and draw order
Sprite sheets and texture atlases; frame-based and skeletal animation; animation state machines
Tile maps: tile sets, layers, culling to the visible area, map editors and loading map files
Cameras and viewports: following, dead zones, screen shake, parallax and resolution independence
WebGL sprite batching: vertex buffers, a textured-quad shader, minimising draw calls and state changes
Scene graphs, render queues and particle effects

syllabus.title: Input handling
topics: Input devices in the browser: keyboard, mouse, touch, pointer events and gamepads
Polling versus events; input buffering and mapping raw input to game actions
Touch controls for phones: virtual joysticks, gestures, tap zones and hit-target sizing
Input latency, debouncing and combos; recording and replaying input for testing

syllabus.title: Entity and component systems
topics: From inheritance hierarchies to composition: the problems with deep game-object class trees
Entity-component-system architecture: entities as identifiers, components as data, systems as behaviour
Data-oriented design: structure of arrays, cache locality, archetypes and sparse sets
Game programming patterns: command, observer, state, component, object pool, update method, service locator
Messaging and events between systems; scripting gameplay and hot reloading
Saving and loading game state; serialisation of entities and components

syllabus.title: Collision detection
topics: Bounding volumes: circles, axis-aligned bounding boxes, oriented boxes and capsules; intersection tests
The separating axis theorem for convex polygons; point-in-polygon and ray casts
Broad phase: uniform grids, quadtrees, sweep and prune, bounding volume hierarchies
Continuous collision detection and tunnelling; swept tests
Collision layers and masks, triggers and resolving overlaps for tile-based and platform games
Measuring broad-phase performance as the number of entities grows

syllabus.title: Audio
topics: Digital audio basics: sampling, formats, compression and latency
The Web Audio API: audio context, buffers, gain and panning nodes, the browser autoplay policy
A sound manager: channels, priorities, pooling, music crossfades and ducking
Positional audio, procedural sound effects and keeping audio in sync with gameplay

syllabus.title: Resources, scenes and tools
topics: Resource management: loading, caching, reference counting and unloading assets
Asset pipelines: image compression, atlasing, audio encoding and bundling for the web
Scene management, transitions and loading screens; progressive loading on slow connections
Debugging tools: in-game console, entity inspector, collision visualisation and time scaling
Offline play with service workers and caching for intermittent connectivity

syllabus.title: Performance on low-end phones
topics: The target: entry-level Android phones with little RAM, slow CPUs and GPUs, and expensive mobile data
Profiling in the browser: frame timelines, CPU profiles, memory snapshots and GPU bottlenecks
Avoiding garbage-collection pauses: object pools, preallocated arrays and avoiding per-frame allocations
Reducing draw calls, overdraw and fill-rate cost; lower resolutions and adaptive quality settings
Battery, thermal throttling, download size and start-up time as design constraints

syllabus.title: Capstone: a complete game on the engine
topics: Integrating the subsystems: loop, renderer, input, ECS, collision and audio into one engine
Building a complete 2D game, such as a platformer about an Ananse story or an arcade game set in a Ghanaian market
Testing on a real low-end phone and meeting a frame-time and memory budget
Packaging as a progressive web app and documenting the engine's architecture

courses.title: Genomics and Next-Generation Sequencing
topics: Sequencing technologies
Read quality control
Read mapping
Genome assembly
Variant calling
Gene expression analysis
Pathogen genomics for disease surveillance
courses.description: Turning raw sequencing reads into biological answers: sequencing technologies and their error profiles, read quality control, mapping to a reference, de novo genome assembly, variant calling and annotation, RNA-seq gene expression analysis, and pathogen genomics for outbreak surveillance. Practised as complete analysis pipelines run on small public datasets with browser-based tools, working through cases such as Vibrio cholerae and Lassa virus genomes and human variants shaped by malaria.
modelledOn: Pevsner, Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics
Compeau and Pevzner, Bioinformatics Algorithms: An Active Learning Approach
Brown, Genomes
WHO, Global Genomic Surveillance Strategy for Pathogens with Pandemic and Epidemic Potential
outcomes: Compare short-read and long-read sequencing technologies and choose a platform, read length and depth suited to a genomic question.
Assess and clean raw reads using quality scores, adapter trimming and duplication metrics, and justify each filtering decision.
Map reads to a reference genome with indexed aligners and interpret SAM and BAM records, mapping quality and coverage.
Assemble a genome from reads with de Bruijn and overlap graph methods and evaluate the assembly with contiguity and completeness measures.
Call, filter and annotate genetic variants and analyse differential gene expression from RNA-seq counts with appropriate statistics.
Apply pathogen genomics to outbreak surveillance, from sample to lineage assignment and resistance prediction, and report the findings to public health teams.

syllabus.title: Genomes and sequencing technologies
topics: Genome organisation in bacteria, viruses and eukaryotes: genes, repeats, plasmids, ploidy; the human reference genome
Sanger sequencing and the move to massively parallel sequencing; cost and throughput
Illumina sequencing by synthesis: library preparation, cluster amplification, single-end and paired-end reads
Long-read technologies: nanopore sequencing (MinION) and PacBio HiFi; error profiles and when long reads are essential
Experimental design: coverage and depth (Lander-Waterman), multiplexing and barcodes, whole-genome versus exome versus amplicon
Portable sequencing for field surveillance: nanopore runs in national and regional laboratories in Africa

syllabus.title: Read quality control
topics: FASTQ in depth: Phred scores, encodings, per-base and per-read quality
Quality reports with FastQC and MultiQC: base composition, GC distribution, overrepresented sequences, duplication
Adapter and quality trimming; length filtering; removing host and contaminant reads
Quality control for nanopore reads: read length distributions and basecalling accuracy
Recording QC decisions so an analysis can be reproduced

syllabus.title: Read mapping
topics: Why mapping differs from classical alignment: speed, seeds and the scale of the problem
Indexing a reference: suffix arrays, the Burrows-Wheeler transform and the FM-index; backward search
Short-read aligners (BWA, Bowtie2) and long-read aligners (minimap2); paired-end constraints
SAM and BAM formats: flags, CIGAR strings, mapping quality; sorting, indexing and viewing with samtools
Coverage, insert size and duplicate marking; inspecting alignments in a genome browser

syllabus.title: Genome assembly
topics: The assembly problem: reads, overlaps, contigs and scaffolds; why repeats make it hard
Overlap-layout-consensus and string graphs for long reads
De Bruijn graphs from k-mers: Eulerian paths, choice of k, error correction, bubbles and tips
Assemblers in practice: SPAdes for bacteria, Flye for long reads; hybrid assembly
Evaluating assemblies: N50, misassemblies, BUSCO completeness, comparison with a reference
Genome annotation basics: gene prediction and functional labelling of a bacterial assembly

syllabus.title: Variant calling
topics: Types of variation: SNVs, indels, structural variants, copy-number variation
Genotype likelihoods and Bayesian variant calling; how base and mapping quality enter the model
Calling pipelines: GATK best practices and bcftools; base quality recalibration and joint genotyping
The VCF format; hard filtering versus model-based filtering; transition/transversion ratio as a sanity check
Variant annotation and effect prediction; population databases such as gnomAD and the under-representation of African genomes
Case study: the HbS allele, G6PD deficiency and other human variants shaped by malaria selection

syllabus.title: Gene expression analysis
topics: RNA-seq experimental design: replicates, depth, batch effects, stranded and poly-A libraries
Spliced alignment and pseudo-alignment for quantification (HISAT2, Salmon); counts per gene
Normalisation: library size, TPM, size factors; exploratory analysis with PCA and clustering
Differential expression with negative binomial models (DESeq2, edgeR); multiple testing and the false discovery rate
Interpreting results: volcano plots, gene set and pathway enrichment
Single-cell RNA-seq in brief

syllabus.title: Pathogen genomics for disease surveillance
topics: From sample to sequence in an outbreak: amplicon schemes, turnaround time and laboratory networks
Lineage and genotype assignment for SARS-CoV-2, Vibrio cholerae and Lassa virus; typing schemes such as MLST
Antimicrobial resistance prediction from genomes; resistance gene databases
Linking genomes to case data; sharing sequences through public archives and GISAID
Case study: genomic surveillance of cholera and Lassa fever in West Africa and the Africa CDC Pathogen Genomics Initiative

syllabus.title: Reproducible pipelines and project
topics: Workflow managers (Snakemake, Nextflow) and containers for reproducible pipelines
Compute, storage and cost on limited infrastructure; working with shared servers and the cloud
Ethics and governance of genomic data: consent, community engagement, benefit sharing, data sovereignty in Africa
Project: an end-to-end analysis of a public bacterial or viral outbreak dataset with a surveillance report

courses.title: Health Data Standards and Interoperability
topics: Why interoperability matters
Terminologies: ICD, SNOMED CT and LOINC
HL7 messaging
FHIR resources and APIs
Patient identity and matching
Health information exchanges
Building a FHIR integration
courses.description: Making health systems exchange data that both sides understand: the levels of interoperability, clinical terminologies such as ICD, SNOMED CT and LOINC, HL7 version 2 messaging and CDA documents, FHIR resources and RESTful APIs, patient identity and record matching, health information exchange architectures and a working FHIR integration. Practised hands-on with browser-based message parsers, terminology browsers and a FHIR server sandbox, linking simulated clinics, laboratories and a district reporting system.
modelledOn: HL7 International, FHIR R4 specification and HL7 Version 2 messaging standard
Benson and Grieve, Principles of Health Interoperability: FHIR, HL7 and SNOMED CT
WHO, International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10 and ICD-11)
IHE International, IT Infrastructure Technical Framework
outcomes: Explain technical, syntactic, semantic and organisational interoperability and the cost of its absence in a health system.
Code clinical data with ICD, SNOMED CT and LOINC and map between local codes and standard terminologies.
Parse, construct and validate HL7 version 2 messages and explain the structure of CDA clinical documents.
Model clinical data as FHIR resources and query and update a FHIR server through its RESTful API with appropriate security.
Design patient identification and record matching with master patient indexes and deterministic and probabilistic matching.
Design and build an integration between health applications through a health information exchange using IHE profiles and FHIR.

syllabus.title: Why interoperability matters
topics: Fragmented systems in practice: repeated tests, lost referrals, duplicate reporting, siloed vertical programmes
Levels of interoperability: foundational, structural, semantic and organisational
The standards landscape: HL7, ISO health informatics standards, CEN, IHE, WHO, DICOM, openEHR; how standards are developed
National digital health strategies and enterprise architectures; OpenHIE as a reference
A referral from a CHPS compound to a district hospital traced through systems that do not talk

syllabus.title: Terminologies: ICD, SNOMED CT and LOINC
topics: Terminologies, classifications and code systems: purpose, granularity, versioning
ICD-10 and ICD-11: chapters, coding rules, mortality and morbidity coding, use in insurance claims
SNOMED CT: concepts, descriptions, relationships, hierarchies, post-coordination and expression constraints
LOINC for laboratory tests and observations; UCUM units; RxNorm and ATC for medicines
Mapping local codes to standards; value sets and terminology services
Coding diagnoses and procedures for NHIS claims and district reports in Ghana

syllabus.title: HL7 messaging
topics: HL7 version 2: segments, fields, components, delimiters, encoding; MSH, PID, PV1, OBR and OBX segments
Message types and trigger events: ADT admissions and transfers, ORM orders, ORU results; acknowledgements
Interface engines and message routing, transformation and error handling
HL7 version 3 and the Reference Information Model in brief; why it saw limited adoption
Clinical Document Architecture: header, structured body, templates; discharge summaries and referral letters
Building a laboratory results interface between a hospital laboratory and a records system

syllabus.title: FHIR resources and APIs
topics: FHIR principles: resources, references, data types, JSON and XML representations
Core resources: Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Encounter, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, Immunization
RESTful interactions: read, search with parameters and chaining, create, update, delete, history; bundles and transactions
Profiles, extensions and implementation guides; validating resources against profiles
Terminology in FHIR: CodeSystem, ValueSet, ConceptMap and terminology operations
Security: SMART on FHIR, OAuth 2.0 scopes, audit events and consent resources
Bulk data export and FHIR for public health reporting

syllabus.title: Patient identity and matching
topics: Why identity is hard: naming conventions, missing birth dates, shared phone numbers, transliteration
Master patient indexes and enterprise identifiers; national IDs such as the Ghana Card and NHIS numbers
Deterministic and probabilistic record linkage; the Fellegi-Sunter model, blocking and match thresholds
Measuring matching quality: false matches versus missed matches and their clinical risk
Biometrics and privacy-preserving linkage; IHE PIX and PDQ profiles

syllabus.title: Health information exchanges
topics: Exchange architectures: point-to-point, hub and spoke, federated and centralised models
OpenHIE components: interoperability layer, client registry, facility registry, health worker registry, shared health record, terminology service
IHE profiles for document sharing (XDS) and mobile access (MHD)
Aggregate exchange with ADX and linking patient-level systems to DHIS2
Governance, consent, data sharing agreements and Data Protection Act 843 obligations
Case studies of national health information exchanges in Africa

syllabus.title: Building a FHIR integration
topics: Requirements and data mapping from a clinic system to FHIR resources
Implementing a client that searches, creates and updates resources against a FHIR server
Testing with validators and test servers; conformance statements and capability statements
Error handling, retries and offline queues for unreliable connections
Project: an integration that sends immunisation or laboratory data from a simulated clinic to a shared record and a district report

courses.title: Human-Computer Interaction
topics: Usability principles and heuristics
User research and personas
Prototyping and wireframes
Interaction design patterns
Accessibility
Usability evaluation
Designing for low-bandwidth and mobile users
courses.description: Designing software that people can actually use: research, prototyping, interaction design, accessibility and evaluation, carried through a full design cycle with real users on real phones. Taught to the depth of a leading human-computer interaction design course.
modelledOn: Norman, The Design of Everyday Things
Rogers, Sharp and Preece, Interaction Design: Beyond Human-Computer Interaction
Krug, Don't Make Me Think
W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
outcomes: Apply usability principles and Nielsen's heuristics to critique and improve an interface.
Plan and run user research with interviews, observation and surveys and synthesise personas and journey maps.
Produce sketches, wireframes and interactive prototypes at increasing fidelity.
Choose and apply interaction design patterns for navigation, input, feedback and error handling.
Design for accessibility and verify against WCAG with assistive technology.
Run usability tests and controlled studies, analyse the data, and design for low-bandwidth mobile users.

syllabus.title: Foundations and usability principles
topics: Human-centred design and the design cycle; what usability means (ISO 9241)
Human capabilities: perception, memory, attention, Fitts's law, Hick's law, Gestalt principles
Norman's principles: affordances, signifiers, mapping, feedback, conceptual models
Nielsen's ten heuristics; heuristic evaluation of a Ghanaian banking app
Ethics in design: dark patterns, consent, inclusion

syllabus.title: User research and personas
topics: Needfinding: interviews, contextual inquiry, observation, diary studies, surveys
Recruiting participants and research ethics; working across languages and literacy levels
Affinity diagrams and synthesis; personas, scenarios, journey maps, point-of-view statements
Task analysis and hierarchical task analysis
Field exercise: researching market traders, students or clinic staff

syllabus.title: Ideation, prototyping and wireframes
topics: Brainstorming, sketching, storyboards, crazy eights
Low-fidelity paper prototypes and Wizard-of-Oz testing
Wireframes and information architecture; card sorting; navigation structures
Medium and high-fidelity prototypes in Figma or Penpot; design systems and components
Choosing fidelity for the question you need answered

syllabus.title: Interaction design patterns and visual design
topics: Patterns for navigation, search, forms, lists, onboarding, notifications, empty states and errors
Direct manipulation, modes, undo, progressive disclosure, defaults
Visual design: layout and grids, typography, colour, hierarchy, icons; platform guidelines (Material, iOS)
Microinteractions, animation and feedback; responsiveness and perceived performance
Designing for voice, USSD and feature phones; multilingual interfaces

syllabus.title: Accessibility
topics: Disability, situational impairment and universal design
WCAG principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, robust) and success criteria
Screen readers, keyboard navigation, captions, contrast, text size, motion
Testing with assistive technology and automated checkers; accessible forms and charts

syllabus.title: Implementing interfaces
topics: Model-view-controller and component architectures; state and events
Building the prototype for real: web (HTML/CSS/JS or React) or mobile; responsive layout
Input handling, validation and feedback; offline states
Instrumenting an interface with analytics

syllabus.title: Usability evaluation
topics: Formative versus summative evaluation; think-aloud usability testing; task design and metrics
Heuristic evaluation and cognitive walkthrough
Controlled experiments and A/B tests: hypotheses, variables, within and between subjects, basic statistics
Questionnaires: SUS, NASA-TLX; analysing qualitative data
Reporting findings and iterating on the design

syllabus.title: Designing for low-bandwidth and mobile users
topics: Constraints: small screens, touch, intermittent 2G/3G, data cost, shared devices, low-end phones
Performance budgets, offline-first, progressive web apps, lightweight assets
Lessons from M-Pesa, WhatsApp, Jumia and USSD services
Final project: a complete design cycle from research to tested prototype

courses.title: IT Project Management
topics: Project management context and processes
Integration management
Scope management
Time management (networks, CPM/PERT)
Cost management
Quality management
Resource management
Communications management
Risk management
Stakeholder management
courses.description: Managing IT projects through all ten knowledge areas, from charter to closure, with the quantitative tools of scheduling, cost and risk and the agile practices that modern software teams use. Taught to the depth of the professional project management body of knowledge.
modelledOn: PMI, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK, 6th and 7th editions)
Schwalbe, Information Technology Project Management
Scrum Guide and the Agile Practice Guide
outcomes: Explain the project life cycle, process groups and the role of the project manager in an IT organisation.
Write a project charter, scope statement and work breakdown structure for an IT project.
Build a network diagram, compute the critical path and PERT estimates, and resource-level a schedule.
Estimate and control costs with earned value management.
Plan quality, resources, communications and stakeholder engagement for a project.
Identify, analyse and respond to risks quantitatively and qualitatively, and apply agile methods where they fit.

syllabus.title: Project management context and processes
topics: Projects, programmes and portfolios; the triple constraint and beyond
The project life cycle; process groups: initiating, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, closing
Organisational structures, PMO, the project manager's skills; why IT projects fail (Standish, local cases)
Predictive, iterative, incremental, agile and hybrid approaches
Project management software: MS Project, OpenProject, Jira

syllabus.title: Integration management

Traffic engineering
Regulation of telecommunications
courses.description: How telecommunication networks carry voice and data at scale: an overview of network structure, switching and signalling, transmission systems, optical-fibre and satellite communication, traffic engineering, and the regulation of telecommunications. Taught with browser-based simulations of links, switches and traffic loads, so students dimension networks, model blocking and trace a call or packet across the network without physical equipment.
modelledOn: Stallings, Data and Computer Communications
Rappaport, Wireless Communications: Principles and Practice
ITU-T recommendations and the ITU radio regulations
outcomes: Describe the structure of a telecommunication network from access to core.
Explain circuit and packet switching and the signalling that sets up and controls connections.
Analyse transmission systems in terms of bandwidth, multiplexing, modulation and impairments.
Explain optical-fibre and satellite links and when each is the right choice.
Apply traffic engineering to dimension a network and estimate blocking and quality of service.
Describe how telecommunications are regulated and how spectrum and licensing are managed.

syllabus.title: Telecommunication networks overview
topics: The anatomy of a network: access, aggregation, core and interconnection
A brief history from the telegraph and telephone to mobile and all-IP networks
Analogue versus digital; bandwidth, bit rate and the Nyquist and Shannon limits
Standards and layering; the roles of the ITU, IEEE and regional bodies
Ghana's telecom landscape: the mobile operators, mobile money and the national backbone

syllabus.title: Switching and signalling
topics: Circuit, message and packet switching and the trade-offs between them
Space- and time-division switching inside a switch fabric
Signalling: in-band versus out-of-band and the common-channel signalling system
Call set-up, routing and teardown; numbering and addressing plans
The move from circuit-switched telephony to voice over IP and softswitches

syllabus.title: Transmission systems
topics: Transmission media: copper pair, coaxial, radio and fibre and their characteristics
Impairments: attenuation, noise, distortion and the link budget
Modulation: amplitude, frequency, phase and quadrature schemes
Multiplexing: frequency-, time-, wavelength- and code-division
Digital transmission hierarchies and the synchronous optical and digital hierarchies
Error detection and correction on a link

syllabus.title: Optical fibre communication
topics: Light guiding in fibre: total internal reflection, single- and multi-mode fibre
Sources, detectors and the optical link budget; attenuation and dispersion windows
Wavelength-division multiplexing and optical amplifiers for long-haul capacity
Submarine cable systems and the West Africa cables that carry the region's traffic
Fibre to the home and the access network; resilience when a cable is cut

syllabus.title: Wireless and mobile transmission
topics: Radio propagation: path loss, fading, multipath and interference
Cellular principles: cells, frequency reuse, handover and capacity
Generations of mobile networks and their air interfaces in brief
Spectrum as a scarce resource and why it is licensed
Mobile coverage realities in rural Ghana and the economics of extending it

syllabus.title: Satellite communication
topics: Orbits: geostationary, medium and low earth orbit and their latency and coverage trade-offs
The satellite link: uplink, downlink, transponders and the ground segment
Link budget, rain fade and frequency bands
Applications: backhaul for remote areas, broadcasting and new low-earth-orbit broadband
When satellite is the right choice for underserved communities

syllabus.title: Traffic engineering
topics: Offered traffic, the erlang and grade of service
The Erlang-B and Erlang-C models for blocking and queued systems
Dimensioning circuits and channels for a target blocking probability
Queueing basics for packet networks: utilisation, delay and loss
Quality of service, congestion and admission control
Dimensioning a mobile cell or a data link under a given load in the simulator

syllabus.title: Regulation of telecommunications
topics: Why telecoms are regulated: scarce spectrum, natural monopoly and universal service
Licensing, interconnection and number portability
Spectrum management and the ITU's role in international coordination
Ghana's National Communications Authority: licensing, SIM registration and consumer protection
Pricing, competition and universal-access funds for underserved areas
Capstone: plan and dimension a regulated access network for a Ghanaian district

courses.title: Theory of Computation
topics: Alphabets, strings and languages
Finite automata (DFA, NFA)
Regular expressions
Context-free grammars and pushdown automata
Turing machines
Decidability and the halting problem
Complexity classes P and NP
courses.description: What machines can compute, what they cannot, and what they cannot compute quickly: automata, grammars, Turing machines, decidability and complexity, with every machine built and run in the simulator. Taught to the depth of the standard automata and complexity course.
modelledOn: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation
Hopcroft, Motwani and Ullman, Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation
Lewis and Papadimitriou, Elements of the Theory of Computation
outcomes: Define languages formally and construct DFAs, NFAs and regular expressions for them and convert between the three.
Prove languages non-regular with the pumping lemma and minimise automata.
Write context-free grammars and pushdown automata and reason about ambiguity and normal forms.
Design Turing machines and explain the Church-Turing thesis and the variants of the model.
Prove problems undecidable by reduction from the halting problem.
Define P, NP, NP-completeness and reductions and classify problems accordingly.

syllabus.title: Alphabets, strings and languages
topics: Alphabets, strings, concatenation, powers, Kleene star; languages as sets of strings
Operations on languages: union, concatenation, star, complement
Proof techniques review: induction, contradiction, diagonalisation, pigeonhole
The Chomsky hierarchy as the map of the course

syllabus.title: Finite automata
topics: Deterministic finite automata: formal definition, transition function, acceptance; designing DFAs
Nondeterministic finite automata and epsilon-transitions; the subset construction
Closure properties of regular languages; product construction
DFA minimisation and the Myhill-Nerode theorem
Applications: lexical analysers, protocol and vending-machine controllers, pattern matching

syllabus.title: Regular expressions and the limits of regularity
topics: Regular expressions: syntax, semantics, algebraic laws
Equivalence of regular expressions and finite automata: Thompson's construction and state elimination
The pumping lemma for regular languages and non-regularity proofs
Decision problems for regular languages: emptiness, membership, equivalence
Regular expressions in practice: grep, validation of phone numbers and Ghana Card IDs

syllabus.title: Context-free grammars
topics: Grammars, derivations, parse trees, leftmost and rightmost derivations; ambiguity
Designing grammars for balanced brackets, arithmetic expressions, palindromes
Chomsky normal form and Greibach normal form; eliminating useless symbols, epsilon and unit productions
The CYK membership algorithm
Pumping lemma for context-free languages; closure and non-closure properties

syllabus.title: Pushdown automata
topics: Pushdown automata: definition, acceptance by final state and by empty stack
Equivalence of PDAs and context-free grammars
Deterministic PDAs and deterministic context-free languages; parsing preview
Decision problems for CFLs

syllabus.title: Turing machines
topics: The Turing machine: definition, configurations, acceptance, recognisers versus deciders
Designing machines for arithmetic and string problems; programming conventions
Variants: multi-tape, nondeterministic, enumerators and their equivalence
The Church-Turing thesis; other models: lambda calculus, random access machines, counter machines
Universal Turing machines and the idea of a stored program
Context-sensitive languages and linear bounded automata in brief

syllabus.title: Decidability and the halting problem
topics: Decidable problems for automata and grammars
Countability, diagonalisation and the existence of unrecognisable languages
The halting problem is undecidable; recognisable but not decidable; co-recognisability
Reductions: proving undecidability of emptiness, equivalence, Rice's theorem
Post correspondence problem; undecidable questions about software (virus detection, program equivalence)

syllabus.title: Complexity classes P and NP
topics: Time complexity of Turing machines; the class P and polynomial-time algorithms
The class NP: verifiers and nondeterministic machines; examples: SAT, clique, Hamiltonian path, subset sum
Polynomial-time reductions; NP-completeness and the Cook-Levin theorem
NP-complete problems and reductions among them; coNP; the P versus NP question
Dealing with hardness: approximation, heuristics, parameterised algorithms; space complexity and PSPACE in brief
Why this matters: cryptography, scheduling, timetabling at a university

courses.title: Web Application Security
topics: How web applications are attacked
Injection attacks
Cross-site scripting
Authentication and session flaws
Access control flaws
Server-side request forgery and file attacks
Defences and secure headers
courses.description: How web applications are attacked and defended: injection, cross-site scripting, broken authentication and session management, access-control flaws, server-side request forgery and file attacks, and the defences of input handling, output encoding and secure headers. Practised against deliberately vulnerable applications running on isolated virtual machines in the browser, so every attack and fix is carried out hands-on and safely.
modelledOn: Stuttard and Pinto, The Web Application Hacker's Handbook
OWASP Top Ten and OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
Hoffman, Web Application Security
outcomes: Explain the client-server web model and map an application's attack surface.
Find and exploit injection flaws including SQL and command injection and then fix them.
Detect and prevent cross-site scripting and cross-site request forgery.
Analyse authentication, session and access-control flaws and design correct controls.
Exploit and mitigate server-side request forgery and unsafe file upload and inclusion.
Harden an application with validation, output encoding, secure headers and a sound configuration.

syllabus.title: The web platform and its attack surface
topics: HTTP and HTTPS, requests, responses, methods, status codes and headers as an attacker sees them
The browser security model: the same-origin policy, cookies, storage and the DOM
Where trust boundaries lie: client, network, server, database and third-party services
Mapping an application: spidering, parameters, entry points and hidden functionality
Setting up an intercepting proxy and a deliberately vulnerable app on an isolated virtual machine

syllabus.title: How web applications are attacked
topics: The OWASP Top Ten as a map of common risks and how it is used
Trust and tainted data: never trusting input from the client
Threat modelling a feature such as a mobile-money top-up form
The economics of attacks on small-business and cafe-hosted sites in Ghana
Reading an application's behaviour through error messages and timing

syllabus.title: Injection attacks
topics: SQL injection: in-band, blind and error-based; extracting and modifying data
Exploiting a login bypass and data exfiltration against a lab database
Command, LDAP and NoSQL injection; the common root cause of mixing code and data
Defences: parameterised queries and prepared statements, least-privilege database accounts
Input validation and allow-listing as defence in depth

syllabus.title: Cross-site scripting
topics: Reflected, stored and DOM-based cross-site scripting and their impact
Stealing sessions and performing actions as the victim; keylogging a form
Context-aware output encoding for HTML, attributes, JavaScript and URLs
Content Security Policy and trusted types; sanitising rich input
Cross-site request forgery: tokens, same-site cookies and re-authentication

syllabus.title: Authentication and session flaws
topics: Credential handling: hashing and salting, password policy, and the weakness of SMS codes against SIM-swap
Flaws in login: user enumeration, weak reset flows, missing lockout and multi-factor
Session management: generation, transport, fixation, hijacking and timeout
Secure cookie attributes and token-based sessions
Account-recovery abuse and safe re-authentication for sensitive actions

syllabus.title: Access control flaws
topics: Vertical and horizontal privilege escalation
Insecure direct object references and broken function-level authorisation
Exploiting an identifier to read another user's wallet or records in a lab app
Designing enforced server-side authorisation and deny-by-default
Multi-tenant isolation and testing access control systematically

syllabus.title: Server-side request forgery and file attacks
topics: Server-side request forgery: reaching internal services and cloud metadata; blind variants
Unrestricted file upload leading to code execution; content-type and extension pitfalls
Local and remote file inclusion and path traversal
Insecure deserialisation and XML external entity attacks in brief
Defences: allow-lists, network egress restriction, safe storage and rendering of uploads

syllabus.title: Defences and secure headers
topics: A layered defence: validation, encoding, parameterisation, authorisation and logging
Security headers: HSTS, Content Security Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, frame controls and referrer policy
Secure configuration: TLS, cookie flags, CORS and error handling that does not leak
Dependency and supply-chain risk; keeping components patched
A web application firewall as a stopgap, not a cure

syllabus.title: Building and testing a secure application
topics: Secure development lifecycle: requirements, design review, testing and verification against the ASVS
Automated and manual testing with OWASP ZAP and Burp Suite
Triaging and fixing a backlog of findings for a resource-constrained team
Capstone: attack a vulnerable application, then remediate it and prove the fixes hold

courses.title: Electronic Health Records
topics: What an electronic health record holds
Clinical workflows and documentation
Data models for patient records
Clinical decision support
Usability and clinician burden
Privacy, consent and access control
Implementing records in low-resource clinics
courses.description: Designing, using and implementing electronic health records: what a patient record holds, clinical workflows and documentation, data models from relational schemas to openEHR archetypes, clinical decision support, usability and clinician burden, privacy, consent and access control, and implementation in low-resource clinics. Taught through case-based simulations of an outpatient clinic and district hospital, where students configure, use and critique a working record system built in the browser.
modelledOn: Shortliffe and Cimino, Biomedical Informatics: Computer Applications in Health Care and Biomedicine
Hoyt and Hersh, Health Informatics: Practical Guide
ISO 13606 and openEHR, Electronic Health Record Communication and Reference Model
ISO 18308, Requirements for an Electronic Health Record Architecture
outcomes: Describe the content and structure of an electronic health record and distinguish EHRs, EMRs, personal health records and registries.
Analyse clinical workflows and design structured and unstructured documentation that supports care, reporting and billing.
Design data models for patient records with relational schemas, entity-attribute-value models and openEHR archetypes and templates.
Build rule-based clinical decision support and evaluate alerts for accuracy, relevance and alert fatigue.
Evaluate EHR usability with heuristic and task-based methods and propose changes that reduce clinician burden.
Plan the implementation of a record system in a low-resource clinic, including privacy, access control, infrastructure, training and evaluation.

syllabus.title: What an electronic health record holds
topics: The purposes of a medical record: care, communication, continuity, legal record, billing, research
EHR, EMR, personal health record and registry distinguished; the longitudinal record
Record content: demographics, problem list, allergies, medications, encounters, vital signs, laboratory results, imaging, notes
From paper folders to electronic records: the problem-oriented medical record and SOAP notes
The patient folder in a Ghanaian outpatient department and what is lost between visits

syllabus.title: Clinical workflows and documentation
topics: Mapping clinical workflows: outpatient visits, admissions, ward rounds, maternity, laboratory and pharmacy
Structured versus free-text documentation; templates, forms and smart phrases
Computerised provider order entry and results management; closing the loop on orders
Medication management: prescribing, dispensing, administration records
Documentation for insurance: diagnosis coding and NHIS claims generated from the record
Copy-paste, note bloat and documentation quality

syllabus.title: Data models for patient records
topics: Relational schemas for patients, encounters, observations and orders; normalisation and its limits
Entity-attribute-value models for sparse clinical data; querying them efficiently
openEHR: the two-level model, reference model, archetypes and templates; ISO 13606
Concept-based models in OpenMRS: concepts, observations and forms
Representing time, versions, amendments and provenance in a legal record
Coding record data with SNOMED CT, ICD and LOINC; exporting to FHIR

syllabus.title: Clinical decision support
topics: Kinds of decision support: alerts, reminders, order sets, dose calculators, guidelines, dashboards
Rule-based systems and the knowledge base; Arden syntax and CDS Hooks in outline
Implementing guidelines: WHO IMCI for childhood illness, malaria test-and-treat, antenatal care schedules
Drug interaction and allergy checking; dose checking for children
Evaluating decision support: sensitivity, override rates, alert fatigue; the five rights of CDS
Machine learning for prediction in the record: promise, bias and validation

syllabus.title: Usability and clinician burden
topics: Usability principles applied to clinical software; cognitive load and interruption
Heuristic evaluation and task-based usability testing with clinicians; the System Usability Scale
Clinician burnout, time spent on documentation and the click burden
Usability-related patient safety incidents and how design prevents them

syllabus.title: Privacy, consent and access control
topics: Confidentiality, privacy and security; patient rights to access and correct their record
Ghana's Data Protection Act 843: lawful processing, sensitive health data, data subject rights, the Data Protection Commission
Access control models: role-based and attribute-based; break-the-glass emergency access
Consent models: opt-in, opt-out, granular consent; sensitive records such as HIV and mental health
Audit trails, monitoring and responding to breaches; encryption at rest and in transit
Secondary use for research and reporting: de-identification and its limits

syllabus.title: Implementing records in low-resource clinics
topics: Choosing a system: open-source versus commercial; OpenMRS, Bahmni and national systems such as Lightwave e-Health
Infrastructure: intermittent power and connectivity, offline-first design, solar power, device choice, local servers versus cloud
Data migration from paper registers, backup and disaster recovery
Change management: training, super-users, champions, workflow redesign, parallel running
Monitoring adoption and evaluating impact on care quality and efficiency
Case studies of EHR rollouts in Ghana, Rwanda, Kenya and Malawi

syllabus.title: Project
topics: Specifying requirements for a chosen clinic and its workflows
Configuring forms, decision rules and access roles in a simulated record system
Usability testing with realistic clinical scenarios
Project: an implementation plan and working prototype record for a rural health centre

courses.title: Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing
topics: Rules of engagement and the law
Reconnaissance
Scanning and enumeration
Exploitation
Password attacks
Post-exploitation
Reporting findings
courses.description: Conducting an authorised penetration test end to end: rules of engagement and the law, open-source and active reconnaissance, scanning and enumeration, exploitation and password attacks, post-exploitation and privilege escalation, and reporting findings with remediation. Practised only against isolated virtual machines and simulated networks in the browser, with every exercise scoped and authorised so techniques are learned lawfully.
modelledOn: Weidman, Penetration Testing: A Hands-On Introduction to Hacking
Engebretson, The Basics of Hacking and Penetration Testing
OWASP Testing Guide and NIST SP 800-115
Offensive Security Certified Professional (OSCP) objectives
outcomes: Scope an engagement and work within rules of engagement, authorisation and the relevant law.
Gather intelligence on a target with open-source and active reconnaissance.
Scan and enumerate hosts, services and versions to build an attack surface map.
Exploit vulnerabilities and crack passwords against authorised lab targets.
Escalate privilege, move laterally and establish persistence during post-exploitation.
Write a clear penetration test report that prioritises findings and recommends remediation.

syllabus.title: Rules of engagement and the law
topics: Why authorisation is everything: the line between a penetration test and a crime
Ghana's Cybersecurity Act 2020 and Data Protection Act 843; the Cyber Security Authority and lawful disclosure
Scoping: targets, exclusions, time windows, permitted techniques and emergency contacts
Rules of engagement, get-out-of-jail letters, data handling and confidentiality
Penetration testing methodologies and standards; types of test: black, grey and white box
Professional ethics and responsible disclosure

syllabus.title: The tester's environment
topics: Building an isolated lab of virtual machines and a simulated network in the browser
A testing distribution and its toolchain; keeping test traffic off production
Note-taking, evidence capture and command logging for a defensible report
Networking refresher: addressing, ports, protocols and the OSI layers as they matter to testing

syllabus.title: Reconnaissance
topics: Passive open-source intelligence: WHOIS, DNS records, certificate transparency, search and social media
Footprinting an organisation: employees, technologies, leaked credentials and metadata
Active reconnaissance and when passive crosses into active
Mapping the external attack surface, including exposed mobile-money and SIM-registration portals
Organising findings into a target profile

syllabus.title: Scanning and enumeration
topics: Host discovery and port scanning with nmap; scan types, timing and evasion basics
Service and version detection and operating-system fingerprinting
Vulnerability scanning with OpenVAS and interpreting results without over-trusting them
Enumerating services: web, SMB, SNMP, SMTP, DNS and databases
Turning scan output into a prioritised list of likely entry points

syllabus.title: Exploitation
topics: From vulnerability to working exploit; matching a service version to a known flaw and CVE/CVSS
Using an exploitation framework: payloads, listeners and sessions
Common server-side flaws: unpatched services, default credentials, misconfigurations
Client-side and social-engineering vectors in a controlled lab
Verifying impact without damaging the target; avoiding denial of service

syllabus.title: Password attacks
topics: Where credentials live: hashes, caches, configuration files and memory
Online attacks: brute force, dictionary, spraying and credential stuffing against lab services
Offline cracking of captured hashes with John the Ripper and hashcat; wordlists and rules
Default and reused passwords; the weakness of SMS one-time codes and SIM-swap risk
Defences: strong hashing, lockout, multi-factor authentication

syllabus.title: Post-exploitation
topics: Local situational awareness after a foothold: users, processes, network and stored secrets
Privilege escalation on Linux and Windows: misconfigurations, weak permissions, kernel and service flaws
Lateral movement and pivoting through a simulated internal network
Persistence, and the difference between a test artefact and real-world stealth
Collecting proof of access and cleaning up afterwards

syllabus.title: Web and network attack techniques
topics: Web application testing against the OWASP Top Ten: injection, broken authentication, access control
Intercepting proxies and request manipulation with Burp Suite and OWASP ZAP
Network attacks in the lab: sniffing, spoofing and man-in-the-middle
Wireless assessment basics against a simulated access point

syllabus.title: Reporting findings
topics: Structure of a penetration test report: executive summary, methodology, findings, evidence
Rating severity with likelihood and impact; CVSS as an input, not the whole story
Writing actionable remediation that a stretched IT team in a cafe or school can apply
Re-testing and verifying fixes; the debrief
Capstone: a full authorised test of a simulated small-business network and a written report

courses.title: Game Physics and Simulation
topics: Kinematics and numerical integration
Forces and Newton's laws
Collision response
Rigid body dynamics
Particles and springs
Fluids and cloth
Stability and determinism
courses.description: The physics behind games and interactive simulations: kinematics and numerical integration, forces and Newton's laws, particles and springs, collision detection and response, rigid body dynamics with constraints, fluids and cloth, and keeping simulations stable and deterministic. Every method is derived, then implemented and visualised in a browser physics sandbox where students compare integrators, break simulations on purpose and tune them to run in real time on a phone.
modelledOn: Millington, Game Physics Engine Development
Eberly, Game Physics
Ericson, Real-Time Collision Detection
Bridson, Fluid Simulation for Computer Graphics
outcomes: Model motion with vectors and kinematics and implement explicit, semi-implicit and higher-order numerical integrators.
Apply Newton's laws to compute forces such as gravity, drag, friction and springs and simulate particle systems.
Detect collisions and resolve them with impulses, restitution and friction for particles and rigid bodies.
Simulate rigid body dynamics in 2D and 3D, including rotation, inertia tensors, contacts and joint constraints.
Implement mass-spring cloth and particle-based fluids and explain the trade-offs between accuracy and speed.
Analyse the stability, energy behaviour and determinism of a simulation and design it for networked and replayable games.

syllabus.title: Vectors, kinematics and the simulation loop
topics: Vector algebra for physics: dot and cross products, projections, normalisation and coordinate frames
Kinematics: position, velocity and acceleration; projectile motion and analytic solutions
The physics step inside the game loop: fixed time steps, accumulators and rendering interpolation
Units, scales and choosing world dimensions for a game; floating-point precision

syllabus.title: Numerical integration
topics: Ordinary differential equations as the model of motion; initial value problems
Explicit Euler, semi-implicit (symplectic) Euler and velocity Verlet; local and global error
Runge-Kutta methods (RK2, RK4) and when the extra cost is worth it
Stability: stiff systems, the effect of step size, energy drift and damping
Implicit integration for stiff springs; position-based approaches as an alternative
Comparing integrators on an orbit and a spring and plotting energy over time

syllabus.title: Forces and Newton's laws
topics: Newton's three laws, mass and momentum; force accumulation in an engine
Gravity, drag (linear and quadratic), buoyancy and friction (static and kinetic)
Force generators and registries; game-tuned forces versus physically accurate ones
Projectiles and vehicles: a thrown ball, a bicycle on a laterite road, an okada braking

syllabus.title: Particles and springs
topics: Particle systems: emitters, lifetimes and effects such as smoke, fire, dust and rain
Hooke's law, damped springs and critical damping; bungees and anchored springs
Mass-spring networks: structural, shear and bending springs; soft bodies
Stiff springs and instability; fake springs and position constraints
Rods, cables and simple particle contact constraints
Building a rope bridge or a hanging chain in the sandbox

syllabus.title: Collision detection for physics
topics: Broad phase and narrow phase: bounding volume hierarchies, grids and sweep and prune
Contact generation: sphere, box and plane tests, the separating axis theorem and contact manifolds
GJK and EPA for convex shapes; penetration depth and contact normals
Continuous collision detection and time of impact against tunnelling

syllabus.title: Collision response
topics: Impulse-based response: relative velocity, coefficient of restitution and conservation of momentum
Friction impulses and the Coulomb friction cone
Resolving interpenetration: projection, Baumgarte stabilisation and slop
Resting contact, stacking and sleeping bodies
Simulating a game of marbles or oware seeds bouncing in a board

syllabus.title: Rigid body dynamics
topics: Rotational kinematics: angular velocity, orientation as angles, matrices and quaternions
Torque, angular momentum, moment of inertia and the inertia tensor in world and body space
Integrating rigid bodies in 2D and 3D; normalising quaternions and avoiding drift
Contacts on rigid bodies: impulses at contact points and the effect on spin
Constraints and joints: distance, hinge, ball and socket; sequential impulse solvers and warm starting
Building a 2D rigid body engine with stacking boxes and a ragdoll

syllabus.title: Fluids and cloth
topics: Cloth as a mass-spring system and with position-based dynamics; collisions and self-collision
Fluid models: Eulerian grids versus Lagrangian particles; the Navier-Stokes equations in outline
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics: kernels, density, pressure and viscosity
Grid-based smoke and water: advection, diffusion and pressure projection (stable fluids)
Height-field water and other cheap approximations for phones
Simulating a flag in the wind or kente cloth draped over a figure

syllabus.title: Stability and determinism
topics: Sources of instability: large time steps, stiff constraints, mass ratios and accumulated error
Determinism: floating-point differences across devices, fixed-point arithmetic and fixed update order
Deterministic lockstep and rollback netcode for multiplayer; replays from recorded input
Performance: island partitioning, sleeping, solver iterations and budgets on low-end phones
Capstone: a physics-driven browser game with a documented, stable and deterministic simulation

courses.title: Infrastructure as Code
topics: Why infrastructure as code
Declarative provisioning
Modules and reuse
State and drift
Configuration management
Testing infrastructure
GitOps workflows

Brikman, Terraform: Up and Running
Geerling, Ansible for DevOps
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate objectives

Design reusable, versioned modules and structure code for multiple environments and teams.
Manage remote state safely, detect and reconcile drift, and import existing resources.

Test infrastructure code, enforce policy and deliver changes through GitOps workflows with review and audit.

syllabus.title: Why infrastructure as code
topics: The problems of manual provisioning: snowflake servers, configuration drift, undocumented changes, slow recovery
Principles: everything in version control, idempotence, repeatability, disposability, small changes
Declarative versus imperative tools; provisioning versus configuration management; the tool landscape
Infrastructure as code in a team: code review for infrastructure, change records, blast radius

syllabus.title: Declarative provisioning

The workflow: init, plan, apply, destroy; reading a plan; the dependency graph and parallelism
Expressions: count, for_each, conditionals, dynamic blocks, built-in functions
Provisioning a VPC, subnets, security groups, virtual machines and object storage
Cloud-native alternatives in brief: CloudFormation, Bicep, Pulumi and OpenTofu

syllabus.title: Modules and reuse
topics: Writing modules: inputs, outputs, encapsulation; root and child modules
Module sources and versioning: registries, Git tags, semantic versioning
Composing modules into stacks; environment layouts for development, staging and production
Workspaces versus separate directories; managing differences with variable files
A reusable module for a three-tier web application used by several teams

syllabus.title: State and drift
