Remote backends, state locking and encryption; secrets that leak into state
Drift: how it happens, detecting it with refresh and plan, deciding whether to revert or adopt
Refactoring safely: moved blocks, state mv, rm and import; splitting large states
Recovering from a corrupted or lost state file

syllabus.title: Configuration management
topics: Ansible architecture: inventories, ad hoc commands, playbooks, modules, agentless SSH
Idempotent tasks, handlers, variables, facts and templates with Jinja2
Roles and collections; Ansible Vault for secrets
Immutable infrastructure: building golden images with Packer versus configuring running servers
Configuring a fleet of servers for a mobile money agent network, with Terraform and Ansible working together

syllabus.title: Testing infrastructure
topics: The testing pyramid for infrastructure: formatting, validation, static analysis, unit, integration, end-to-end
Linting and security scanning: tflint, Checkov, tfsec; ansible-lint
Native terraform test, Terratest and Molecule; ephemeral test environments and their cost
Policy as code with Open Policy Agent and Sentinel: blocking public buckets and enforcing data residency rules
Cost estimation in pull requests

syllabus.title: GitOps workflows
topics: GitOps principles: Git as the source of truth, declarative desired state, pull-based reconciliation
CI/CD for infrastructure: plan on pull request, apply on merge, approvals and protected environments
Argo CD and Flux for Kubernetes; Atlantis and similar tools for Terraform
Secrets in GitOps: sealed secrets, external secret operators, short-lived credentials with OIDC

syllabus.title: Operating infrastructure as code at scale
topics: Disaster recovery by rebuilding from code; tested recovery times
Platform engineering and self-service infrastructure; golden paths
Compliance and audit: change history, tagging standards, data residency under the Data Protection Act
Capstone: provision, configure, test and deliver through GitOps a complete environment, then detect and fix injected drift

courses.title: IT Service Management and Governance
topics: IT services and value
Service desk, incidents and problems
Change and release management
Service levels and agreements
IT governance frameworks
Risk, audit and compliance
Measuring IT performance
courses.description: How IT is run as a set of services that create value and how it is directed and controlled: service value and the service value system, the service desk, incident, problem, change and release management, service level agreements, IT governance frameworks, risk, audit and compliance, and measuring IT performance. Students work tickets, changes and outages on a simulated IT department in the browser, write service level agreements and run a governance and audit review against recognised frameworks.
modelledOn: AXELOS, ITIL 4 Foundation and the ITIL 4 practice guides
ISACA, COBIT 2019 Framework: Governance and Management Objectives
ISO/IEC 20000-1, Service management system requirements
ISO/IEC 38500, Governance of IT for the organisation
outcomes: Explain how IT services co-create value and describe the service value system, value chain and guiding principles.
Operate service desk, incident, request and problem management processes and prioritise work by impact and urgency.
Plan and assess changes and releases so that risk to live services is controlled.
Negotiate and write service level agreements with measurable targets and supporting agreements.
Apply IT governance, risk and audit frameworks to evaluate controls and compliance in an organisation.
Design metrics, dashboards and improvement plans that measure IT performance against business goals.

syllabus.title: IT services and value
topics: Services, products, service offerings and service relationships; value co-creation with consumers
Utility and warranty; outcomes, costs and risks
The four dimensions of service management: organisations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams and processes
IT as a cost centre versus a service provider; services at a university, a bank and a mobile operator

syllabus.title: The service value system
topics: The service value system: guiding principles, governance, the service value chain, practices and continual improvement
The seven guiding principles and how they shape decisions
Service value chain activities: plan, improve, engage, design and transition, obtain or build, deliver and support
Service catalogue and service portfolio management; mapping a value stream

syllabus.title: Service desk, incidents and requests
topics: Service desk structures: local, centralised, virtual and follow-the-sun; channels including phone, WhatsApp and SMS
Incident lifecycle: logging, categorisation, prioritisation by impact and urgency, diagnosis, escalation and closure
Major incident procedures and communication during outages
Service requests and request fulfilment; self-service portals and knowledge bases
Ticketing tools, queues and workload; first-contact resolution
Handling a mobile money outage on a public holiday

syllabus.title: Problem management
topics: Problems, known errors and workarounds; reactive and proactive problem management
Root cause analysis techniques: five whys, Ishikawa diagrams, fault tree and Kepner-Tregoe analysis
Trend analysis of incident data to find recurring problems
Blameless post-incident reviews

syllabus.title: Change and release management
topics: Change enablement: standard, normal and emergency changes; change authority and the change advisory board
Risk and impact assessment, change schedules and freeze periods
Release and deployment management: release planning, build, test, deployment and early life support
Configuration management: configuration items, the CMDB and service dependency maps
Integrating change management with DevOps, continuous delivery and automated testing
Planning a core banking upgrade with minimal downtime

syllabus.title: Service levels and agreements
topics: Service level management: service level requirements, targets and reviews
Service level agreements, operational level agreements and underpinning contracts
Availability, capacity, continuity and information security as warranty requirements
Supplier and relationship management; SLAs with internet and cloud providers serving low-bandwidth regions
Writing an SLA with measurable availability and response targets

syllabus.title: IT governance frameworks
topics: Corporate governance and IT governance; governance versus management
COBIT 2019: governance system principles, objectives, components, design factors and capability levels
ISO/IEC 38500 principles: evaluate, direct and monitor
ISO/IEC 20000 certification and how ITIL, COBIT and ISO standards fit together
IT strategy, investment decisions, IT steering committees and portfolio governance
Governance of public sector IT and e-government services in Ghana

syllabus.title: Risk, audit and compliance
topics: IT risk management: identification, assessment, risk appetite, treatment and risk registers
Internal controls: preventive, detective and corrective; general and application controls
The IT audit process: planning, evidence, testing controls and reporting findings
Compliance obligations: ISO/IEC 27001, data protection law and sector regulators such as the Bank of Ghana
Business continuity and disaster recovery planning; recovery time and recovery point objectives

syllabus.title: Measuring IT performance
topics: Critical success factors, KPIs and metrics; the metrics hierarchy from operational to strategic
Service metrics: availability, MTTR, MTBF, first-contact resolution and customer satisfaction
IT balanced scorecard and value measurement; cost of services and chargeback
Continual improvement models and maturity assessment
Service reporting dashboards for management

syllabus.title: Capstone
topics: Assessing the service management maturity of a simulated organisation
Running a governance and audit review against COBIT objectives
Producing a service improvement plan with prioritised actions and metrics
Presenting findings to an IT steering committee

courses.title: Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
topics: Propositional and first-order logic
Inference and resolution
Rules and expert systems
Ontologies and semantic networks
Reasoning under uncertainty
Bayesian networks
Planning
courses.description: Representing what a system knows and drawing conclusions from it: propositional and first-order logic, inference and resolution, rule-based and expert systems, ontologies and semantic networks, reasoning under uncertainty with Bayesian networks, and automated planning. Taught through browser-based reasoners, a Prolog-style interpreter and a Bayesian-network tool, so every representation is encoded and every inference is run and checked.
modelledOn: Brachman and Levesque, Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
Poole and Mackworth, Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents
outcomes: Represent knowledge in propositional and first-order logic with correct syntax and semantics.
Perform inference by resolution, unification and forward and backward chaining.
Build rule-based and expert systems and explain their conclusions.
Model a domain with ontologies and semantic networks and reason over them.
Represent and reason about uncertain knowledge with Bayesian networks.
Formulate and solve planning problems and connect them to knowledge representation.

syllabus.title: Knowledge, representation and reasoning
topics: What it means for a system to know something; the knowledge level versus the symbol level
Declarative versus procedural knowledge; the representation hypothesis
Entailment, soundness and completeness as the standards an inference method must meet
A survey of representations: logic, rules, frames, networks and probabilistic models
Applications: a crop-advisory assistant and a clinic triage aid for a rural health post

syllabus.title: Propositional logic
topics: Syntax and semantics; truth tables, models and logical equivalence
Validity, satisfiability and entailment; the deduction theorem
Normal forms: conjunctive and disjunctive; converting to clauses
Model checking and the DPLL procedure for satisfiability
Encoding a scheduling or configuration constraint as a propositional formula

syllabus.title: First-order logic
topics: Objects, relations and functions; constants, predicates, quantifiers and variables
Syntax and semantics of first-order logic; interpretations and models
Knowledge engineering: translating statements about a domain into first-order sentences
Expressing a family, organisation or geography ontology of Ghanaian regions and districts
The expressiveness and the decidability cost of first-order logic

syllabus.title: Inference and resolution
topics: Inference rules; forward and backward chaining with Horn clauses
Unification and the most general unifier
Resolution refutation: converting to clausal form and proving by contradiction
Soundness, completeness and the search involved in finding a proof
A Prolog-style interpreter: facts, rules, queries and backtracking
Negation as failure and the closed-world assumption

syllabus.title: Rules and expert systems
topics: Production systems: working memory, rule base and the inference engine
The match-resolve-act cycle and the Rete matching idea; conflict resolution
Forward- versus backward-chaining expert systems and when each fits
Explanation facilities and maintaining a rule base
Building a small diagnostic expert system for a common problem

syllabus.title: Ontologies and semantic networks
topics: Semantic networks and frames; inheritance, defaults and exceptions
Ontologies: classes, individuals, properties and the subsumption hierarchy
Description logics as the formal basis; the open-world assumption
The semantic web stack: RDF triples, RDFS and OWL; querying a knowledge graph
Reasoning tasks: classification, consistency checking and instance retrieval
Modelling a local agriculture or health domain as an ontology

syllabus.title: Reasoning under uncertainty
topics: Why strict logic is brittle for real knowledge; degrees of belief
Probability as a representation of uncertainty; the axioms and conditional probability
Bayes' rule and the naive Bayes assumption
Alternatives in brief: certainty factors, fuzzy logic and non-monotonic reasoning

syllabus.title: Bayesian networks
topics: Representing a joint distribution compactly; conditional independence and the graph
Constructing a network and its conditional probability tables for a domain
Exact inference by enumeration and variable elimination
Approximate inference by sampling when exact inference is too costly
A diagnosis network for malaria-like symptoms at a clinic as a worked example

syllabus.title: Planning
topics: Representing actions with preconditions and effects; the STRIPS and PDDL languages
State-space planning: forward and backward search and useful heuristics
Partial-order planning and planning graphs in brief
Planning as logical inference and as satisfiability; the link back to representation
Capstone: encode a logistics domain and have a planner produce and explain a plan

courses.title: Mobile and Cellular Networks
topics: Cellular concepts
Radio access and spectrum
GSM and 3G architecture
4G LTE
5G networks
Mobility management
Mobile data services and USSD
courses.description: How mobile networks are built and run end to end: cellular concepts and spectrum, the GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G architectures and their protocols, mobility management and roaming, and the SMS, USSD and data services that carry mobile money and everyday traffic. Every procedure, from attach and handover to a USSD session, is traced message by message in a network simulator, and a network is planned for real coverage and traffic targets.
modelledOn: 3GPP Technical Specifications for GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G NR
Sauter, From GSM to LTE-Advanced Pro and 5G: An Introduction to Mobile Networks and Mobile Broadband
Holma and Toskala, LTE for UMTS: Evolution to LTE-Advanced
Dahlman, Parkvall and Skold, 5G NR: The Next Generation Wireless Access Technology
outcomes: Explain the cellular concept and plan cells, frequency reuse and capacity for a given coverage area and traffic load.
Describe the radio access and core networks of GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G and the role of each network element and interface.
Trace signalling procedures such as attach, authentication, bearer setup, paging and handover across the protocol stack.
Analyse mobility management, location updating and roaming and their cost in signalling load and latency.
Design SMS, USSD and mobile data services and explain how the operator's network delivers and charges for them.
Compare 4G and 5G deployment options and assess them for urban and rural coverage in Ghana and the wider region.

syllabus.title: Cellular concepts and the evolution of mobile networks
topics: Generations of mobile networks from 1G analogue to 5G: what each added in services, data rate and architecture; the roles of 3GPP and the ITU
Cells, clusters and frequency reuse; reuse distance, co-channel interference and the signal-to-interference ratio
Capacity: cell splitting, sectoring, microcells, picocells and small cells; traffic in Erlangs and grade of service
Macro, micro and umbrella cell layers; coverage-limited versus capacity-limited cells
Mobile markets in Africa: operator landscape, tower sharing, mobile penetration and the rural coverage gap

syllabus.title: Radio access and spectrum
topics: Spectrum bands for 2G to 5G (sub-1 GHz, mid-band, millimetre wave); the coverage and capacity trade-offs of each
Spectrum licensing and auctions; the National Communications Authority and spectrum policy in Ghana
Duplexing (FDD, TDD) and multiple access (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA, OFDMA) as used by each generation
Link budget and cell range; why low bands matter for rural cell coverage
Base station hardware: antennas, remote radio heads, baseband units; backhaul over microwave, fibre and satellite

syllabus.title: GSM architecture and protocols
topics: GSM network elements: MS, SIM, BTS, BSC, MSC, HLR, VLR, AuC, EIR; the Um, Abis and A interfaces
Air interface: TDMA frames, timeslots, logical channels (traffic, broadcast, common and dedicated control)
Signalling: SS7, MAP and the GSM protocol stack (LAPDm, RR, MM, CM)
Call setup for mobile-originated and mobile-terminated calls; paging and channel assignment
Security: IMSI and TMSI, A3 and A8 challenge-response authentication, A5 ciphering and the known weaknesses of 2G

syllabus.title: GPRS and 3G UMTS
topics: GPRS and EDGE: packet data over GSM, SGSN and GGSN, PDP contexts, the Gn and Gi interfaces
UMTS architecture: UTRAN with NodeB and RNC, the Iub and Iu interfaces, circuit-switched and packet-switched domains
WCDMA radio: spreading, fast power control, soft handover and the near-far problem
HSPA and HSPA+: higher data rates, fast scheduling and the shift to data-dominated traffic
Mutual authentication with AKA and the improvements over GSM security

syllabus.title: 4G LTE: E-UTRAN and the Evolved Packet Core
topics: Flat all-IP architecture: eNodeB, MME, S-GW, P-GW, HSS, PCRF; the S1, X2 and S11 interfaces
LTE radio: OFDMA downlink, SC-FDMA uplink, resource blocks, frame structure, MIMO and carrier aggregation
Protocol stack: PDCP, RLC, MAC and PHY in the user plane; RRC and NAS in the control plane
Attach, default and dedicated bearers, QoS class identifiers and policy control
Voice over LTE with IMS; circuit-switched fallback as a transition
Simulating an LTE attach and measuring control-plane latency

syllabus.title: Mobility management and roaming
topics: Idle-mode mobility: location, routing and tracking areas; the trade-off between location updating and paging
Connected-mode handover: measurement reports, hard, soft and X2-based handover, inter-RAT handover
Handover failures, ping-pong and parameter tuning (hysteresis, time to trigger)
National and international roaming: home routing versus local breakout, HLR and VLR signalling, GRX and IPX
Cross-border roaming arrangements in East and West Africa and their effect on what subscribers pay

syllabus.title: 5G networks
topics: 5G use cases: enhanced mobile broadband, massive machine-type communication, ultra-reliable low-latency communication
5G NR radio: flexible numerology, bandwidth parts, massive MIMO and beamforming, millimetre wave
5G core service-based architecture: AMF, SMF, UPF, AUSF, UDM, PCF, NRF; HTTP-based service interfaces
Non-standalone and standalone deployment options; dual connectivity with LTE
Network slicing, multi-access edge computing and the virtualised, cloud-native core
Fixed wireless access and the business case for 5G in African cities versus extending 4G to rural areas

syllabus.title: Mobile data services, SMS and USSD
topics: SMS: the SMSC, store and forward, MAP signalling, delivery reports, SMS over IMS and bulk SMS gateways
USSD: session-oriented signalling, mobile-initiated and network-initiated sessions, the USSD gateway and session timeouts
Designing USSD menus for mobile money and government services: shortcodes such as *170#, menu depth and session limits
Mobile data services: APNs, DNS, carrier-grade NAT, data bundles and charging (online and offline charging, the OCS)
Security and fraud in mobile services: SIM swap, SS7 attacks, SMS one-time passwords and their weaknesses

syllabus.title: Network planning, operations and capstone
topics: Radio network planning: coverage prediction, capacity dimensioning, site selection and drive tests
Key performance indicators: call setup success, drop rate, handover success, throughput; network optimisation
Network management with OSS and BSS; powering off-grid sites with solar and generators
Capstone: plan an LTE network for a rural Ghanaian district and simulate attach, handover and a USSD transaction across it

courses.title: Phylogenetics and Molecular Evolution
topics: Evolution and homology
Distance-based tree building
Parsimony
Maximum likelihood methods
Bayesian phylogenetics
Molecular clocks
Tracking outbreaks with phylogenies
courses.description: Reconstructing evolutionary history from molecular sequences: homology and models of sequence change, distance methods, parsimony, maximum likelihood, Bayesian inference, molecular clocks and the use of time-scaled phylogenies to track pathogen outbreaks. Practised by building and testing trees in browser-based simulators and on public alignments, with outbreak cases such as Ebola in West Africa, Lassa fever and cholera.
modelledOn: Felsenstein, Inferring Phylogenies
Yang, Molecular Evolution: A Statistical Approach
Lemey, Salemi and Vandamme, The Phylogenetic Handbook
Graur, Molecular and Genome Evolution
outcomes: Explain mutation, selection, drift and homology and read rooted and unrooted trees, clades and branch lengths correctly.
Fit nucleotide and amino acid substitution models, compute corrected distances and build trees with UPGMA, neighbour joining and minimum evolution.
Score trees by parsimony and likelihood, implement Fitch and Felsenstein pruning algorithms and search tree space with heuristic rearrangements.
Run and diagnose Bayesian phylogenetic analyses, assess convergence and summarise posterior distributions of trees and parameters.
Estimate divergence times with strict and relaxed molecular clocks and test for temporal signal and selection with dN/dS.
Infer the origin, spread and growth of an outbreak from pathogen genomes with phylodynamic and phylogeographic methods and report the limits of the inference.

syllabus.title: Evolution and homology
topics: Mutation, natural selection, genetic drift and gene flow; the neutral theory of molecular evolution
Homology versus similarity; orthology, paralogy and xenology; horizontal gene transfer in bacteria
Trees as hypotheses: rooted and unrooted, topology, branch lengths, clades, polytomies; Newick format
Rooting with outgroups and midpoint rooting; gene trees versus species trees
Selection in human populations: the sickle cell allele and balancing selection under malaria

syllabus.title: Models of sequence evolution
topics: Substitution as a continuous-time Markov process: rate matrices and transition probabilities
Nucleotide models: Jukes-Cantor, Kimura two-parameter, HKY, GTR; base frequencies and transition bias
Rate heterogeneity among sites: gamma distribution and invariant sites
Amino acid and codon models; empirical matrices such as JTT, WAG and LG
Model selection with likelihood ratio tests, AIC and BIC

syllabus.title: Distance-based tree building
topics: From alignments to distances: p-distance, saturation and model-corrected distances
UPGMA and the ultrametric assumption; when it fails
Neighbour joining derived and implemented step by step; minimum evolution and least squares
Additive and ultrametric metrics; the four-point condition
Speed versus accuracy: distance methods for very large datasets

syllabus.title: Parsimony
topics: The principle of minimum change; informative and uninformative sites
The Fitch algorithm and weighted Sankoff parsimony; reconstructing ancestral states
Counting trees and searching tree space: exhaustive, branch and bound, heuristic searches
Long-branch attraction and statistical inconsistency of parsimony
Consensus trees: strict, majority-rule; measuring homoplasy with consistency indices

syllabus.title: Maximum likelihood methods
topics: The likelihood of a tree; Felsenstein's pruning algorithm implemented
Optimising branch lengths and model parameters; tree rearrangements with NNI, SPR and TBR
Practical maximum likelihood with RAxML and IQ-TREE; partitioned analyses
Assessing support: non-parametric bootstrap, ultrafast bootstrap, SH-aLRT
Comparing trees statistically: KH, SH and AU tests; Robinson-Foulds distances

syllabus.title: Bayesian phylogenetics
topics: Bayes' theorem for trees: priors on topology, branch lengths and parameters; posterior probabilities
Markov chain Monte Carlo: Metropolis-Hastings proposals, burn-in, mixing; coupled chains
Diagnosing runs: trace plots, effective sample size, convergence between independent runs
Summarising posteriors: maximum clade credibility trees, credible sets, posterior support compared with the bootstrap
Running MrBayes and BEAST; prior sensitivity and model averaging

syllabus.title: Molecular clocks and selection
topics: The molecular clock hypothesis; testing it with likelihood ratio tests
Strict and relaxed clocks; calibration with fossils or sampling dates; tip-dating of rapidly evolving pathogens
Root-to-tip regression and temporal signal; estimating substitution rates and time to the most recent common ancestor
Detecting selection: synonymous and non-synonymous rates, dN/dS, site and branch models
Drug resistance and immune escape in Plasmodium falciparum as examples of positive selection

syllabus.title: Tracking outbreaks with phylogenies
topics: Phylodynamics: coalescent and birth-death models; inferring effective population size and the reproduction number
Phylogeography: discrete trait and continuous diffusion models; reconstructing spread between districts and countries
Transmission trees versus phylogenies; within-host diversity and sampling bias
Real-time tools: Nextstrain, Nextclade and TreeTime; lineage nomenclature
Case studies: the 2014-2016 Ebola epidemic in West Africa, Lassa fever reservoirs and spillover, seventh-pandemic cholera lineages in Africa
Reporting phylogenetic evidence responsibly to outbreak response teams

syllabus.title: Phylogenomics and project
topics: Phylogenomics: concatenation versus coalescent species-tree methods; incomplete lineage sorting
Recombination and reticulate evolution; networks and recombination detection
Reproducible phylogenetic workflows and archiving trees and alignments
Project: a dated phylogeny of a public pathogen dataset with an interpretation for public health

courses.title: Real-Time Systems
topics: Real-time requirements and deadlines
Real-time operating systems
Scheduling: rate monotonic and EDF
Synchronisation and priority inversion
Timing analysis
Real-time communication
Safety-critical design
courses.description: Designing systems where correctness depends on timing as well as results: hard and soft deadlines, real-time operating systems, fixed- and dynamic-priority scheduling, synchronisation and priority inversion, worst-case timing analysis, real-time communication, and the design of safety-critical software. Taught with browser-based simulations of a real-time scheduler and task sets, so students run schedules, inject timing faults and measure response times without physical hardware.
modelledOn: Liu, Real-Time Systems
Buttazzo, Hard Real-Time Computing Systems
Burns and Wellings, Real-Time Systems and Programming Languages
outcomes: Distinguish hard, firm and soft real-time requirements and state tasks as periodic, sporadic or aperiodic with deadlines.
Select and configure a real-time operating system and explain how it bounds latency.
Apply rate-monotonic and earliest-deadline-first scheduling and test a task set for schedulability.
Diagnose priority inversion and apply priority inheritance and ceiling protocols to shared resources.
Compute worst-case execution and response times and reason about jitter and overload.
Design communication and safety-critical architectures that meet timing and dependability requirements.

syllabus.title: Real-time requirements and deadlines
topics: What makes a system real-time: timing as a correctness condition, not just performance
Hard, firm and soft deadlines; value-versus-time functions and the cost of a miss
Task models: periodic, sporadic and aperiodic tasks; period, deadline, release and execution time
Metrics: response time, latency, jitter, throughput and utilisation
Examples across domains: engine control, a mobile-money transaction switch under load, medical monitors

syllabus.title: Real-time operating systems
topics: General-purpose versus real-time operating systems; sources of unbounded latency in a general-purpose kernel
The real-time kernel: task control blocks, states, the ready queue and the dispatcher
Preemptive priority scheduling, context-switch cost and tick-based versus tickless timing
Interrupt handling, deferred work and interrupt latency
Clocks, timers and time representation; measuring kernel overhead in the simulator

syllabus.title: Fixed-priority scheduling: rate monotonic
topics: Fixed-priority preemptive scheduling and priority assignment
Rate-monotonic priority assignment and its optimality among fixed-priority schemes
The utilisation bound test and its sufficiency but not necessity
Deadline-monotonic assignment when deadlines differ from periods
Running task sets in the simulator and observing missed deadlines at high utilisation

syllabus.title: Dynamic-priority scheduling: earliest deadline first
topics: Earliest-deadline-first scheduling and its optimality for preemptive single-processor systems
The EDF utilisation test and comparison with rate monotonic
Least-laxity-first and other dynamic schemes
Behaviour under transient overload: domino effect in EDF versus graceful degradation
Admission control and handling aperiodic work with servers

syllabus.title: Synchronisation and priority inversion
topics: Shared resources, critical sections and mutual exclusion in a real-time context
Unbounded priority inversion: how a low-priority task blocks a high-priority one
The priority-inheritance protocol and its limits
The priority-ceiling and immediate-ceiling protocols; bounding blocking time and preventing deadlock
Accounting for blocking in a schedulability test
Reproducing a priority-inversion failure in the simulator and fixing it

syllabus.title: Worst-case timing analysis
topics: Worst-case execution time: why average time is not enough for hard deadlines
Measurement-based and static analysis of execution time; the effect of caches and pipelines
Response-time analysis: the recurrence for a task's worst-case response under interference
Accounting for release jitter, blocking and context-switch overhead
Sensitivity analysis and headroom; what to do when a set is not schedulable

syllabus.title: Real-time communication
topics: Timing on a shared medium; bounding message latency and jitter
Priority-based and time-triggered buses; the controller area network arbitration scheme
Time-triggered and time-sensitive networking; clock synchronisation across nodes
End-to-end deadlines across a distributed system and holistic analysis
Degradation under a congested or lossy link, as on intermittent West Africa backhaul

syllabus.title: Safety-critical design
topics: Dependability: reliability, availability, safety and the difference between faults, errors and failures
Hazard analysis and safety integrity levels; fail-safe and fail-operational design
Redundancy, watchdogs, and detecting a missed deadline or a hung task
Handling power cuts and brown-outs with safe shutdown and an uninterruptible supply
Certification evidence and the role of standards in safety-critical software

syllabus.title: Designing and evaluating a real-time system
topics: Putting it together: task decomposition, priority assignment, resource protocols and timing budget
Validating a design by schedulability analysis and by simulation
Diagnosing overload, jitter and inversion from traces
Capstone: specify, schedule and verify a small safety-critical controller under a fixed timing budget

courses.title: Robot Programming with ROS
topics: Robot software architecture
Nodes, topics and messages
Services and actions
Transforms and coordinate frames
Simulation of robots
Perception pipelines
Launching and debugging robot systems
courses.description: Building robot software with the Robot Operating System: the node graph and architecture, publish-subscribe topics and messages, request-reply services and long-running actions, coordinate-frame transforms, simulation, perception pipelines, and the tools for launching and debugging a running robot. Practised entirely in the browser against a simulated robot and sensors, with no physical hardware required.
modelledOn: Quigley, Gerkey and Smart, Programming Robots with ROS
Siciliano and Khatib, Springer Handbook of Robotics
Corke, Robotics, Vision and Control
outcomes: Design a robot application as a graph of cooperating nodes with clear responsibilities and interfaces.
Implement publishers, subscribers, services and action servers and choose the right communication pattern for a task.
Model a robot's links and sensors with coordinate frames and transform data correctly between them.
Run and inspect a robot in simulation, driving it and reading its sensors without physical hardware.
Assemble a perception pipeline that turns sensor streams into usable world information.
Launch, parameterise, record and debug a multi-node robot system and diagnose failures from its logs.

syllabus.title: Robots and robot software architecture
topics: What a robot is: sensing, computation and actuation; the sense-plan-act loop and reactive versus deliberative control
Why robot software is a distributed system: many processes, asynchronous messages, partial failure
ROS as a framework: the computation graph, the master or discovery layer, and the reasons for a message-passing design
The robotics software ecosystem and where ROS fits; versions and long-term support
Setting up a browser-based ROS workspace, building packages and running a first node

syllabus.title: Nodes, topics and messages
topics: Nodes as units of computation; naming, namespaces and the parameter server
Publish-subscribe over topics: decoupling producers and consumers, many-to-many communication
Message types and interface definition; standard messages for sensors, geometry and diagnostics
Defining custom messages; serialisation and message versioning pitfalls
Queue size, latching, publish rate and the cost of dropped or stale messages
Inspecting the graph with command-line tools: listing topics, echoing messages, measuring rates

syllabus.title: Services and actions
topics: Request-reply services for short synchronous queries; service definitions and blocking calls
When a service is wrong: long tasks, cancellation, progress feedback
Action servers and clients: goals, feedback and results for navigate-to-goal and grasp tasks
Pre-emption, cancelling and goal state machines
Choosing between topics, services and actions for a given interaction

syllabus.title: Transforms and coordinate frames
topics: Rigid-body pose: translation and rotation, rotation matrices, quaternions and Euler angles
The frame tree: base, odometry, map, sensor and end-effector frames; parent-child relationships
Broadcasting and buffering transforms over time; looking up a transform at a timestamp
Static versus dynamic transforms; extrinsic sensor calibration
Transforming a point, a laser scan or a detected object between frames
Diagnosing a broken or disconnected frame tree

syllabus.title: Simulation of robots
topics: Why simulate: safety, cost, repeatability, and the reality gap for teams without hardware
Robot description: links, joints, inertia, collision and visual geometry in a URDF model
Spawning a robot in a simulated world with gravity, contact and sensor plugins
Simulated sensors: cameras, depth, lidar and IMU, and the noise models that make them realistic
Driving the simulated robot by publishing velocity commands and reading joint states

syllabus.title: Perception pipelines
topics: From raw sensor stream to decision: the stages of a perception pipeline and their data types
Images: encoding, rectification, and converting between image messages and processing buffers
Point clouds and laser scans: filtering, downsampling and segmentation
Detecting and localising objects and publishing them as poses in the correct frame
Time synchronisation of multiple sensor streams and approximate-time matching
Visualising sensor data and pipeline output to confirm correctness

syllabus.title: Launching, configuring and recording systems
topics: Launch files: starting many nodes, setting parameters, remapping names and composing subsystems
Parameters and configuration files for reusable, deployable robot stacks
Recording and replaying message logs to debug offline and build repeatable tests
Namespacing and multi-robot launches on one graph
Lifecycle and managed nodes; bringing a system up in a known order

syllabus.title: Debugging and introspecting robot systems

Common failures: no messages, wrong frame, clock and timestamp mismatch, queue overflow
Measuring latency and throughput and finding the bottleneck node
Diagnosing simulation artefacts under power-cut-interrupted sessions common on shared campus machines

syllabus.title: Integrating a complete robot behaviour

A state machine or behaviour tree coordinating drive, sense and act
Parameterising the stack for a different simulated robot or world

courses.title: Software Testing and Quality Assurance
topics: Testing fundamentals and the test pyramid
Black-box test design
White-box testing and coverage
Unit, integration and end-to-end tests
Test-driven development
Performance and security testing
Quality metrics and process improvement
courses.description: Systematic software testing and quality assurance: testing fundamentals and the test pyramid, black-box and white-box test design, coverage criteria, unit, integration and end-to-end testing, test-driven development, performance and security testing, and quality metrics and process improvement. Students write and run real test suites against seeded-fault programs in the browser, measuring coverage and mutation scores to see which of their tests actually find bugs.
modelledOn: Ammann and Offutt, Introduction to Software Testing
Myers, Badgett and Sandler, The Art of Software Testing
ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level syllabus
ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 Software Testing
outcomes: Explain the vocabulary and principles of testing and plan a test strategy using the test pyramid and risk.
Design black-box tests with equivalence partitioning, boundary values, decision tables, state transitions and combinatorial methods.
Measure and improve white-box coverage, including branch, MC/DC and data-flow coverage, and assess test quality by mutation analysis.
Write maintainable unit, integration and end-to-end tests with test doubles, and develop code test-first.
Plan and run performance and security tests and interpret their results.
Use quality metrics, reviews and process models to assess and improve software quality.

syllabus.title: Testing fundamentals and the test pyramid
topics: Errors, faults and failures; testing versus debugging; verification and validation
The test oracle problem; the principles of testing; why exhaustive testing is impossible
Test levels and test types; static and dynamic testing
The test pyramid and its alternatives; the cost of finding defects late
Famous failures and what testing would have caught

syllabus.title: Black-box test design
topics: Equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis
Decision tables and cause-effect graphing
State transition testing
Combinatorial and pairwise testing; covering arrays
Use-case-based, error-guessing and exploratory testing
Worked example: testing mobile money transfer limits, fee bands and reversals

syllabus.title: White-box testing and coverage
topics: Control-flow graphs; statement, branch and condition coverage
Modified condition/decision coverage and where it is required
Basis-path testing and cyclomatic complexity
Data-flow testing: definitions, uses and def-use paths
Mutation testing: mutation operators, mutation score and equivalent mutants
Coverage tools and the limits of coverage as a goal

syllabus.title: Unit, integration and end-to-end tests
topics: Unit testing frameworks; arrange-act-assert, fixtures and parameterised tests
Test doubles: dummies, stubs, fakes, spies and mocks; when mocking hurts
Integration strategies: big bang, top-down, bottom-up and sandwich; testing against real databases in containers
Contract testing between services
End-to-end browser testing; flaky tests and how to fix them
Testing under simulated slow and unreliable 2G and 3G networks

syllabus.title: Test-driven development
topics: The red-green-refactor cycle; katas and worked examples
Behaviour-driven development with Gherkin scenarios
Property-based testing and generators
Characterisation tests for legacy code without tests
Evidence on the costs and benefits of TDD

syllabus.title: Performance and security testing
topics: Load, stress, soak and spike testing; workload models
Performance metrics: latency percentiles, throughput, error rates and resource utilisation
Capacity testing for month-end salary peaks on a payment service
Security testing: static and dynamic analysis, fuzzing and penetration testing basics
The OWASP Web Security Testing Guide
Reporting performance and security findings

syllabus.title: Test management and automation
topics: Test plans and strategies; risk-based testing and entry and exit criteria
The defect life cycle and writing good bug reports
Continuous integration pipelines and automated regression suites; regression test selection
Test environments, test data management and data privacy

syllabus.title: Quality metrics and process improvement
topics: Software quality models: ISO/IEC 25010 characteristics
Product metrics: defect density, escaped defects, complexity, code churn
Reliability: failure intensity, MTTF and reliability growth models
Reviews and inspections; static analysis and linters in the pipeline
Process improvement: CMMI, ISO 9001, retrospectives and root-cause analysis
Delivery metrics: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore

syllabus.title: Testing for real users
topics: Usability and accessibility testing
Localisation testing for local languages, number and currency formats
Mobile testing across low-end devices and Android versions
Capstone: a complete test suite and quality report for a seeded-fault application

courses.title: Time Series Analysis and Forecasting
topics: Time series components
Smoothing and decomposition
Stationarity and autocorrelation
ARIMA models
Seasonal models
Forecast evaluation
Forecasting rainfall, prices and demand
courses.description: Modelling data ordered in time and forecasting it with honest uncertainty: trend, seasonality and cycles, smoothing and decomposition, exponential smoothing, stationarity and autocorrelation, ARIMA and seasonal ARIMA models, regression with time series, and rigorous forecast evaluation. Every model is fitted and diagnosed in browser notebooks on real series such as rainfall in northern Ghana, food prices in Kumasi and electricity demand, and judged only by out-of-sample accuracy.
modelledOn: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice
Box, Jenkins, Reinsel and Ljung, Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control
Shumway and Stoffer, Time Series Analysis and Its Applications
Brockwell and Davis, Introduction to Time Series and Forecasting
outcomes: Identify the trend, seasonal, cyclical and irregular components of a time series and decompose it with classical and STL methods.
Produce forecasts with benchmark methods and exponential smoothing models, including prediction intervals.
Test for stationarity, interpret autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions and transform a series to stationarity.
Identify, estimate and diagnose ARIMA and seasonal ARIMA models and use them to forecast.
Evaluate forecasts with appropriate accuracy measures and time series cross-validation and choose between models.
Build and communicate a forecasting system for rainfall, prices or demand that decision makers can act on.

syllabus.title: Time series data and components
topics: What makes time series different: dependence, ordering and the forecasting horizon
Time plots, seasonal plots, subseries plots, lag plots and scatter-plot matrices
Components: trend, seasonality, cycles and irregular variation; additive and multiplicative structure
Calendar effects, missing observations, irregular sampling and resampling to a common frequency
Handling time series in pandas: datetime indexes, rolling windows and resampling

syllabus.title: Smoothing and decomposition
topics: Moving averages: simple, centred and weighted; moving averages of moving averages
Classical additive and multiplicative decomposition
STL decomposition with LOESS; robustness to outliers
Seasonal adjustment and its uses in official statistics (X-13ARIMA-SEATS in brief)
Box-Cox and log transformations; adjusting for inflation, population and calendar days
Decomposing monthly rainfall at Tamale into trend and seasonal patterns

syllabus.title: Benchmark forecasts and exponential smoothing
topics: Benchmark methods: mean, naive, seasonal naive and drift; residual diagnostics
Simple exponential smoothing; choosing the smoothing parameter by minimising errors
Holt's linear trend and damped trend methods
Holt-Winters additive and multiplicative seasonal methods
The ETS state space framework: error, trend and seasonal combinations, likelihood and AIC
Prediction intervals and why they widen with the horizon

syllabus.title: Stationarity and autocorrelation
topics: Strict and weak stationarity; white noise and random walks
The autocorrelation function and partial autocorrelation function; correlograms
Differencing and seasonal differencing; unit roots
Unit root and stationarity tests: augmented Dickey-Fuller and KPSS
Portmanteau tests for residual autocorrelation: Box-Pierce and Ljung-Box

syllabus.title: ARIMA models
topics: The backshift operator; autoregressive AR(p) and moving average MA(q) processes
ARMA processes: stationarity and invertibility conditions; theoretical ACF and PACF patterns
ARIMA(p,d,q): model identification by the Box-Jenkins approach
Estimation by maximum likelihood; information criteria AIC, AICc and BIC; automatic order selection
Diagnostic checking of residuals and forecasting from ARIMA models
Modelling the monthly price of a bag of maize in Kumasi

syllabus.title: Seasonal models and regression with time series
topics: Seasonal ARIMA models: (p,d,q)(P,D,Q)m notation, identification and fitting
Time series regression: trend and seasonal dummies, Fourier terms for long or multiple seasonality
Dynamic regression with ARIMA errors; lagged predictors and spurious regression
Interventions and outliers: level shifts, pulses and holiday effects such as Ramadan and Christmas trading
Multiple seasonality in hourly and daily data; an overview of TBATS and Prophet
Forecasting daily mobile money transaction volumes with weekly and monthly patterns

syllabus.title: Forecast evaluation
topics: Training and test sets for time series; why random splitting fails
Point accuracy measures: MAE, RMSE, MAPE and its problems, and the scaled MASE
Evaluating distributions: prediction interval coverage, Winkler score and CRPS
Time series cross-validation with a rolling origin
Comparing models and the Diebold-Mariano test; forecast combination

syllabus.title: Forecasting rainfall, prices and demand
topics: Rainfall forecasting for farmers in the north: onset dates, dry spells and seasonal totals
Market price forecasting for traders and food security monitoring; forecasting with sparse market data
Demand forecasting for inventory: hierarchical series, reconciliation and intermittent demand with Croston's method
Machine learning for time series in brief: lag features, gradient boosting and recurrent networks
Communicating forecasts and uncertainty to non-specialists; scenario forecasts
Capstone: a forecasting study on a Ghanaian series with model comparison and a written brief

courses.title: Advanced Software Development with Java

Generate dynamic pages with JavaServer Pages, JSTL and expression language, and deploy to a servlet container.

syllabus.title: Classes, objects and OO principles

Generics, collections and streams in application code; Optional and immutability
Unit testing with JUnit and mocking; Maven project structure and dependencies

syllabus.title: Abstract classes and interfaces

syllabus.title: JavaFX basics

Introduction to JPA/Hibernate as the next step

topics: Assembling a complete web application: authentication, CRUD, reports, MVC, database

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence

Constraint satisfaction problems
Game trees and tree-structured computation

Markov decision processes

courses.description: The classical core of artificial intelligence: search, constraint satisfaction, adversarial games, logic and inference, decision theory, Markov decision processes, and the entry points to machine learning, neural networks and bio-inspired methods, each implemented and run on real problems. Taught to the depth of the standard introductory AI course.

Poole and Mackworth, Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents
Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (introductory chapters)

Model and solve constraint satisfaction problems with backtracking, propagation and local search.
Play adversarial games with minimax, alpha-beta pruning and expectimax.
Represent knowledge in propositional and first-order logic and perform inference by resolution and chaining.
Make decisions under uncertainty with Bayesian networks, utility theory and Markov decision processes.
Train simple classifiers, perceptrons and neural networks and apply genetic algorithms and swarm methods.

syllabus.title: Introduction to AI and intelligent agents

courses.title: Cloud Security

courses.description: Securing workloads and data in public and hybrid clouds: the shared responsibility model, identity and access management, network security, encryption and key management, logging and threat detection, securing containers and serverless functions, and compliance including data residency under Ghana's Data Protection Act 843. NIST SP 800-144 Guidelines on Security and Privacy in Public Cloud Computing and NIST SP 800-53 controls
ISO/IEC 27017 and ISO/IEC 27018
(ISC)2 Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP) and AWS Certified Security - Specialty objectives

Design identity and access policies with least privilege, federation and short-lived credentials, and find privilege escalation paths.
Secure cloud networks with segmentation, private endpoints, firewalls and protection against denial of service.

syllabus.title: The shared responsibility model

syllabus.title: Network security in the cloud

Web application firewalls, DDoS protection and API rate limiting

syllabus.title: Data protection and encryption

syllabus.title: Logging, monitoring and detection

Threat detection services and SIEM integration; writing detection rules for suspicious API activity
Cloud incident response: containment by revoking credentials, snapshotting for forensics, recovery

syllabus.title: Securing containers and serverless
topics: Container supply chain: image scanning, signing, software bills of materials, trusted registries
Kubernetes security: RBAC, Pod Security Standards, network policies, admission control, runtime detection
Serverless risks: over-privileged functions, event injection, dependency vulnerabilities, denial of wallet
Securing APIs and gateways: authentication, authorisation, input validation against the OWASP API Security Top 10

syllabus.title: Compliance and data residency

topics: Image formation: light, lenses, sensors, the Bayer pattern; sampling, quantisation and aliasing
Pixels, channels and colour spaces: RGB, HSV, Lab, greyscale conversion; image file formats and compression
Point operations: brightness, contrast, gamma, histograms and histogram equalisation
Tooling: NumPy, OpenCV, PIL and PyTorch tensors; loading and inspecting a dataset of cassava and cocoa leaf images

syllabus.title: Filtering and edge detection
topics: Linear filtering: convolution and correlation, box and Gaussian filters, separability, border handling
The Fourier transform of images; frequency-domain filtering; the sampling theorem and image pyramids
Non-linear filters: median, bilateral; morphological operations: erosion, dilation, opening, closing
Image gradients, Sobel and Laplacian of Gaussian; the Canny edge detector implemented step by step
Lines and shapes: the Hough transform for lines and circles; finding road lane markings

syllabus.title: Features and matching
topics: Corner detection: Harris and Shi-Tomasi; scale space and blob detection with the difference of Gaussians
Descriptors: SIFT, ORB and BRIEF; invariance to scale, rotation and illumination
Matching: nearest neighbours, the ratio test, approximate nearest neighbour search
Geometric transformations: similarity, affine, homography; robust estimation with RANSAC
Image stitching for panoramas; optical flow with Lucas-Kanade in brief

syllabus.title: Image classification with CNNs
topics: From hand-crafted to learned features: convolution layers, pooling, receptive fields, parameter sharing
Architectures: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet and residual connections, MobileNet and EfficientNet; vision transformers in brief
Training in practice: data augmentation, batch normalisation, learning-rate schedules, overfitting on small datasets
Transfer learning and fine-tuning pretrained networks; classifying crop diseases from smartphone photos
Interpreting CNNs: filter visualisation, saliency maps, Grad-CAM; adversarial examples

syllabus.title: Object detection
topics: The detection problem: bounding boxes, intersection over union, non-maximum suppression
Two-stage detectors: R-CNN, Fast and Faster R-CNN, region proposal networks, anchors
One-stage detectors: YOLO, SSD and RetinaNet with focal loss; anchor-free detection
Evaluation with precision-recall curves and mean average precision
Building a dataset: annotation tools and labelling guidelines; detecting vehicles and motorbikes in Accra traffic footage

syllabus.title: Segmentation
topics: Classical segmentation: thresholding and Otsu's method, k-means in colour space, region growing, watershed, graph cuts
Semantic segmentation: fully convolutional networks, U-Net, encoder-decoder designs and dilated convolutions
Instance and panoptic segmentation: Mask R-CNN; promptable segmentation models
Metrics: pixel accuracy, mean IoU, Dice coefficient; segmenting malaria parasites in blood smear images and farmland in satellite imagery

syllabus.title: Geometry, cameras and 3D
topics: Homogeneous coordinates and projective geometry; the pinhole camera model, intrinsics, extrinsics and lens distortion
Camera calibration with a checkerboard; pose estimation and perspective-n-point
Two-view geometry: epipolar constraints, the essential and fundamental matrices, the eight-point algorithm
Stereo vision and depth from disparity; triangulation
Structure from motion and visual SLAM in outline; bundle adjustment; depth sensors and point clouds

syllabus.title: Video, generative models and responsible vision
topics: Video understanding: tracking by detection, Kalman filtering for tracks, action recognition in brief
Generative models for images in brief: autoencoders, GANs, diffusion; synthetic data and deepfakes
Deploying vision on phones and edge devices: quantisation, pruning, latency budgets
Fairness and privacy: skin-tone bias in face analysis, surveillance concerns, consent and the Data Protection Act
Capstone: an end-to-end vision application with a dataset card, evaluation report and deployment demonstration

courses.title: Cryptography and Network Security
topics: Classical ciphers
Symmetric encryption: AES and modes
Public-key cryptography: RSA, Diffie-Hellman, elliptic curves
Hash functions and MACs
Digital signatures and PKI
TLS and secure protocols
Key management
courses.description: The mathematics and engineering of secrecy and authenticity: classical ciphers and how they break, block and stream ciphers, public-key cryptography, hashes, MACs, signatures, certificates, key management and the protocols such as TLS that secure the Internet. Taught to the depth of a leading applied cryptography course.
modelledOn: Stallings, Cryptography and Network Security: Principles and Practice
Katz and Lindell, Introduction to Modern Cryptography
Boneh and Shoup, A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography (selected chapters)
Ferguson, Schneier and Kohno, Cryptography Engineering
outcomes: Break classical ciphers with frequency analysis and explain why modern ciphers resist such attacks.
Describe AES and modes of operation, choose a mode correctly, and implement authenticated encryption.
Explain and implement RSA, Diffie-Hellman and elliptic-curve operations and the number theory behind them.
Use hash functions, MACs and digital signatures for integrity and authentication and explain their security properties.
Describe PKI, certificates and the TLS handshake and analyse the security of a protocol.
Design key management, including generation, distribution, storage and rotation, and recognise common implementation failures.

syllabus.title: Security goals and classical ciphers
topics: Confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, non-repudiation; threat models and Kerckhoffs's principle
Caesar, substitution, Vigenere, Playfair, Hill, transposition ciphers; the Enigma
Cryptanalysis: frequency analysis, Kasiski examination, known- and chosen-plaintext attacks
The one-time pad and perfect secrecy; why keys must be random and unreused
Computational security, security parameters and negligible probabilities

syllabus.title: Number theory for cryptography
topics: Modular arithmetic, groups, Euler's totient, Fermat and Euler theorems
Extended Euclid and modular inverses; fast modular exponentiation
Primality testing (Miller-Rabin), prime generation, the Chinese remainder theorem
Discrete logarithms and the hardness assumptions (factoring, DLP, ECDLP)
Finite fields GF(2^8) as used in AES

syllabus.title: Symmetric encryption: block ciphers, AES and modes
topics: Block cipher design: confusion and diffusion, Feistel networks, DES and its weaknesses, 3DES
AES: SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey, key schedule; implementing a round
Modes of operation: ECB (and the penguin), CBC, CTR, CFB, OFB; padding and padding-oracle attacks
Authenticated encryption: GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305; nonce misuse
Stream ciphers: RC4 history, ChaCha20; pseudo-random generators and CSPRNGs
Side channels: timing, power, cache; constant-time implementation

syllabus.title: Public-key cryptography: RSA, Diffie-Hellman, elliptic curves
topics: The public-key idea; RSA key generation, encryption, decryption and correctness proof
Attacks on textbook RSA; padding (OAEP); key sizes and factoring records
Diffie-Hellman key exchange, man-in-the-middle, authenticated key exchange; ElGamal
Elliptic curves over finite fields, point addition, scalar multiplication, ECDH, Curve25519
Hybrid encryption and key encapsulation; post-quantum cryptography overview (lattices, Kyber)

syllabus.title: Hash functions and MACs
topics: Properties: preimage, second-preimage and collision resistance; the birthday bound
MD5 and SHA-1 breaks; SHA-2, SHA-3; Merkle-Damgard and sponge constructions
Message authentication codes: HMAC, CMAC; MAC-then-encrypt versus encrypt-then-MAC
Password hashing: salts, bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2; rainbow tables
Applications: integrity checking, commitments, blockchains, deduplication

syllabus.title: Digital signatures and PKI
topics: RSA signatures (PSS), DSA, ECDSA, EdDSA; hash-then-sign; nonce reuse disasters
Certificates, X.509, certificate authorities, chains, revocation (CRL, OCSP), Certificate Transparency
Web of trust versus hierarchical PKI; code signing; Ghana's national PKI and e-signature law
Certificate pinning and the risks of mis-issued certificates

syllabus.title: TLS and secure protocols
topics: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 handshakes, cipher suites, forward secrecy, session resumption, 0-RTT
Attacks on TLS history: BEAST, POODLE, Heartbleed, downgrade attacks; configuring a server correctly
SSH, IPsec and VPNs (IKE, WireGuard), Kerberos, S/MIME and PGP, Signal protocol and double ratchet
DNSSEC and DNS over HTTPS; email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)
Analysing a protocol: attacker models, replay, reflection, the Needham-Schroeder lesson

syllabus.title: Key management
topics: Key generation and randomness; entropy sources and failures (Debian OpenSSL, low-entropy devices)
Key distribution: KDCs, public-key distribution, key agreement; key hierarchies and derivation (HKDF)
Storage: hardware security modules, TPMs, secure enclaves, key management services; secrets in applications
Rotation, revocation, escrow, backup; secret sharing (Shamir)
Cryptographic policy: algorithms and key lengths, NIST and ECRYPT recommendations

syllabus.title: Applied cryptography and capstone
topics: Using cryptographic libraries correctly: libsodium, OpenSSL, Web Crypto; what not to build yourself
Cryptography in mobile money, banking (EMV, HSMs), messaging and blockchains
Common implementation mistakes and how to review code for them
Capstone: a secure messaging or file-sharing tool with authenticated key exchange and authenticated encryption

courses.title: Data Science
topics: Introduction to data science
R/Python
Data collection and blending
Business intelligence and data warehousing
Data science project life cycle
Data visualisation
Machine learning: clustering, PCA, association rules, regression, classification
Big data analytics
Ethics, privacy, storytelling with data
courses.description: The full data science workflow on real datasets: collecting and cleaning data, warehousing and business intelligence, visualisation, machine learning for clustering, dimensionality reduction, association rules, regression and classification, big data tools, and the ethics and storytelling that make results usable. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory data science course.
modelledOn: Adhikari, DeNero and Wagner, Computational and Inferential Thinking: The Foundations of Data Science
VanderPlas, Python Data Science Handbook
Wickham, Cetinkaya-Rundel and Grolemund, R for Data Science
Provost and Fawcett, Data Science for Business
outcomes: Describe the data science life cycle and plan a project from question to deployed insight.
Use Python and R to load, clean, transform, blend and summarise data from files, databases, APIs and the web.
Design a simple data warehouse and build business intelligence dashboards.
Create honest, effective visualisations and communicate findings as a data story.
Apply clustering, PCA, association rules, regression and classification with proper validation.
Process data at scale with distributed tools and handle privacy and ethics responsibly.

syllabus.title: Introduction to data science and the project life cycle
topics: What data science is: statistics, computing and domain knowledge; roles in a data team
The life cycle: question, acquire, clean, explore, model, evaluate, communicate, deploy, monitor (CRISP-DM)
Data types and sources: structured, semi-structured, unstructured; open data from the Ghana Statistical Service and the World Bank
Framing business and research questions; defining success metrics
Reproducible work: notebooks, scripts, version control, environments

syllabus.title: R and Python for data
topics: Python: NumPy arrays, pandas DataFrames, indexing, grouping, merging, reshaping
R: vectors, data frames, the tidyverse (dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2)
Reading and writing CSV, Excel, JSON, SQL; dates and times; text and regular expressions
Exploratory data analysis: summaries, distributions, outliers, missing data
Choosing between R and Python and moving between them

syllabus.title: Data collection and blending
topics: Collecting data: surveys, sensors, logs, APIs, web scraping (ethically and legally)
Data cleaning: types, duplicates, inconsistent categories, missing values and imputation, outliers
Blending sources: joins, entity resolution, fuzzy matching, unit and currency harmonisation
Data quality assessment and documentation (data dictionaries, provenance)

syllabus.title: Business intelligence and data warehousing
topics: OLTP versus OLAP; the data warehouse and data marts; ETL and ELT pipelines
Dimensional modelling: facts, dimensions, star and snowflake schemas
OLAP operations: slice, dice, roll-up, drill-down; SQL for analytics (window functions, CUBE)
Dashboards with Power BI, Tableau, Metabase or Superset; KPIs for a retail chain or a hospital

syllabus.title: Data visualisation
topics: Principles: encoding, chart choice, colour, scales, small multiples, avoiding deception
matplotlib, seaborn, plotly and ggplot2; maps and geospatial plots of Ghana's regions
Interactive dashboards and notebooks
Critiquing charts from the press and government reports

syllabus.title: Machine learning: regression and classification
topics: Supervised learning setup; train/validation/test splits; cross-validation; overfitting and regularisation
Linear and polynomial regression; logistic regression; k-nearest neighbours; decision trees and random forests; gradient boosting
Evaluation: RMSE, R-squared, accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, confusion matrices, class imbalance
Feature engineering, encoding, scaling, pipelines in scikit-learn and tidymodels
Case: predicting loan default, crop yield or student dropout

syllabus.title: Machine learning: clustering, PCA and association rules
topics: k-means, hierarchical and DBSCAN clustering; choosing k; interpreting clusters (customer segmentation)
Principal component analysis: variance, loadings, visualisation of high-dimensional data; t-SNE and UMAP in brief
Association rules: support, confidence, lift, Apriori and FP-growth; market basket analysis
Anomaly detection basics

syllabus.title: Big data analytics
topics: The Vs of big data; when a laptop is not enough
Distributed storage and compute: HDFS, MapReduce, Spark DataFrames and MLlib; cloud data warehouses
Streaming analytics and real-time dashboards
Working with big data on a small budget: sampling, columnar formats (Parquet), DuckDB

syllabus.title: Ethics, privacy and storytelling with data
topics: Privacy, consent, anonymisation and re-identification; Ghana's Data Protection Act and GDPR
Bias in data and models; fairness metrics; algorithmic accountability; responsible AI
Storytelling: narrative structure, audience, executive summaries, presenting uncertainty
Capstone: an end-to-end project on a local dataset with a dashboard, model and written story

courses.title: Deep Learning
topics: Neural network building blocks
Training deep networks
Convolutional networks
Recurrent networks and sequences
Attention and transformers
Generative models
Transfer learning with limited compute
courses.description: Modern deep learning from the building blocks up: layers, activations and automatic differentiation, training deep networks reliably, convolutional networks for vision, recurrent networks for sequences, attention and transformers, generative models from autoencoders to diffusion, and transfer learning when compute and data are scarce. Every architecture is built from tensors in PyTorch, trained in the browser lab on small budgets and then scaled up, with experiments on African data such as crop disease images and local-language text.
modelledOn: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning
Prince, Understanding Deep Learning
Zhang, Lipton, Li and Smola, Dive into Deep Learning
Bishop and Bishop, Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts
outcomes: Build neural networks from layers, activations and loss functions and implement automatic differentiation for them.
Train deep networks reliably using suitable initialisation, normalisation, optimisers and regularisation, and diagnose training failures.
Design and train convolutional networks for image classification, detection and segmentation.
Model sequences with recurrent networks and with attention-based transformers, and explain their trade-offs.
Implement and evaluate generative models including autoencoders, GANs and diffusion models.
Adapt pretrained models with transfer learning, fine-tuning and compression to work under limited compute and data.

syllabus.title: Neural network building blocks
topics: From linear models to multilayer perceptrons; depth, width and universal approximation
Activation functions: sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU and their gradients
Loss functions: mean squared error, cross-entropy and their probabilistic interpretation
Computational graphs and reverse-mode automatic differentiation implemented from scratch
Tensors, broadcasting and GPU computation in PyTorch; modules, datasets and data loaders

syllabus.title: Training deep networks
topics: Initialisation schemes: Xavier and He; vanishing and exploding gradients
Normalisation: batch, layer and group normalisation; residual connections
Optimisers: SGD with momentum, Adam and AdamW; learning-rate schedules and warm-up
Regularisation: weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, label smoothing and early stopping
Double descent and generalisation in over-parameterised networks
Debugging training: overfitting a small batch, loss curves, gradient norms and experiment tracking

syllabus.title: Convolutional networks
topics: Convolution, padding, stride, pooling and receptive fields; parameter sharing and equivariance
Architectures: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, and efficient networks such as MobileNet and EfficientNet
Object detection and semantic segmentation: anchor boxes, YOLO-style detectors and U-Net
Visualising and interpreting CNNs: saliency maps and Grad-CAM
Classifying cassava and cocoa leaf diseases from smartphone photographs

syllabus.title: Recurrent networks and sequences
topics: Sequence modelling tasks; recurrent neural networks and backpropagation through time
Long short-term memory and gated recurrent units; gradient clipping
Bidirectional and stacked RNNs; sequence-to-sequence encoder-decoder models
Word embeddings and tokenisation for low-resource languages such as Twi, Ewe and Hausa

syllabus.title: Attention and transformers
topics: Attention as soft lookup; scaled dot-product and multi-head attention
The transformer: positional encodings, encoder and decoder blocks, layer normalisation and feed-forward layers
Pretraining objectives: masked language modelling and next-token prediction; BERT and GPT-style models
Vision transformers and multimodal models in brief
Scaling laws, efficient attention and the cost of large models
Building a small transformer for machine translation between English and a Ghanaian language

syllabus.title: Generative models
topics: Autoencoders and variational autoencoders: the evidence lower bound and the reparameterisation trick
Generative adversarial networks: the minimax game, training instability and mode collapse
Normalising flows in brief
Diffusion models: forward noising, denoising score matching and sampling
Autoregressive language models and decoding strategies: greedy, beam search, top-k and nucleus sampling
Evaluating generative models and the risks of synthetic media and deepfakes

syllabus.title: Transfer learning with limited compute
topics: Feature extraction versus fine-tuning; choosing layers to freeze
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning: adapters and LoRA
Self-supervised and contrastive pretraining; few-shot learning with foundation models
Model compression: quantisation, pruning and knowledge distillation
Mixed precision, gradient accumulation and free or shared GPUs; on-device inference for low-bandwidth users

syllabus.title: Responsible deployment and capstone
topics: Dataset bias, under-representation of African data and fairness evaluation
Robustness, adversarial examples and distribution shift
Serving a model and monitoring it after deployment; energy and environmental cost
Capstone: a deep learning project on an African dataset with a model card and compute budget report

courses.title: Digital Health and Telemedicine
topics: Digital health landscape
Mobile health applications
Telemedicine models
Community health worker tools
Remote monitoring and wearables
Regulation and ethics
Scaling and sustaining digital health
courses.description: Designing and delivering health services through digital technology: the digital health landscape and its evidence, mobile health applications, telemedicine models, tools for community health workers, remote monitoring and wearables, regulation and ethics, and the economics of scaling and sustaining digital health programmes. Taught through case-based simulations and prototypes built in the browser, from USSD and SMS services and offline-first community health worker apps to a teleconsultation flow between a rural clinic and a specialist.
modelledOn: WHO, Guideline: Recommendations on Digital Interventions for Health System Strengthening
WHO, Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health
WHO, Monitoring and Evaluating Digital Health Interventions: A Practical Guide
Wootton, Craig and Patterson, Introduction to Telemedicine
outcomes: Describe the digital health landscape using WHO classifications and appraise the evidence for digital interventions.
Design mobile health applications and services for low-bandwidth and basic-phone settings using SMS, USSD, voice and offline-first apps.
Compare synchronous, store-and-forward and remote monitoring telemedicine models and design a teleconsultation service with referral pathways.
Design and evaluate digital tools for community health workers that support decision making, reporting and supervision.
Analyse the regulatory, ethical and data protection requirements for a digital health product, including software as a medical device.
Plan the scale-up and sustainability of a digital health programme with costing, interoperability, governance and monitoring and evaluation.

syllabus.title: Digital health landscape
topics: Digital health, eHealth, mHealth and telehealth defined; the WHO classification of digital health interventions
Health system challenges digital tools address: access, workforce shortages, information gaps, supply chains
The evidence base: what works, the pilot problem and the WHO digital health guideline
National digital health strategies and the WHO-ITU National eHealth Strategy Toolkit; Ghana's eHealth strategy
Stakeholders and business models: ministries, donors, start-ups, mobile network operators
The Principles for Digital Development

syllabus.title: Mobile health applications
topics: Channels for basic phones: SMS, USSD and interactive voice response; local languages and low literacy
Smartphone apps: offline-first architecture, synchronisation and low data usage
Use cases: appointment reminders, adherence support, maternal messaging, health education, drug verification by SMS
Human-centred design with patients and health workers; designing for shared and low-end devices
Mobile money and health: insurance premium payments and mobile NHIS renewal
Building a USSD or SMS reminder service prototype

syllabus.title: Telemedicine models
topics: Synchronous video and audio consultation, store-and-forward and remote monitoring compared
Specialties suited to telemedicine: teledermatology, teleradiology, telepathology, tele-ophthalmology, telepsychiatry
Hub-and-spoke teleconsultation between rural facilities and referral hospitals; national teleconsultation centres in Ghana
Technical requirements: bandwidth, latency, image quality, DICOM and secure messaging
Clinical governance: protocols, documentation, liability, licensing across borders
Simulated teleconsultation workflow from a CHPS compound to a specialist

syllabus.title: Community health worker tools
topics: Community health workers and volunteers in African health systems; the CHPS model in Ghana
Decision support for community case management of malaria, pneumonia and diarrhoea
Household registration, visit scheduling, referrals and follow-up; community-based surveillance
Platforms for CHW tools: Community Health Toolkit, CommCare, DHIS2 Android; offline data collection
Supervision, performance feedback and motivation through digital tools
Evaluating CHW tools: accuracy of classification, workload, data quality

syllabus.title: Remote monitoring and wearables
topics: Remote patient monitoring for chronic disease: hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, pregnancy
Connected devices and wearables: blood pressure monitors, glucometers, pulse oximeters, activity trackers
Device data standards and integration: IEEE 11073, Bluetooth health profiles, FHIR observations
Signal quality, validation of consumer devices and alert thresholds
Point-of-care diagnostics with smartphones; AI-assisted screening

syllabus.title: Regulation and ethics
topics: Software as a medical device: risk classification, IEC 62304, ISO 14971; the Ghana Food and Drugs Authority
Data protection: Ghana's Data Protection Act 843, the Malabo Convention, cross-border data transfer and cloud hosting
Informed consent, privacy and confidentiality in remote care; shared phones and family access
Equity and the digital divide: gender, rurality, literacy, disability, language
Ethics of AI in health: bias, accountability, explainability; WHO guidance on AI ethics
Security of mobile health systems: authentication, encryption, device loss

syllabus.title: Scaling and sustaining digital health
topics: From pilot to national scale: pilotitis, government ownership and integration into the health system
Costing and economic evaluation: total cost of ownership, cost-effectiveness, financing models
Interoperability and digital public goods; avoiding vendor lock-in
Monitoring and evaluation frameworks for digital health; maturity models such as the Global Digital Health Monitor
Case studies: drone delivery of medical supplies, mobile maternal messaging, national telemedicine programmes in Africa

syllabus.title: Project
topics: Identifying a health problem and the users affected through a needs assessment
Designing and prototyping a digital intervention with user feedback
Writing a regulatory, data protection and sustainability plan
Project: a working prototype with an evaluation plan and a pitch to a district health directorate

courses.title: Distributed Systems
topics: Client-server and peer-to-peer models
Remote procedure calls and messaging
Time, clocks and ordering
Replication and consistency
Consensus: Paxos and Raft
Fault tolerance
Distributed storage
courses.description: Why systems built from many unreliable machines are hard and how they are made to work: communication, time and ordering, replication and consistency, consensus with Paxos and Raft, fault tolerance and distributed storage, with the key algorithms implemented and tested under injected failures. Taught to the depth of a leading distributed systems course.
modelledOn: Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications
van Steen and Tanenbaum, Distributed Systems
Ongaro and Ousterhout, In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Raft)
Lamport, Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System
outcomes: Compare client-server, peer-to-peer and other architectures and explain the fallacies of distributed computing.
Build services with RPC and message queues and handle partial failure, retries and idempotency.
Reason about time with logical and vector clocks and order events across machines.
Explain replication strategies and consistency models and choose one for a given application.
Implement a Raft-based replicated log and explain Paxos and the FLP and CAP results.
Design fault-tolerant, scalable storage with partitioning, replication and transactions.

syllabus.title: Introduction and architectures
