topics: What a distributed system is; goals: scalability, availability, fault tolerance, transparency
The fallacies of distributed computing; partial failure; latency numbers every programmer should know
Client-server, multi-tier, peer-to-peer (structured and unstructured), microservices, serverless
Case studies: a mobile-money platform, a content delivery network, a university portal under load
Lab environment: running a cluster of processes or containers locally and injecting failures

syllabus.title: Communication: RPC and messaging
topics: Sockets review; request-reply protocols; marshalling and interface definition languages
Remote procedure calls: stubs, semantics (at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once myths), failures; gRPC and REST
Message-oriented middleware: queues, publish-subscribe, Kafka and RabbitMQ; delivery guarantees
Idempotency, retries, timeouts, backoff, circuit breakers
Group communication and multicast; gossip protocols

syllabus.title: Time, clocks and ordering
topics: Physical clocks, drift, NTP and PTP; why wall clocks cannot order events
Lamport logical clocks and the happens-before relation; vector clocks and causality
Global snapshots (Chandy-Lamport) and distributed debugging
Hybrid logical clocks and TrueTime in Spanner

syllabus.title: Coordination and naming
topics: Mutual exclusion: centralised, token ring, Ricart-Agrawala; leader election (bully, ring)
Distributed locks and coordination services: ZooKeeper, etcd; leases and fencing tokens
Naming and discovery: DNS, service registries, consistent hashing, distributed hash tables (Chord)
Membership and failure detection: heartbeats, phi-accrual, SWIM

syllabus.title: Replication and consistency
topics: Why replicate; primary-backup, chain replication, multi-leader, leaderless (Dynamo-style quorums)
Consistency models: linearizability, sequential consistency, causal consistency, eventual consistency; read-your-writes and monotonic reads
The CAP theorem and PACELC; what partition tolerance really means
Conflict handling: last-writer-wins, version vectors, CRDTs; collaborative editing
Caching and invalidation; CDNs

syllabus.title: Consensus: Paxos and Raft
topics: The consensus problem; the FLP impossibility result and what it means in practice
Paxos: proposers, acceptors, learners; the two phases; Multi-Paxos
Raft: leader election, log replication, safety, membership changes, snapshots
Implementing Raft and testing it with partitions, crashes and message loss
State machine replication; Byzantine fault tolerance (PBFT) and its use in blockchains

syllabus.title: Fault tolerance and transactions
topics: Failure models: crash, omission, timing, Byzantine; redundancy and recovery
Reliable group communication and virtual synchrony
Distributed transactions: two-phase commit, three-phase commit, blocking; sagas and compensation
Checkpointing, logging and recovery; designing for graceful degradation

syllabus.title: Distributed storage and file systems
topics: Distributed file systems: NFS, GFS/HDFS design and trade-offs
Key-value stores and wide-column stores: Dynamo, Cassandra, Bigtable; LSM trees
Partitioning (sharding), rebalancing, secondary indexes; replication across data centres
Spanner and globally consistent databases; NewSQL
Object storage and blob stores

syllabus.title: Building and operating distributed systems
topics: Observability: distributed tracing, metrics, logs; debugging across machines
Load balancing, autoscaling, back-pressure, rate limiting
Security in distributed systems: authentication between services, TLS everywhere, zero trust
Capstone: a fault-tolerant replicated key-value store with a client library and chaos tests

courses.title: Information Security
topics: Information security fundamentals (CIA triad)
Addressing threats
Backdoors, viruses, worms
Password cracking
Cryptography
Authentication
Intrusion detection systems
Firewalls and honeypots
Introduction to ethical hacking
Network attacks
Management of information security
Security management models, standards, audits, disaster recovery
courses.description: Defending information and systems end to end: threats and malware, password attacks, applied cryptography, authentication, intrusion detection, firewalls and honeypots, ethical hacking and network attacks, and the management side of standards, audits and disaster recovery. Taught to the depth of a leading computer security course and the professional security certifications.
modelledOn: Whitman and Mattord, Principles of Information Security
Anderson, Security Engineering
Pfleeger, Pfleeger and Margulies, Security in Computing
ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CompTIA Security+ objectives
outcomes: Explain the CIA triad and extended security properties and classify threats, vulnerabilities and controls.
Analyse how malware, backdoors and password attacks work and defend against them.
Apply cryptography and authentication mechanisms correctly in systems.
Deploy and tune intrusion detection, firewalls and honeypots and read their output.
Carry out authorised reconnaissance, scanning and exploitation in a lab and write a penetration test report.
Manage information security with policies, risk assessment, standards, audits and business continuity planning.

syllabus.title: Information security fundamentals
topics: The CIA triad; authenticity, accountability, non-repudiation; the security versus usability trade-off
Assets, threats, vulnerabilities, risks, controls; attack surfaces and threat modelling (STRIDE)
Security principles: least privilege, defence in depth, fail-safe defaults, separation of duties
The security landscape in Ghana: mobile-money fraud, sakawa, ransomware against institutions, the Cyber Security Authority

syllabus.title: Addressing threats: backdoors, viruses, worms and malware
topics: Malware taxonomy: viruses, worms, trojans, backdoors, rootkits, ransomware, spyware, botnets; famous cases (Morris worm, Stuxnet, WannaCry)
Infection vectors: phishing, drive-by downloads, removable media, supply chain; social engineering
How antivirus and endpoint detection work: signatures, heuristics, behaviour, sandboxing; evasion
Safe malware analysis in an isolated lab: static and dynamic basics
Software vulnerabilities: buffer overflows, injection, race conditions; CVE and CVSS; patch management

syllabus.title: Password cracking and authentication
topics: Password storage: hashing, salting, slow hashes; what happens in a breach
Attacks: brute force, dictionary, rainbow tables, credential stuffing, spraying; John the Ripper and hashcat in the lab
Password policies that work; password managers; passphrases
Authentication factors; OTP, TOTP, SMS and its weaknesses, hardware keys, FIDO2/WebAuthn, biometrics
Single sign-on, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, Kerberos; session management
Access control models: DAC, MAC, RBAC, ABAC

syllabus.title: Cryptography in practice
topics: Symmetric and asymmetric encryption, hashes, MACs and signatures as tools
TLS, VPNs, disk and file encryption, encrypted messaging; certificates and PKI
Common misuse: ECB, hard-coded keys, weak randomness, home-made crypto
Steganography and watermarking in brief

syllabus.title: Intrusion detection systems
topics: Host and network IDS/IPS; signature-based versus anomaly-based detection; false positives and negatives
Snort and Suricata rules; Zeek; OSSEC/Wazuh
Log management and SIEM; correlation and alerting
Deploying an IDS in the lab and detecting a scan and an exploit

syllabus.title: Firewalls and honeypots
topics: Firewall types: packet filtering, stateful, application-layer, next-generation; architectures (DMZ, screened subnet)
Writing rules: iptables/nftables, pfSense; web application firewalls
Honeypots and honeynets: low and high interaction, deception, legal issues
Network segmentation and zero-trust architecture

syllabus.title: Introduction to ethical hacking
topics: Legal and ethical framework: authorisation, scope, rules of engagement, Ghana's Cybersecurity Act
The penetration testing methodology: reconnaissance (OSINT), scanning (nmap), enumeration, vulnerability assessment (OpenVAS, Nessus), exploitation (Metasploit), post-exploitation, reporting
Web application testing with OWASP Top Ten: injection, broken authentication, XSS, IDOR; Burp Suite and OWASP ZAP
Wireless and social engineering assessments
Writing a penetration test report and remediation plan

syllabus.title: Network attacks and defences
topics: Sniffing, ARP spoofing, DNS spoofing, man-in-the-middle, session hijacking
Denial of service and DDoS: SYN floods, amplification; mitigation
Wireless attacks: WEP/WPA cracking, evil twins; securing Wi-Fi
Hardening hosts and networks; secure configuration baselines (CIS Benchmarks)

syllabus.title: Management of information security
topics: Security governance; roles (CISO), policies, standards, procedures, guidelines; security awareness training
Risk management: identification, assessment (qualitative and quantitative, ALE), treatment
Legal and regulatory: Data Protection Act 843, Cybersecurity Act 2020, PCI DSS, GDPR for international customers
Incident response planning and the incident life cycle

syllabus.title: Security management models, standards, audits and disaster recovery
topics: Models: ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and 27002 controls, NIST CSF and SP 800-53, COBIT; the Bell-LaPadula and Biba models
Security audits and compliance; vulnerability management programmes; security metrics
Business continuity and disaster recovery: BIA, RTO/RPO, backup strategies, hot/warm/cold sites, testing the plan
Capstone: a security assessment and ISMS plan for a small organisation

courses.title: Machine Learning
topics: Supervised and unsupervised learning
Linear and logistic regression
Decision trees and ensembles
Neural networks and backpropagation
Model evaluation and overfitting
Feature engineering
Ethics and bias in ML
courses.description: Learning from data with the mathematics made explicit: regression, classification, trees and ensembles, neural networks trained by backpropagation, unsupervised learning, rigorous evaluation, feature engineering and the ethics of deployed models, with every algorithm implemented from scratch before using a library. Taught to the depth of a leading machine learning course.
modelledOn: Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning
Murphy, Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning (introductory chapters)
outcomes: Formulate supervised and unsupervised learning problems and derive and implement the core algorithms with gradient descent.
Fit and regularise linear and logistic regression models and interpret their coefficients.
Train decision trees, random forests and gradient-boosted ensembles and explain why ensembles work.
Implement a neural network with backpropagation and train it with modern optimisers and regularisation.
Evaluate models with appropriate metrics, cross-validation and learning curves and diagnose bias and variance.
Engineer features for tabular, text and image data and assess fairness, bias and privacy before deployment.

syllabus.title: Supervised and unsupervised learning
topics: What learning from data means; supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised and reinforcement settings
Hypothesis spaces, loss functions, empirical risk minimisation; generalisation
Linear algebra, probability and calculus refresher as used in the course
Tooling: NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch; notebooks and experiment tracking

syllabus.title: Linear regression
topics: Least squares: closed form and gradient descent; batch, stochastic and mini-batch
Feature scaling, polynomial features, basis functions
Ridge and lasso regularisation; the bias-variance trade-off
Probabilistic view: maximum likelihood with Gaussian noise; Bayesian regression in brief
Predicting crop yield or house prices in Accra from tabular data

syllabus.title: Logistic regression and linear classifiers
topics: Logistic regression: sigmoid, cross-entropy loss, gradient, decision boundaries; multiclass with softmax
Generative versus discriminative: naive Bayes and Gaussian discriminant analysis
Support vector machines: margins, hinge loss, kernels
k-nearest neighbours and the curse of dimensionality

syllabus.title: Model evaluation, overfitting and model selection
topics: Train, validation and test splits; k-fold and stratified cross-validation; data leakage
Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC and PR curves, AUC, log loss, RMSE, MAE; imbalanced classes
Bias and variance; learning curves; underfitting and overfitting diagnosis
Hyperparameter search: grid, random, Bayesian; nested cross-validation
Statistical significance of model comparisons; reporting results honestly

syllabus.title: Decision trees and ensembles
topics: Decision trees: entropy, information gain, Gini, CART, pruning, handling continuous and missing values
Bagging and random forests; out-of-bag error; feature importance
Boosting: AdaBoost, gradient boosting, XGBoost and LightGBM; stacking
Why ensembles reduce variance; interpretability with SHAP and partial dependence

syllabus.title: Neural networks and backpropagation
topics: Perceptron to multilayer perceptron; activation functions; universal approximation
Backpropagation derived and implemented with NumPy; computational graphs and automatic differentiation
Optimisation: SGD with momentum, Adam, learning-rate schedules; initialisation; batch normalisation
Regularisation: weight decay, dropout, early stopping, data augmentation
Convolutional networks for images and recurrent networks and transformers for sequences, in brief; transfer learning
Training a classifier for cassava leaf disease images

syllabus.title: Unsupervised learning
topics: k-means, Gaussian mixture models and the EM algorithm; hierarchical and density-based clustering
Dimensionality reduction: PCA derived from variance maximisation and SVD; t-SNE and UMAP for visualisation
Anomaly detection; autoencoders in brief
Recommender systems: collaborative filtering and matrix factorisation

syllabus.title: Feature engineering and the ML pipeline
topics: Encoding categorical variables, scaling, binning, interactions, date features, handling missing data
Text features: bag of words, TF-IDF, word embeddings; image features and pretrained encoders
Feature selection: filter, wrapper, embedded methods
Pipelines, reproducibility, model versioning and deployment basics (serving a model behind an API)

syllabus.title: Learning theory and advanced topics
topics: PAC learning, VC dimension and generalisation bounds in brief
Online learning, active learning, semi-supervised learning
Reinforcement learning overview: bandits, Q-learning, policy gradients
Large language models and foundation models: what they are and how to use them responsibly

syllabus.title: Ethics and bias in machine learning
topics: Sources of bias: data, labels, proxies, feedback loops; fairness definitions and their incompatibility
Explainability and accountability; model cards and datasheets
Privacy: differential privacy and federated learning in brief; data protection law
Case studies: credit scoring, facial recognition, predictive policing; deploying ML responsibly in Ghana
Capstone: a complete project with a model card and fairness audit

courses.title: Mobile Robotics and Navigation
topics: Locomotion and motion models
Localisation
Mapping
Simultaneous localisation and mapping
Path planning
Obstacle avoidance
Multi-robot systems
courses.description: How a mobile robot moves and finds its way: locomotion and motion models, probabilistic localisation, mapping, simultaneous localisation and mapping, global and local path planning, reactive obstacle avoidance, and coordination across multiple robots. Taught through browser simulations of wheeled robots moving through mapped and unmapped environments, so every algorithm is run and measured without physical hardware.
modelledOn: Thrun, Burgard and Fox, Probabilistic Robotics
Siegwart, Nourbakhsh and Scaramuzza, Introduction to Autonomous Mobile Robots
LaValle, Planning Algorithms
outcomes: Derive and apply motion models for wheeled robots and predict pose from control inputs.
Localise a robot in a known map with Bayesian filters including the Kalman and particle filters.
Build an occupancy grid or feature map from range data and estimate its uncertainty.
Explain and run a SLAM algorithm that maps an unknown environment while tracking the robot's pose.
Plan global paths with graph and sampling-based planners and follow them with a local controller.
Coordinate obstacle avoidance and simple cooperation across several robots sharing a space.

syllabus.title: Mobile robots and the navigation problem
topics: Classes of mobile robot: differential drive, Ackermann, omnidirectional, legged; actuation and sensing
The navigation stack: where am I, where is everything else, how do I get there
Sources of uncertainty: slip, noise, drift, and why probabilistic reasoning is unavoidable
Sensors for navigation: wheel encoders, IMU, lidar, cameras, GNSS and their failure modes
Setting up the browser simulation of a wheeled robot and a mapped environment

syllabus.title: Locomotion and motion models
topics: Kinematics of differential-drive and Ackermann robots; nonholonomic constraints
Dead reckoning from wheel odometry and its accumulating error
Velocity and odometry motion models with noise; sampling predicted poses
Representing pose and uncertainty: covariance ellipses and belief distributions
Calibrating a motion model against simulated ground truth

syllabus.title: Localisation
topics: Bayesian filtering recursion: prediction and correction with a measurement model
The Kalman filter and extended Kalman filter for pose estimation
Grid and histogram localisation; the global versus local localisation problem
Monte Carlo localisation with a particle filter; resampling and particle depletion
The kidnapped-robot problem and recovery; convergence and the number of particles

syllabus.title: Mapping
topics: Map representations: occupancy grids, feature and landmark maps, topological maps
Building an occupancy grid from range scans with an inverse sensor model
Mapping with known poses; log-odds update and clearing dynamic obstacles
Representing and visualising map uncertainty and unobserved space

syllabus.title: Simultaneous localisation and mapping
topics: Why mapping and localisation are coupled; the full and online SLAM problems
Scan matching and the iterative closest point idea for registering range scans
Filter-based SLAM and the growth of the state; FastSLAM with particles
Graph-based SLAM: pose graphs, constraints and nonlinear optimisation
Loop closure and its effect on global consistency; detecting and correcting drift
Running a SLAM session over a simulated building and evaluating the resulting map

syllabus.title: Path planning
topics: Configuration space, obstacles and the free space for a mobile robot
Graph search planners: grids, Dijkstra, A* and heuristics for navigation
Sampling-based planners: probabilistic roadmaps and rapidly exploring random trees
Cost maps, inflation and planning with clearance from obstacles
Smoothing and re-planning when the map changes

syllabus.title: Obstacle avoidance and local control
topics: Reactive avoidance: potential fields, the vector field histogram and their local minima
The dynamic window approach and trajectory sampling under velocity limits
Tracking a global path with a local controller while avoiding unexpected obstacles
Handling moving obstacles such as people in a corridor
Safe behaviour under sensor dropout and intermittent power on shared campus robots

syllabus.title: Multi-robot systems
topics: Architectures for teams: centralised, decentralised and market-based coordination
Collision avoidance between robots and shared-space deconfliction
Task allocation and formation keeping
Communication limits and consistency of a shared map across robots
Simulating a small fleet delivering across a campus map

syllabus.title: Integrating an autonomous navigation system
topics: Combining localisation, mapping, planning and avoidance into one navigation stack
Tuning and evaluating navigation: success rate, path length, time, safety margin
Failure recovery behaviours when localisation is lost or the goal is unreachable
Capstone: an autonomous robot that maps an unknown simulated market, then navigates deliveries through it

courses.title: Natural Language Processing
topics: Text processing and tokenisation
Language models
Word and sentence embeddings
Text classification
Sequence labelling
Machine translation and transformers
Working with African languages
courses.description: How computers process human language: tokenisation and text normalisation, n-gram and neural language models, word and sentence embeddings, text classification, sequence labelling, transformers and machine translation, with sustained attention to low-resource African languages such as Twi, Ewe and Hausa. Every model is built and probed in browser notebooks on real corpora, taught to the depth of a strong final-year NLP course.
modelledOn: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing
Eisenstein, Introduction to Natural Language Processing
Tunstall, von Werra and Wolf, Natural Language Processing with Transformers
Goldberg, Neural Network Methods for Natural Language Processing
outcomes: Build text-processing pipelines that tokenise, normalise and segment text in English and African languages, including subword tokenisers trained from scratch.
Implement and evaluate n-gram and neural language models and explain perplexity, smoothing and decoding strategies.
Train and compare word and sentence embeddings and use them for similarity search, classification and analysis of bias.
Design, train and evaluate text classifiers and sequence labellers with appropriate metrics and error analysis.
Explain the transformer architecture and fine-tune pretrained models for classification, tagging and machine translation.
Plan an NLP project for a low-resource language, covering data collection, annotation, evaluation and the ethics of language technology.

syllabus.title: Text processing and tokenisation
topics: What makes language hard for computers: ambiguity, variation, Zipf's law, code-switching between English and Twi or Pidgin
Unicode, encodings and normalisation; diacritics and tone marks in Ewe and Yoruba; regular expressions for text cleaning
Word, sentence and morphological segmentation; stemming and lemmatisation; edit distance and spelling correction
Subword tokenisation: byte-pair encoding, WordPiece and unigram models trained and compared on an Akan corpus
Corpora and annotation: building a corpus from radio transcripts, news and social media; licensing and consent

syllabus.title: Language models
topics: n-gram language models: the chain rule, Markov assumption, maximum likelihood estimates
Smoothing and backoff: Laplace, Kneser-Ney, interpolation; handling unknown words
Evaluation: perplexity, cross-entropy and their relation; intrinsic versus extrinsic evaluation
Neural language models: feedforward and recurrent models, LSTMs and GRUs, teacher forcing
Decoding: greedy, beam search, temperature, top-k and nucleus sampling; generating text and its failure modes

syllabus.title: Word and sentence embeddings
topics: Distributional semantics: co-occurrence matrices, PMI, SVD-based word vectors
word2vec skip-gram and CBOW with negative sampling derived and implemented; GloVe and fastText subword vectors
Evaluating embeddings: similarity benchmarks, analogies, visualisation with t-SNE and UMAP
Contextual embeddings and sentence encoders: mean pooling, siamese networks, contrastive training
Semantic search and retrieval with vector indexes; bias measured in embedding spaces

syllabus.title: Text classification
topics: Bag of words and TF-IDF features; naive Bayes and logistic regression baselines
Neural classifiers over embeddings; convolutional text classifiers; class imbalance
Sentiment analysis of Ghanaian tweets and mobile money customer complaints; topic and intent classification
Evaluation: precision, recall, macro and micro F1, confusion matrices, inter-annotator agreement with Cohen's kappa
Error analysis and robustness: adversarial inputs, spurious cues, out-of-domain text

syllabus.title: Sequence labelling
topics: Part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition; BIO tagging schemes
Hidden Markov models and the Viterbi algorithm; forward-backward
Conditional random fields; BiLSTM-CRF taggers
Span-level evaluation; NER for Hausa, Yoruba and Swahili news text using community datasets
Dependency parsing in brief: transition-based parsing and Universal Dependencies treebanks

syllabus.title: Attention and transformers
topics: Encoder-decoder models and attention; the alignment problem
The transformer: scaled dot-product and multi-head attention, positional encodings, layer normalisation, residual connections
Pretraining objectives: masked language modelling, causal language modelling, span corruption
Encoder, decoder and encoder-decoder families; multilingual models and their coverage of African languages
Fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adaptation with adapters and LoRA, and prompting

syllabus.title: Machine translation
topics: From rule-based and statistical translation to neural machine translation
Training a transformer translation model; data cleaning and parallel corpus alignment
Evaluation: BLEU, chrF and COMET; human evaluation of adequacy and fluency
Low-resource translation: back-translation, transfer from related languages, multilingual models; English to Twi and Ewe experiments
Speech in brief: automatic speech recognition and text-to-speech for languages with little written text

syllabus.title: Working with African languages
topics: The landscape: over two thousand African languages; tone, noun classes, rich morphology and orthographic variation
Data scarcity: community data collection, crowdsourcing, participatory research and fair pay for annotators
Building resources: lexicons, morphological analysers, keyboards and spell checkers for Ghanaian languages
Benchmarking multilingual models on African languages and reporting results per language
Language technology for inclusion: health information, agricultural advisories and government services in local languages

syllabus.title: Large language models, evaluation and ethics
topics: Scaling, instruction tuning and alignment in brief; retrieval-augmented generation
Evaluating generated text: hallucination, factuality, toxicity and benchmark contamination
Bias, representation and harms across languages and dialects; privacy of text data under the Data Protection Act
Capstone: an NLP system for a Ghanaian language with a datasheet, evaluation report and model card

courses.title: Operating Systems
topics: Introduction to operating systems
Memory management
Process management, concurrency and synchronisation
File systems
I/O system
Virtual machines
Multiple processor systems
Mobile operating systems
courses.description: How an operating system virtualises the processor and memory, lets programs share safely, stores data persistently and talks to devices, learned by reading, modifying and measuring a real teaching kernel. Taught to the depth of a leading operating systems course.
modelledOn: Arpaci-Dusseau, Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts
Tanenbaum and Bos, Modern Operating Systems
The xv6 teaching operating system and its commentary
outcomes: Explain the structure of an operating system, system calls, kernel and user modes, and the boot process.
Describe process and thread life cycles and implement and evaluate CPU scheduling algorithms.
Write correct concurrent programs with locks, semaphores, condition variables and monitors, and detect and prevent deadlock.
Analyse memory management with paging, segmentation, virtual memory and page replacement.
Explain file system design, disk scheduling, I/O subsystems and device drivers.
Describe virtual machines, multiprocessor operating systems and the design of mobile operating systems.

syllabus.title: Introduction to operating systems
topics: What an OS does: abstraction, virtualisation, resource management, protection; history from batch to cloud and mobile
Kernel and user mode, system calls, traps and interrupts; the boot sequence
OS structures: monolithic, layered, microkernel, modules, exokernel; Linux, Windows and xv6 compared
Shell, processes and system programming in C: fork, exec, wait, pipes, signals
Building and running xv6 in an emulator; reading kernel code

syllabus.title: Process management
topics: Processes: states, PCB, context switch, creation and termination; the process tree
Threads: user and kernel threads, pthreads, thread pools; why threads
CPU scheduling: FCFS, SJF, SRTF, priority, round robin, multilevel feedback queues; metrics and Gantt charts
Real-time scheduling (RM, EDF), proportional share and the Linux CFS
Implementing a scheduler in xv6 and measuring turnaround and response time

syllabus.title: Concurrency and synchronisation
topics: Race conditions, critical sections, atomicity; Peterson's algorithm and hardware primitives (test-and-set, compare-and-swap)
Locks, spinlocks, semaphores, condition variables, monitors; producer-consumer, readers-writers, dining philosophers
Deadlock: conditions, resource allocation graphs, prevention, avoidance (banker's algorithm), detection and recovery
Concurrency bugs: atomicity and order violations; lock-free structures in brief
Inter-process communication: shared memory, message passing, pipes, sockets

syllabus.title: Memory management
topics: Address spaces, address binding, logical versus physical addresses; base and bounds
Contiguous allocation and fragmentation; segmentation; free-space management (first fit, best fit, buddy, slab)
Paging: page tables, TLBs, multi-level and inverted page tables; address translation worked examples
Virtual memory: demand paging, page faults, copy-on-write; replacement (FIFO, LRU, clock, optimal); thrashing and the working set
Memory in xv6: page tables, allocation, implementing lazy allocation

syllabus.title: File systems
topics: Files, directories, links, permissions; the file system interface and the VFS layer
Storage layout: inodes, extents, bitmaps, directories; FAT, ext4, NTFS compared
Crash consistency: fsck, journaling, copy-on-write (ZFS, Btrfs), log-structured file systems
Caching, buffering, read-ahead; disk scheduling (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN); SSDs and flash translation layers
RAID and reliability; network file systems

syllabus.title: I/O system
topics: I/O hardware: controllers, ports, buses, polling, interrupts, DMA
The I/O subsystem: device drivers, character and block devices, buffering, spooling
Writing a simple device driver; interrupt handling in the kernel
Clocks, timers and power management

syllabus.title: Protection, security and virtual machines
topics: Protection domains, access control lists, capabilities; user authentication and privilege
OS security: buffer overflows, privilege escalation, sandboxing, address-space randomisation
Virtual machines: hypervisors (type 1 and 2), trap-and-emulate, paravirtualisation, hardware support, nested page tables
Containers: namespaces, cgroups, images; VMs versus containers

syllabus.title: Multiple processor systems and mobile operating systems
topics: Multiprocessor scheduling, load balancing, processor affinity, cache coherence effects, NUMA
Distributed and cluster operating systems in brief
Mobile operating systems: Android architecture (Linux kernel, ART, Binder, app sandbox), iOS; power management, app life cycle, permissions
Case study: the Linux kernel and how to contribute; the future of operating systems

courses.title: Regulatory Technology and Compliance
topics: Financial regulation and why it exists
Know your customer and anti-money laundering
Data protection law
Reporting to regulators
Automated compliance monitoring
Regulatory sandboxes
Risk management frameworks
courses.description: How financial institutions meet their legal obligations and how technology automates the work: why financial regulation exists, know your customer and anti-money laundering, data protection law, reporting to regulators, automated compliance monitoring, regulatory sandboxes and risk management frameworks, with the Bank of Ghana and other African regulators as the running cases. Students build compliance tools in the browser, including a KYC onboarding flow, a transaction monitoring engine and a machine-readable regulatory return, and test them against simulated customers and transactions.
modelledOn: FATF Recommendations on combating money laundering and the financing of terrorism
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Basel III framework
ISO 31000 Risk Management and the COSO Enterprise Risk Management framework
Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) body of knowledge
outcomes: Explain why financial regulation exists, the roles of central banks and other regulators, and the main regulatory objectives.
Design know-your-customer and customer due diligence processes that follow a risk-based approach.
Build anti-money laundering controls, including sanctions screening and transaction monitoring, and evaluate their accuracy.
Apply data protection law to the design of financial systems and the handling of personal data.
Automate regulatory reporting and compliance monitoring and explain the use of SupTech by regulators.
Apply risk management frameworks and assess innovations through a regulatory sandbox.

syllabus.title: Financial regulation and why it exists
topics: Market failures that justify regulation: information asymmetry, systemic risk, contagion and consumer harm
Objectives of regulation: financial stability, consumer protection, market integrity and financial inclusion
Regulators and their mandates: the Bank of Ghana, the Securities and Exchange Commission, the National Insurance Commission; central banks across Africa
Prudential regulation: capital adequacy, liquidity and the Basel accords; conduct regulation
Lessons from crises: the 2008 global crisis and Ghana's 2017 to 2019 banking sector clean-up
What RegTech and SupTech are: automating compliance for firms and supervision for regulators

syllabus.title: Know your customer
topics: Customer due diligence: identification, verification, beneficial ownership and the purpose of the relationship
Risk-based approach: simplified, standard and enhanced due diligence; politically exposed persons
Digital identity and e-KYC: the Ghana Card and the national identification system, biometric and document verification, liveness checks
Tiered KYC for mobile money and financial inclusion; balancing access and risk
Building a KYC onboarding flow with identity checks and a customer risk score

syllabus.title: Anti-money laundering and countering terrorist financing
topics: Money laundering stages (placement, layering, integration) and terrorist financing; typologies in mobile money and trade
The FATF Recommendations, mutual evaluations and grey listing; Ghana's AML/CFT law and the Financial Intelligence Centre
Sanctions screening: sanctions lists, fuzzy name matching, transliteration and managing false positives
Suspicious transaction reports, cash transaction reports and record keeping
Correspondent banking, de-risking and its effect on remittances to Africa
Crypto-assets and virtual asset service providers; the travel rule

syllabus.title: Data protection law
topics: Principles of data protection: lawfulness, purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, security and accountability
Ghana's Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843) and the Data Protection Commission; registration of data controllers
Comparing the EU GDPR, Kenya's Data Protection Act, Nigeria's Data Protection Act and the African Union Malabo Convention
Data subject rights, consent, cross-border data transfers and data localisation rules
Privacy by design: data protection impact assessments, pseudonymisation, encryption and retention schedules
Breach notification and the tension between data protection and KYC record-keeping obligations

syllabus.title: Reporting to regulators
topics: Prudential returns: capital, liquidity, large exposures and asset quality; reporting calendars
Electronic reporting systems such as the Bank of Ghana's Online Regulatory and Analytical Surveillance Software
Data standards for reporting: XBRL, data dictionaries and granular data collection
Machine-readable and machine-executable regulation; regulation as code
Data quality, lineage and reconciliation between source systems and returns
Generating and validating a regulatory return from a simulated loan book

syllabus.title: Automated compliance monitoring
topics: Transaction monitoring: rule-based scenarios, thresholds, structuring and velocity rules
Machine learning for anomaly detection and alert scoring; network analysis of money flows
Measuring a monitoring system: precision, recall, false positive rates and alert backlogs
Explainability, model governance and audit trails for automated decisions
Case management workflows and evidence for investigators
Building a transaction monitoring engine and tuning it against simulated mobile money fraud and laundering

syllabus.title: Regulatory sandboxes
topics: Why sandboxes exist: testing innovation under supervision with limits on customers and exposure
Sandbox design: eligibility, testing parameters, safeguards, exit criteria and reporting
The Bank of Ghana regulatory and innovation sandbox and sandboxes in Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and Sierra Leone
Innovation hubs, test-and-learn approaches and cross-border sandbox networks
Preparing a sandbox application for a fintech product

syllabus.title: Risk management frameworks
topics: Enterprise risk management with ISO 31000 and COSO: risk identification, assessment, treatment and monitoring
Risk categories: credit, market, liquidity, operational, compliance and reputational risk
The three lines model, risk appetite statements, key risk indicators and risk registers
Operational and cyber risk: the Bank of Ghana Cyber and Information Security Directive, business continuity
Third-party and outsourcing risk, including cloud providers and agent networks

syllabus.title: Governance, ethics and capstone
topics: Compliance governance: the compliance officer, board oversight, internal audit and whistleblowing
Ethics and culture: conflicts of interest, fair treatment of customers and responsible use of data
Choosing and integrating RegTech vendors; build versus buy
Capstone: a compliance platform for a mobile money provider covering KYC, monitoring, reporting and a risk register

courses.title: Secure Software Development
topics: Secure development life cycle
Threat modelling
Common vulnerabilities: OWASP Top Ten
Input validation and output encoding
Authentication, sessions and secrets
Static and dynamic analysis
Security code review and dependency management
courses.description: Building software that resists attack across the whole life cycle: secure development processes, threat modelling, the OWASP Top Ten and memory-safety flaws, input validation and output encoding, authentication, sessions and secrets, static and dynamic analysis, and security code review and dependency management. Every vulnerability is first exploited and then fixed in deliberately vulnerable applications running in the browser lab, and every fix is verified with automated tests and scanners.
modelledOn: OWASP Top Ten and the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework
Howard and Lipner, The Security Development Lifecycle
ISC2 Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional (CSSLP)
outcomes: Integrate security activities into each phase of a software development life cycle and write security requirements.
Build threat models with data flow diagrams and STRIDE and rate and mitigate the threats found.
Exploit and remediate the OWASP Top Ten and common memory-safety vulnerabilities.
Implement input validation, output encoding, authentication, session management and secrets handling correctly.
Use static analysis, dynamic analysis and fuzzing in a CI pipeline and triage their findings.
Conduct a security code review and manage third-party dependencies and the software supply chain.

syllabus.title: The secure development life cycle
topics: Why software is insecure; vulnerabilities, exploits and the economics of security
Design principles: least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, defence in depth, economy of mechanism
Secure development processes: the SDL, the NIST SSDF and OWASP SAMM
Security requirements, abuse cases and shifting security left
Ghana's Cybersecurity Act and Data Protection Act and what they demand of developers

syllabus.title: Threat modelling
topics: Data flow diagrams, assets and trust boundaries
STRIDE per element; attack trees
Privacy threat modelling with LINDDUN
Rating risk with CVSS and likelihood-impact matrices; choosing mitigations
Threat modelling a mobile money app with USSD, agent and API channels
Keeping threat models current as the design changes

syllabus.title: Common vulnerabilities: the OWASP Top Ten
topics: Broken access control and insecure direct object references
Injection: SQL, NoSQL, OS command and template injection
Cryptographic failures, insecure design and security misconfiguration
Vulnerable components, identification failures and software and data integrity failures, including insecure deserialisation
Security logging and monitoring failures; server-side request forgery
Memory-safety flaws: buffer overflows, integer overflows, use-after-free and format strings; the CWE Top 25

syllabus.title: Input validation and output encoding
topics: Trust boundaries, allow-listing, canonicalisation and safe parsing
Parameterised queries, stored procedures and ORMs done safely
Cross-site scripting: reflected, stored and DOM-based; context-aware output encoding; Content Security Policy
Cross-site request forgery, SameSite cookies and anti-CSRF tokens
File uploads, path traversal and XML external entities
Validating phone numbers, amounts and names in multiple scripts without breaking real users

syllabus.title: Authentication, sessions and secrets
topics: Password storage with bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2; credential stuffing and rate limiting
Multi-factor authentication; the weaknesses of SMS one-time codes and SIM-swap fraud
OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and JSON Web Token pitfalls
Session management: cookie flags, fixation, expiry, revocation and logout
Secrets management: vaults, environment variables, key rotation and secrets leaked into Git history
Applied cryptography for developers: TLS, authenticated encryption, secure randomness and not inventing your own

syllabus.title: Authorisation and secure API design
topics: Access control models: RBAC and ABAC; enforcing authorisation on the server
API security: object-level and function-level authorisation, mass assignment, rate limiting
Secure defaults, safe error handling and logging without leaking personal data
The OWASP API Security Top Ten

syllabus.title: Static and dynamic analysis
topics: Static application security testing: pattern matching, data-flow and taint analysis
Writing custom static analysis rules
Dynamic application security testing with an intercepting proxy and automated scanner
Fuzzing: mutation-based and coverage-guided fuzzers, sanitisers
Triage: false positives, false negatives and prioritising findings
Integrating security tools into continuous integration with sensible gates

syllabus.title: Security code review and dependency management
topics: Manual security code review: checklists, focusing on trust boundaries and authentication flows
Software composition analysis, CVEs and the National Vulnerability Database
Software bills of materials with CycloneDX and SPDX
Supply-chain attacks: typosquatting, dependency confusion and compromised maintainers
Pinning, signing, reproducible builds and the SLSA framework; patch management

syllabus.title: Secure deployment and incident response
topics: Hardening containers and infrastructure as code; scanning images and configuration
Vulnerability disclosure policies and bug bounties
Incident response for application teams: detection, containment and post-incident review
Capstone: threat-model, attack, fix and verify a vulnerable payment application

courses.title: Security Operations and Incident Response
topics: Security operations centres
Logging and log analysis
Intrusion detection
Threat intelligence
Incident response life cycle
Containment and recovery
Lessons learned and reporting
courses.description: Running the defensive side of security: the security operations centre, logging and log analysis, intrusion detection, threat intelligence, the incident response life cycle, containment and recovery, and the lessons-learned and reporting that close an incident. Taught through browser-based simulations of a monitored network and a live incident, where students triage alerts, investigate logs and work a response on isolated virtual machines.
modelledOn: Sanders and Smith, Applied Network Security Monitoring
NIST SP 800-61 Computer Security Incident Handling Guide
MITRE ATT&CK framework
CompTIA Cybersecurity Analyst (CySA+) objectives
outcomes: Describe how a security operations centre is staffed, tiered and measured.
Collect, normalise and analyse logs to detect and investigate suspicious activity.
Deploy and tune intrusion detection and correlate alerts in a SIEM.
Use threat intelligence and the ATT&CK framework to prioritise detection and hunting.
Work an incident through the full life cycle from detection to recovery.
Conduct a post-incident review and write reports for technical and management audiences.

syllabus.title: Security operations centres
topics: The mission of a SOC: monitor, detect, triage, respond and improve
Tiered analyst roles, shift handover and escalation paths
Metrics that matter: dwell time, mean time to detect and respond, false-positive rate
People, process and technology; build-versus-outsource for a small Ghanaian bank or university
The monitored-network simulation and the analyst's console

syllabus.title: Logging and log analysis
topics: Log sources: endpoints, servers, network devices, applications, cloud and authentication systems
Collection, time synchronisation, normalisation and retention; log integrity and tamper resistance
Searching and pivoting through logs to reconstruct a sequence of events
Baselining normal behaviour to make anomalies visible, including on shared internet-cafe machines
Parsing a mobile-money fraud attempt from authentication and transaction logs

syllabus.title: Intrusion detection
topics: Host and network intrusion detection and prevention; signature versus anomaly detection
Writing and tuning rules with Snort and Suricata; reducing noise
Network security monitoring with Zeek and endpoint telemetry with an EDR agent
Detecting scans, exploitation and command-and-control traffic in the simulator
False positives, false negatives and the cost of each

syllabus.title: SIEM and correlation
topics: Aggregating sources into a SIEM; parsing, enrichment and correlation rules
Dashboards, alerting and case management
Detection engineering: turning an attack technique into a reliable detection
Mapping detections to MITRE ATT&CK for coverage
Managing alert fatigue and prioritisation

syllabus.title: Threat intelligence
topics: Strategic, operational and tactical threat intelligence and who consumes each
Indicators of compromise, the pyramid of pain and the limits of indicators
Sharing and standards: STIX, TAXII and community feeds relevant to West Africa
Threat hunting hypotheses driven by ATT&CK techniques
Attribution, bias and avoiding over-reading an indicator

syllabus.title: The incident response life cycle
topics: The phases: preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned
Preparation: the incident response plan, roles, the RACI, communications and legal contacts
Classifying and prioritising incidents by impact and urgency
Evidence handling and chain of custody for a possible prosecution under the Cybersecurity Act 2020
Declaring an incident and standing up the response team in the simulation

syllabus.title: Containment and recovery
topics: Short-term and long-term containment; isolating hosts without destroying evidence
Eradication: removing malware, closing the entry vector, resetting credentials
Digital forensics basics: disk and memory acquisition, timeline building
Recovery: restoring from clean backups, validating integrity and monitoring for recurrence
Working an incident through brown-outs and unreliable power with offline runbooks

syllabus.title: Lessons learned and reporting
topics: The post-incident review: what happened, what worked, what to change, without blame
Root-cause analysis and tracking remediation to completion
Reporting to management and to the regulator or affected customers
Feeding lessons back into detections, playbooks and training
Updating runbooks and the response plan

syllabus.title: Running a full response exercise
topics: A tabletop and a live simulated breach combining detection, triage and response
Coordinating containment, communication and recovery under time pressure
Producing the incident report and the improvement plan
Capstone: lead the response to a simulated ransomware outbreak and present the after-action review

courses.title: Serverless and Cloud-Native Applications
topics: Cloud-native principles
Functions as a service
Managed databases and storage
Event-driven design and queues
APIs and gateways
Observability
Designing for cost
courses.description: Designing and building applications that are native to the cloud: cloud-native principles, functions as a service, managed databases and object storage, event-driven design with queues and streams, APIs and gateways, observability of distributed systems, and designing for cost. Practised by building and deploying a complete event-driven application in a simulated cloud console and code editor in the browser, taught to the depth of a strong final-year cloud application development course and the cloud developer certifications.
modelledOn: CNCF Cloud Native Definition and the CloudEvents specification
Richardson, Microservices Patterns
Hohpe and Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns
AWS Certified Developer - Associate and Microsoft Azure Developer Associate objectives
outcomes: Apply cloud-native principles to design stateless, loosely coupled and resilient applications.
Build, configure and test functions as a service and explain cold starts, concurrency and execution limits.
Choose and model managed databases and storage services for given access patterns and consistency needs.
Design event-driven systems with queues, topics and streams that handle retries, ordering and idempotence correctly.
Expose and secure APIs through gateways and instrument applications with logs, metrics and distributed traces.
Estimate, compare and reduce the cost of serverless and container-based designs.

syllabus.title: Cloud-native principles
topics: What cloud-native means: containers, microservices, declarative APIs, immutable infrastructure, automation
Twelve-factor applications: configuration, backing services, disposability, logs as event streams
Monoliths, modular monoliths, microservices and serverless: when each fits
Designing for failure: timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers, bulkheads

syllabus.title: Functions as a service
topics: The FaaS execution model: triggers, handlers, statelessness, ephemeral storage, timeouts and memory settings
Cold starts, provisioned concurrency, concurrency limits and throttling
Platforms compared: AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, Google Cloud Run functions; open-source Knative and OpenFaaS
Packaging, dependencies, layers and environment configuration; local emulation and unit testing
Serverless containers and when to choose them over functions

syllabus.title: Managed databases and storage
topics: Object storage: buckets, keys, lifecycle rules, signed URLs, static website hosting
Managed relational databases and serverless SQL; connection pooling from functions
Key-value and document stores: single-table design, partition keys, access patterns, secondary indexes
Consistency, transactions and conditional writes; caching with managed Redis
Choosing a data store for a school results portal, a ride-hailing app and a mobile money ledger

syllabus.title: Event-driven design and queues
topics: Events, commands and messages; event notification, event-carried state transfer and event sourcing
Queues and topics: point-to-point and publish-subscribe; dead-letter queues and visibility timeouts
Streams: partitions, ordering, consumer groups, replay; Kafka and managed streaming services
Delivery guarantees: at-least-once delivery, idempotent consumers, deduplication, the outbox pattern
Workflows and sagas with step functions and durable orchestration; handling mobile money payment callbacks reliably

syllabus.title: APIs and gateways
topics: API styles: REST, GraphQL, gRPC and webhooks; OpenAPI contracts and versioning
API gateways: routing, request validation, throttling, quotas, caching and custom domains
Authentication and authorisation: JWTs, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, API keys, managed identity providers
Real-time APIs with WebSockets and server-sent events
Backend for frontend and API composition; designing APIs for low-bandwidth mobile clients and USSD gateways

syllabus.title: Observability
topics: The three signals: structured logs, metrics and distributed traces; correlation identifiers
OpenTelemetry instrumentation; tracing a request across functions, queues and databases
Dashboards, service level indicators and alerts for serverless applications
Debugging distributed failures: poison messages, retry storms, timeouts and partial failure
Testing cloud-native applications: contract tests, integration tests in ephemeral environments, chaos experiments

syllabus.title: Designing for cost
topics: Serverless pricing: invocations, duration, memory, requests, data transfer and storage
Comparing the monthly cost of functions, containers and virtual machines at different traffic levels
Cost-aware design: batching, caching, right-sizing memory, avoiding chatty architectures and egress
Budgets, alerts and tagging; a worked estimate in dollars and cedis for a growing start-up

syllabus.title: Deployment and capstone
topics: Infrastructure as code for serverless: SAM, Serverless Framework, Terraform; CI/CD pipelines with staged environments
Security essentials: least-privilege function roles, secrets management, dependency scanning
Data residency considerations when choosing regions for Ghanaian users
Capstone: an event-driven application with functions, a managed database, a queue, an API gateway, tracing and a cost estimate

courses.title: Software-Defined Networking
topics: Limits of traditional networks
Control and data planes
OpenFlow
SDN controllers
Network function virtualisation
Programmable data planes
SDN in data centres and operators
courses.description: Why traditional networks are hard to change and how separating the control plane from the data plane fixes that: OpenFlow, SDN controllers and network applications, network function virtualisation, programmable data planes with P4, and SDN in data centres and operator networks. Every idea is built and tested on emulated networks of virtual switches, with students writing controller applications and data-plane programs that run against live traffic.
modelledOn: Open Networking Foundation, OpenFlow Switch Specification
Goransson, Black and Culver, Software Defined Networks: A Comprehensive Approach
Nadeau and Gray, SDN: Software Defined Networks
ETSI Network Functions Virtualisation (NFV) architectural framework
outcomes: Explain the limits of distributed, vendor-closed networks and how SDN separates the control and data planes.
Program OpenFlow switches with flow tables, match fields, actions and counters to implement forwarding and filtering.
Build network applications on an SDN controller, such as a learning switch, a load balancer and a firewall.
Design virtualised network functions and service chains and explain the NFV management and orchestration stack.
Write P4 programs for a programmable data plane and reason about their parsing, match-action and pipeline behaviour.
Evaluate SDN deployments in data centres, wide-area networks and mobile operators for scalability, reliability and security.

syllabus.title: Limits of traditional networks
topics: The traditional router and switch: integrated control and data planes, vendor-specific operating systems and command-line configuration
Distributed control: routing protocols, spanning tree, convergence and the difficulty of enforcing global policy
Operational pain: manual configuration, misconfiguration outages, slow feature rollout and middlebox sprawl
Early programmability: active networks, ForCES, the 4D project and Ethane as precursors to SDN
Setting up the emulator: virtual hosts, Open vSwitch and a scripted topology

syllabus.title: Control and data planes
topics: Data plane, control plane and management plane: responsibilities and timescales
The SDN architecture: logically centralised control, southbound and northbound interfaces, the network operating system
Physical versus logical centralisation; controller placement and the consistency-availability trade-off
Abstractions for forwarding, distribution and specification; the network as a graph the controller computes on
Network virtualisation: overlays, tunnelling with VXLAN and GRE, network hypervisors and slicing

syllabus.title: OpenFlow
topics: OpenFlow switch model: flow tables, match fields, priorities, actions, instructions, counters and timeouts
Multiple tables and pipelines, group tables (all, select, fast failover) and meter tables
The OpenFlow channel: hello, features, packet-in, packet-out, flow-mod, barrier and port-status messages
Reactive versus proactive flow installation; table-miss handling and flow-table capacity limits
Capturing and decoding OpenFlow messages; installing flows by hand from the command line
Alternatives and complements: NETCONF and YANG, OVSDB, gNMI

syllabus.title: SDN controllers
topics: Controller architecture: event loop, topology discovery with LLDP, host tracking, device and flow databases
Open-source controllers compared: Ryu, ONOS, OpenDaylight; distributed controllers and clustering
Northbound interfaces: REST APIs, intent-based networking and policy languages
Controller scalability and fault tolerance: state replication, leader election, switch-to-controller failover
Consistent network updates: two-phase updates, race conditions and transient loops

syllabus.title: Network applications on the controller
topics: A learning switch and shortest-path routing written as controller applications
A stateless firewall and access control driven by a policy file
A server load balancer and traffic engineering from link utilisation statistics
Monitoring: polling flow counters, sampling with sFlow and detecting heavy hitters
Testing and verifying applications: header space analysis and checking for loops and black holes

syllabus.title: Network function virtualisation
topics: From hardware middleboxes to virtual network functions: firewalls, NAT, load balancers, deep packet inspection
The ETSI NFV framework: NFV infrastructure, virtual network functions, management and orchestration (MANO)
Service function chaining and steering traffic through chains with SDN
Performance of software packet processing: kernel bypass, DPDK, SR-IOV and smart NICs
Containers and cloud-native network functions; orchestration with OpenStack and Kubernetes
Building a chain of a virtual firewall and NAT in the emulator and measuring its throughput

syllabus.title: Programmable data planes
topics: Why fixed-function switches are limiting: the protocol-independent switch architecture
The P4 language: headers, parsers, match-action tables, actions, control blocks and deparsers
Targets: software switches, programmable switch ASICs and smart NICs; the P4Runtime control interface
In-band network telemetry and other data-plane applications (load balancing, caching, congestion signalling)
Writing and testing a P4 program for a custom header on a software switch

syllabus.title: SDN in data centres and wide-area networks
topics: Data centre fabrics: leaf-spine and Clos topologies, ECMP, overlays and multi-tenant virtual networks
SDN for cloud providers: tenant isolation, virtual routers and the host virtual switch
Software-defined WAN: centrally engineered inter-data-centre traffic and SD-WAN for enterprise branch offices
Internet exchange points and software-defined exchanges; keeping traffic local at African IXPs

syllabus.title: SDN in operators, security and capstone
topics: SDN and NFV in mobile operators: virtualised packet core, control and user plane separation in 4G and 5G, network slicing
Transport SDN and segment routing for operator backbones
Security of SDN: the controller as a single target, flow-table exhaustion, securing the control channel, SDN for DDoS mitigation
Capstone: an emulated campus or operator network with a controller application for routing, access control and monitoring, plus one P4 or NFV extension

courses.title: Structural Bioinformatics
topics: Protein structure levels
Structure databases and visualisation
Structure comparison
Secondary structure prediction
Protein structure prediction
Molecular docking
Drug discovery workflows
courses.description: Computing with the three-dimensional structures of proteins and their ligands: levels of protein structure, structure databases and visualisation, structural comparison, secondary and tertiary structure prediction including deep learning methods, molecular docking and the computational stages of drug discovery. Practised with browser-based molecular viewers and docking simulations on public structures, with targets drawn from malaria, sickle cell disease and neglected tropical diseases.
modelledOn: Branden and Tooze, Introduction to Protein Structure
Gu and Bourne, Structural Bioinformatics
Leach, Molecular Modelling: Principles and Applications
Petsko and Ringe, Protein Structure and Function
outcomes: Describe primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary protein structure and relate the physical forces that stabilise folds to structure and function.
Retrieve, validate and visualise experimental structures from the Protein Data Bank and judge their quality from resolution, R-factors and validation reports.
Superpose and compare structures with RMSD, TM-score and structural alignment algorithms and classify folds with CATH and SCOP.
Predict secondary and tertiary structure with statistical, homology-based and deep learning methods and assess the confidence of a prediction.
Prepare receptors and ligands, run molecular docking and interpret poses and scores with an understanding of their limitations.
Design a structure-based drug discovery workflow from target selection through virtual screening to ADMET filtering.

syllabus.title: Protein structure levels
topics: Amino acids and the peptide bond; backbone torsion angles phi, psi and omega; the Ramachandran plot
Secondary structure: alpha helices, beta sheets, turns and loops; hydrogen-bonding patterns
Tertiary structure: motifs, domains and folds; the hydrophobic effect, salt bridges, disulphide bonds
Quaternary structure and assemblies; haemoglobin as a model of cooperativity and allostery
Protein folding and stability: Anfinsen's experiment, energy landscapes, Levinthal's paradox
How one substitution changes structure: HbS polymerisation in sickle cell disease

syllabus.title: Experimental methods, databases and visualisation
topics: X-ray crystallography, NMR and cryo-electron microscopy: what each measures and its limits
The Protein Data Bank: PDB and mmCIF formats, chains, residues, atoms, B-factors, occupancy
Assessing structure quality: resolution, R and R-free, validation reports, Ramachandran outliers
Visualising and selecting structures in Mol* and PyMOL: cartoons, surfaces, electrostatics, binding sites
Related resources: UniProt, PDBsum, the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database

syllabus.title: Structure comparison and classification
topics: Optimal superposition: the Kabsch algorithm and root-mean-square deviation
Structural alignment when sequences differ: DALI, CE and TM-align; TM-score and GDT
Fold classification with CATH and SCOP; convergent and divergent evolution of folds
Structure conservation beyond sequence similarity; detecting remote homologues
Contact maps, distance matrices and solvent accessibility

syllabus.title: Secondary structure prediction
topics: Assigning secondary structure from coordinates with DSSP
Early statistical methods: Chou-Fasman and GOR propensities
Neural network predictors using evolutionary profiles (PSIPRED); accuracy measures Q3 and SOV
Predicting transmembrane helices, disordered regions and signal peptides

syllabus.title: Protein structure prediction
topics: Homology modelling: template search, target-template alignment, model building, loop modelling (MODELLER, SWISS-MODEL)
Threading and fold recognition; fragment assembly and ab initio methods (Rosetta)
Coevolution and contact prediction from multiple sequence alignments
Deep learning prediction with AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold: architecture in outline, pLDDT and PAE confidence measures
Assessing models: the CASP experiments, MolProbity, knowing when a prediction should not be trusted
Modelling a Plasmodium falciparum protein with no experimental structure

syllabus.title: Molecular mechanics and dynamics
topics: Force fields: bonded and non-bonded terms, partial charges, solvation models
Energy minimisation by steepest descent and conjugate gradients
Molecular dynamics: integrating Newton's equations, timesteps, thermostats, periodic boundaries
Analysing trajectories: RMSD and RMSF, flexibility and conformational change

syllabus.title: Molecular docking
topics: Protein-ligand interactions: hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, pi stacking, binding affinity
Binding site detection and receptor preparation: protonation, waters, missing atoms
Ligand preparation: SMILES, 3D conformers, tautomers, charges; chemical databases such as PubChem and ChEMBL
Search algorithms and scoring functions in AutoDock Vina; rigid and flexible docking
Validating a docking protocol by redocking a crystal ligand; false positives and the limits of scores
Docking candidate inhibitors into Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase

syllabus.title: Drug discovery workflows
topics: The drug discovery pipeline: target identification, hit finding, lead optimisation, preclinical and clinical stages
Virtual screening: structure-based and ligand-based approaches, pharmacophores, similarity search
Drug-likeness and ADMET prediction: Lipinski's rule of five, toxicity filters
QSAR modelling and machine learning for activity prediction
Case studies: antimalarials such as artemisinin derivatives, open-source drug discovery for neglected tropical diseases, natural products from African medicinal plants

syllabus.title: Project
topics: Choosing a disease target and gathering structural and chemical data
Building or retrieving a structure, preparing it and running a small virtual screen
Reporting results with figures, confidence assessment and limitations
Project: a structure-based screening report for a target relevant to health in Africa

courses.title: VLSI Design
topics: MOS transistors and CMOS logic
Fabrication and layout rules
Combinational and sequential CMOS circuits
Hardware description languages
Timing, power and delay
FPGA design flow
Testing and design for testability
courses.description: Designing digital integrated circuits from the MOS transistor up: CMOS logic, fabrication and layout rules, delay, power and timing, combinational and sequential subsystems, hardware description languages, the FPGA design flow and design for testability. Circuits are described in Verilog, simulated and synthesised in the browser, and laid out and timed until a small design passes its rule checks and tests.
modelledOn: Weste and Harris, CMOS VLSI Design: A Circuits and Systems Perspective
Rabaey, Chandrakasan and Nikolic, Digital Integrated Circuits: A Design Perspective
IEEE 1364 Verilog and IEEE 1800 SystemVerilog hardware description language standards
IEEE 1149.1 Standard Test Access Port and Boundary-Scan Architecture
outcomes: Explain MOS transistor operation and analyse the static and dynamic behaviour of the CMOS inverter.
Design static and dynamic CMOS gates and draw their stick diagrams and layouts within design rules.
Estimate delay with RC and logical-effort models, analyse power dissipation and apply low-power techniques.
Describe, simulate and synthesise combinational and sequential designs in Verilog and take them through an FPGA flow to timing closure.
Apply fault models, scan design and built-in self-test to make a design testable.

syllabus.title: MOS transistors and the CMOS inverter
topics: Integrated circuit history, scaling and Moore's law; design hierarchy and abstraction levels
MOS structure, threshold voltage and the long-channel I-V model
Non-ideal effects: velocity saturation, channel-length modulation, body effect, subthreshold and gate leakage
The CMOS inverter: voltage transfer characteristic, noise margins and beta ratio
Switching behaviour of the inverter; load capacitance

syllabus.title: CMOS logic
topics: Static CMOS: complementary pull-up and pull-down networks; NAND, NOR and compound AOI and OAI gates
Transmission gates and pass-transistor logic; multiplexers
Ratioed logic and pseudo-NMOS
Dynamic and domino logic; charge sharing and keepers
Stick diagrams and Euler paths for gate layout

syllabus.title: Fabrication and layout rules
topics: Wafer preparation, oxidation, photolithography, doping, etching and metallisation
The CMOS process flow: n-well and twin-well processes; interconnect layers and vias
Lambda-based and micron design rules; latch-up and guard rings
Layout of an inverter and a NAND gate; standard-cell layout conventions
Design rule checking, layout-versus-schematic and parasitic extraction
Process variation, corners and yield

syllabus.title: Timing and delay
topics: RC delay models and the Elmore delay
Logical effort: gate sizing and choosing the best number of stages
Interconnect: wire resistance and capacitance, crosstalk and repeater insertion
Static timing analysis: setup and hold constraints, critical paths, clock skew and jitter

syllabus.title: Power
topics: Dynamic switching power, short-circuit power and static leakage
Activity factors and power estimation
Low-power techniques: clock gating, power gating, multiple threshold voltages, dynamic voltage and frequency scaling
Energy-delay trade-offs; designing chips for battery-powered and off-grid devices

syllabus.title: Combinational and sequential subsystems
topics: Static and dynamic latches and flip-flops in CMOS; sequencing overhead
Clock generation and distribution: H-trees, clock skew management, PLLs in brief
Datapath subsystems: ripple, carry-lookahead and prefix adders; array and Booth multipliers; shifters
Memory arrays: the 6T SRAM cell, DRAM, sense amplifiers and decoders
Pipelining a datapath to meet a clock target

syllabus.title: Hardware description languages
topics: Verilog modules, ports, data types and continuous assignment
Procedural blocks: combinational and clocked always blocks; blocking versus non-blocking assignment
Finite state machines in Verilog; parameterised and hierarchical designs
Testbenches, stimulus generation, self-checking tests and waveform debugging
Writing synthesisable code: inferred latches, resets and coding pitfalls
VHDL and SystemVerilog compared in brief

syllabus.title: FPGA design flow
topics: FPGA architecture: look-up tables, configurable logic blocks, routing, block RAM and DSP slices
The flow: synthesis, technology mapping, placement, routing and bitstream generation
Timing constraints, timing reports and achieving timing closure
ASIC and FPGA flows compared: cost, volume, performance and time to market
Project: a UART and a prepaid electricity meter controller implemented on a simulated FPGA

syllabus.title: Testing and design for testability
topics: Manufacturing test versus functional verification; defects and yield
Fault models: stuck-at, transition and bridging faults; fault coverage
Automatic test pattern generation and the D-algorithm
Controllability and observability; scan chains and scan design
Built-in self-test with LFSRs and MISRs
Boundary scan and the JTAG test access port

courses.title: Wireless Communication
topics: Wireless communication systems, 1G-4G standards
Modulation schemes
Statistical channel models, narrowband and wideband fading
Cellular concepts and system design, frequency reuse, SIR, capacity
Quality of service, trunking
Digital modulation and detection in AWGN, error probabilities
Coding for wireless channels
Multiple antenna systems, diversity, MIMO, OFDM
TDMA, FDMA, CDMA
MATLAB-style simulation
courses.description: The physics and engineering of mobile radio: from the generations of cellular standards through channel models, cellular design, digital modulation and coding in fading channels, multiple antennas and OFDM, and multiple access, with every link simulated and its error rate measured. Taught to the depth of a leading wireless communications course.
modelledOn: Goldsmith, Wireless Communications
Rappaport, Wireless Communications: Principles and Practice
Tse and Viswanath, Fundamentals of Wireless Communication
Molisch, Wireless Communications
outcomes: Trace the evolution from 1G to 5G and explain the architecture and key technologies of each generation.
Model path loss, shadowing and multipath fading and classify channels as narrowband or wideband, slow or fast.
Design a cellular layout with frequency reuse and compute signal-to-interference ratio, capacity and trunking performance.
Derive error probabilities for digital modulation in AWGN and fading channels and simulate them.
Explain channel coding, diversity, MIMO and OFDM and quantify their gains.
Compare TDMA, FDMA, CDMA and OFDMA and simulate a complete wireless link in MATLAB or Python.

syllabus.title: Wireless communication systems and standards
topics: History: from Marconi to 5G; 1G AMPS, 2G GSM and IS-95, 2.5G GPRS/EDGE, 3G UMTS/CDMA2000, 4G LTE, 5G NR and what 6G research targets
Cellular network architecture: mobiles, base stations, core network, handover, roaming, SIM and authentication
Spectrum: allocation, licensing, Ghana's NCA bands, unlicensed bands (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, LoRa)
Other wireless systems: satellite, WLAN, WPAN, microwave links; coverage in rural Ghana
Simulation environment: MATLAB or Python with NumPy and SciPy

syllabus.title: Modulation schemes and the radio link
topics: Analog modulation review: AM, FM; the transmitter and receiver chain; mixers, filters, amplifiers
Digital modulation overview: ASK, FSK, PSK, QAM; bandwidth efficiency and power efficiency
Pulse shaping, intersymbol interference, raised-cosine filters, eye diagrams
Link budget: transmit power, antenna gain, path loss, noise figure, receiver sensitivity

syllabus.title: Statistical channel models: narrowband and wideband fading
topics: Large-scale propagation: free space, two-ray, log-distance path loss, empirical models (Okumura-Hata, COST 231); log-normal shadowing
Small-scale multipath: delay spread, coherence bandwidth, Doppler spread, coherence time
Narrowband fading: Rayleigh and Rician distributions; level crossing rate and fade duration
Wideband channels: tapped delay line models, power delay profile, frequency-selective fading
Classifying channels: flat versus frequency selective, slow versus fast; simulating Rayleigh fading (Jakes model)

syllabus.title: Cellular concepts and system design
topics: The cellular concept: cells, clusters, frequency reuse, reuse distance and the cluster size
Co-channel and adjacent-channel interference; signal-to-interference ratio versus cluster size
Capacity: channels per cell, spectral efficiency; improving capacity with sectoring, cell splitting, microcells
Handover strategies, power control, mobility management
Designing a cellular layout for a Ghanaian town with given traffic and coverage targets

syllabus.title: Quality of service and trunking
topics: Traffic theory: Erlangs, offered load, grade of service
Erlang B and Erlang C formulas; blocked-calls-cleared versus queued systems; trunking efficiency
QoS parameters for voice, data and video; delay, jitter, loss; scheduling in LTE
Dimensioning a cell's channels for a target blocking probability

syllabus.title: Digital modulation and detection in AWGN; error probabilities
topics: Signal space representation; matched filter and correlation receivers; maximum likelihood detection
Error probabilities in AWGN for BPSK, QPSK, M-PSK, M-QAM, FSK; the Q-function and union bound
Performance in fading: average BER in Rayleigh fading and the diversity order; outage probability
Synchronisation and channel estimation in brief
Monte Carlo BER simulation and comparison with theory

syllabus.title: Coding for wireless channels
topics: Channel capacity (Shannon) for AWGN and fading channels; coding gain
Block codes (Hamming, Reed-Solomon), convolutional codes and Viterbi decoding; interleaving against bursts
Turbo codes, LDPC and polar codes as used in 3G, 4G and 5G
Hybrid ARQ and adaptive modulation and coding

syllabus.title: Multiple antenna systems: diversity, MIMO, OFDM
topics: Diversity: time, frequency, space; selection, equal-gain and maximal-ratio combining
MIMO: spatial multiplexing, capacity scaling, space-time codes (Alamouti), beamforming, massive MIMO in 5G
OFDM: orthogonal subcarriers, IFFT/FFT implementation, cyclic prefix, PAPR; OFDM in Wi-Fi, LTE and 5G
Simulating an OFDM link over a frequency-selective channel

syllabus.title: Multiple access: TDMA, FDMA, CDMA and beyond
topics: FDMA, TDMA and their use in 1G and GSM; frame structures
CDMA: spreading codes, processing gain, near-far problem and power control, RAKE receiver; IS-95 and UMTS
OFDMA and SC-FDMA in LTE; NOMA and random access (ALOHA, CSMA) for Wi-Fi and IoT
Capacity comparison of multiple access schemes
Capstone: a MATLAB-style end-to-end simulation of a cellular link with fading, coding, modulation and multiple access

courses.title: Big Data and Parallel Computing
topics: Characteristics of big data
MapReduce and distributed file systems
Spark-style dataflow
Threads, locks and parallel speed-up
GPU and SIMD concepts
Stream processing
Scaling and cost
courses.description: Computing on data too large or too slow for one core: shared-memory parallelism with threads and locks, SIMD and GPUs, and distributed data processing with MapReduce, Spark-style dataflow and stream processing, always measuring speed-up, scaling and cost. Taught to the depth of a leading parallel and big-data systems course.
modelledOn: Leskovec, Rajaraman and Ullman, Mining of Massive Datasets
Zaharia and Chambers, Spark: The Definitive Guide
Pacheco and Malensek, An Introduction to Parallel Programming
Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications
outcomes: Characterise big data problems and choose between scaling up, scaling out and smarter algorithms.
