Write correct multithreaded programs with locks and lock-free techniques and measure speed-up against Amdahl's and Gustafson's laws.
Explain SIMD and GPU execution models and write a simple data-parallel kernel.
Design MapReduce jobs over a distributed file system and reason about shuffles, partitioning and fault tolerance.
Build Spark-style dataflow pipelines with RDDs and DataFrames and tune them.
Process unbounded streams with windows and exactly-once semantics and estimate the cost of a data platform.

syllabus.title: Characteristics of big data
topics: Volume, velocity, variety, veracity, value; where big data comes from (telecoms, mobile money, sensors, the web)
Why single machines fail: memory, disk and network limits; latency and throughput
The landscape: Hadoop ecosystem, Spark, cloud data platforms, streaming systems
Storage formats: CSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet, ORC; compression and columnar layout

syllabus.title: Parallel computing foundations
topics: Flynn's taxonomy; shared memory versus distributed memory; task and data parallelism
Speed-up, efficiency, Amdahl's law, Gustafson's law, scalability (strong and weak scaling)
Parallel algorithm design: decomposition, communication, agglomeration, mapping
Benchmarking methodology and reporting

syllabus.title: Threads, locks and parallel speed-up
topics: Threads in C/C++ (pthreads), Java and Python (and the GIL); OpenMP pragmas for loops
Data races, mutexes, condition variables, barriers, atomics; memory models and visibility
Deadlock, livelock, contention, false sharing, load imbalance
Parallel patterns: map, reduce, scan, pipeline, work stealing, fork-join; thread pools
Lock-free queues and compare-and-swap; measuring speed-up on matrix multiply and word count

syllabus.title: GPU and SIMD concepts
topics: Vector instructions (SSE, AVX, NEON) and auto-vectorisation
GPU architecture: streaming multiprocessors, warps, memory hierarchy; CUDA and OpenCL programming model
Writing a vector add and a reduction kernel; occupancy, coalescing, divergence
GPUs for machine learning and scientific computing; using GPUs through NumPy-like libraries

syllabus.title: Distributed file systems and MapReduce
topics: GFS/HDFS design: blocks, replication, name node, fault tolerance
The MapReduce model: map, shuffle, sort, reduce; combiners and partitioners; the execution framework and stragglers
Algorithms in MapReduce: word count, inverted index, joins, matrix multiplication, PageRank
Limitations of MapReduce and the move to in-memory dataflow
Running jobs on a local cluster or a free cloud tier

syllabus.title: Spark-style dataflow
topics: RDDs: transformations, actions, lineage, lazy evaluation, persistence
DataFrames and Spark SQL; the Catalyst optimiser; joins, aggregations, window functions
Partitioning, shuffles, broadcast joins, caching; reading the Spark UI; tuning memory and parallelism
Machine learning at scale with MLlib; graph processing with GraphX or Pregel-style models
Dask and other dataflow engines compared

syllabus.title: Stream processing
topics: Bounded versus unbounded data; event time versus processing time; watermarks
Messaging backbones: Kafka topics, partitions, consumer groups
Windows (tumbling, sliding, session), state, exactly-once semantics; Flink and Spark Structured Streaming
Streaming algorithms: sampling, Bloom filters, count-min sketch, HyperLogLog
Real-time fraud detection on a mobile-money transaction stream

syllabus.title: Data platforms, scaling and cost
topics: Data lakes, lakehouses and warehouses; orchestration with Airflow; schema evolution
Scaling strategies: partitioning, replication, autoscaling, spot instances
Cost models: cloud pricing, storage versus compute, egress; total cost of a pipeline in dollars and cedis
Performance versus cost trade-offs; when a single big machine with DuckDB or Polars is enough

syllabus.title: Capstone
topics: End-to-end project: ingest, process in batch and streaming, store and query a large public dataset
Measuring and reporting speed-up, scaling and cost
Reliability, monitoring and data quality in production pipelines
Presentation and code review

courses.title: Blockchain and Distributed Ledgers
topics: Hashing and Merkle trees
Blocks, chains and immutability
Proof of work and proof of stake
Wallets, keys and transactions
Smart contracts
Use cases: land registry, supply chain, payments
Limitations and regulation
courses.description: Blockchains built up from their parts: hashes and Merkle trees, blocks and chains, consensus by proof of work and proof of stake, keys, wallets and transactions, smart contracts, and a clear-eyed look at real use cases, limits and regulation, with a small blockchain implemented and a contract deployed to a test network. Taught to the depth of a leading blockchain technologies course.
modelledOn: Narayanan, Bonneau, Felten, Miller and Goldfeder, Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies
Antonopoulos, Mastering Bitcoin
Antonopoulos and Wood, Mastering Ethereum
Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
outcomes: Explain and implement the cryptographic building blocks of a blockchain: hashes, Merkle trees, digital signatures.
Describe how blocks, chains, forks and confirmations give tamper-evidence and how a longest-chain rule resolves conflicts.
Compare proof of work, proof of stake and permissioned consensus and analyse their security and energy assumptions.
Create keys and wallets, construct and verify transactions, and explain the UTXO and account models.
Write, test and deploy a smart contract and identify common vulnerabilities.
Evaluate blockchain proposals for land registry, supply chain and payments against simpler alternatives, and summarise the regulatory position.

syllabus.title: Hashing and Merkle trees
topics: Cryptographic hash properties; SHA-256 and Keccak; hash pointers and tamper-evident lists
Merkle trees: construction, proofs of inclusion, light clients
Digital signatures with ECDSA and secp256k1; public keys as identities
Commitments and puzzles; implementing hashes, Merkle proofs and signatures in code

syllabus.title: Blocks, chains and immutability
topics: Block structure: header, previous hash, Merkle root, nonce, timestamp, difficulty
Chaining, forks, orphan blocks, confirmations; why rewriting history is expensive
Peer-to-peer networking: gossip, block and transaction propagation, nodes and miners
Building a minimal blockchain in Python or JavaScript and attacking it
Distributed ledgers versus databases: what immutability does and does not give you

syllabus.title: Proof of work and proof of stake
topics: The double-spend problem and Byzantine agreement among strangers; the Nakamoto consensus
Proof of work: mining, difficulty adjustment, hash rate, pools, 51 percent attacks, selfish mining, energy consumption
Proof of stake: validators, staking, slashing, finality (Casper, Tendermint); nothing-at-stake and long-range attacks
Permissioned consensus: PBFT, Raft-based ledgers (Hyperledger Fabric)
Comparing security, decentralisation, throughput and energy; the scalability trilemma

syllabus.title: Wallets, keys and transactions
topics: Key generation, addresses, hierarchical deterministic wallets, seed phrases, custody and loss
Transactions: inputs and outputs (UTXO model), scripts, fees, mempool; the account model in Ethereum
Constructing, signing and verifying a transaction by hand; multisignature and time locks
Exchanges, stablecoins, and how cedis move into and out of crypto; the risks of custodial services

syllabus.title: Smart contracts
topics: Ethereum: the EVM, gas, accounts, state; Solidity basics: types, functions, events, modifiers
Writing, testing (Hardhat or Foundry) and deploying a contract to a test network; interacting from a web page
Token standards (ERC-20, ERC-721) and decentralised applications; oracles
Vulnerabilities: reentrancy (The DAO), integer issues, access control, front-running; auditing and formal verification in brief
Layer-2 scaling: payment channels, rollups; cross-chain bridges

syllabus.title: Use cases: land registry, supply chain, payments
topics: Land registry: Ghana's land title problems, the Bitland pilot, what a ledger can and cannot fix (garbage in, legal recognition)
Supply chain provenance: cocoa and pharmaceuticals; the oracle problem; IBM Food Trust lessons
Payments and remittances: cross-border transfers, stablecoins, central bank digital currencies (e-Cedi), mobile money comparison
Identity, voting, academic credentials and other proposals; a decision framework: do you need a blockchain?
Enterprise ledgers: Hyperledger Fabric and permissioned deployments

syllabus.title: Limitations and regulation
topics: Limits: throughput, latency, energy, privacy on public ledgers, key loss, upgradeability, governance
Scams, fraud and consumer harm; AML/KYC and the travel rule
Regulation: Bank of Ghana and SEC positions, the e-Cedi, international approaches (MiCA, FATF)
Capstone: a complete decentralised application with a report on whether a blockchain was the right choice

courses.title: Cloud Computing
topics: Roots of cloud computing
Deployment models and service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS)
Characteristics of cloud computing
Architecture layers and methodologies
Security in the cloud
Service selection and SMI attributes
Cloud economics: provisioning, cost optimisation, multitenancy, monitoring
Google, Azure and AWS platforms
Service management
courses.description: What the cloud is made of and how to use it well: its roots in virtualisation and distributed systems, the service and deployment models, architecture layers, security, service selection, economics and the major platforms, with real deployments on free tiers throughout. Taught to the depth of a leading cloud computing course and the foundational cloud certifications.
modelledOn: Buyya, Vecchiola and Selvi, Mastering Cloud Computing
NIST SP 800-145 The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing and NIST SP 500-292 Cloud Computing Reference Architecture
AWS Cloud Practitioner, Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) and Google Cloud Digital Leader objectives
Erl, Mahmood and Puttini, Cloud Computing: Concepts, Technology and Architecture
outcomes: Trace the technical roots of cloud computing and explain its essential characteristics.
Distinguish IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, FaaS and public, private, hybrid and community deployments and choose among them.
Describe cloud architecture layers and design applications for elasticity, resilience and multitenancy.
Apply the shared responsibility model and configure identity, network and data security in the cloud.
Select services using measurable attributes and compare providers on fit and cost.
Estimate and optimise cloud cost and operate services with monitoring, SLAs and service management practices.

syllabus.title: Roots of cloud computing
topics: From mainframes and time-sharing to grids, utility computing, virtualisation and web services
Enabling technologies: virtualisation (hypervisors, containers), data centres, broadband, SOA and web APIs
The economics that made it work: scale, automation, pay-as-you-go
Cloud in Africa: regions in South Africa and Nigeria, latency to Ghana, local providers and data sovereignty

syllabus.title: Characteristics, service models and deployment models
topics: Essential characteristics: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service
IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, FaaS/serverless, CaaS; the responsibility split at each level
Public, private, hybrid, community and multi-cloud deployments; edge and fog
Hands-on: launching a virtual machine, deploying an app to a PaaS, calling a serverless function

syllabus.title: Architecture layers and methodologies
topics: Reference architecture: physical, virtualisation, orchestration, platform and application layers
Compute: VMs, containers, Kubernetes, serverless; storage: object, block, file; databases: managed relational, NoSQL, caches
Networking: VPCs, subnets, load balancers, CDNs, DNS
Design methodologies: well-architected pillars, twelve-factor apps, microservices, stateless design, infrastructure as code
Building a three-tier application on a cloud platform

syllabus.title: Security in the cloud
topics: The shared responsibility model; threats specific to cloud (misconfiguration, credential leaks, insecure APIs)
Identity and access management: users, roles, policies, least privilege, MFA, federation
Network security: security groups, private subnets, bastions, WAF, DDoS protection
Data security: encryption at rest and in transit, key management, backups, data residency and the Data Protection Act
Compliance and assurance: ISO 27017/27018, SOC 2, audits; security monitoring and incident response

syllabus.title: Service selection and SMI attributes
topics: The Service Measurement Index: accountability, agility, assurance, financials, performance, security and privacy, usability
Defining requirements and weighting attributes; multi-criteria decision making
Comparing providers and services for a case: a university LMS, a fintech API, a data analytics platform
Vendor lock-in and portability; open standards and open-source alternatives

syllabus.title: Cloud economics: provisioning, cost optimisation, multitenancy, monitoring
topics: Pricing models: on-demand, reserved, spot, serverless; storage and egress costs; free tiers
Capacity planning and provisioning; autoscaling policies; right-sizing
Cost optimisation: tagging, budgets, alerts, FinOps practices; a worked estimate in dollars and cedis
Multitenancy: isolation models, noisy neighbours, SaaS tenancy design
Monitoring and observability: metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, alerting

syllabus.title: Google, Azure and AWS platforms
topics: AWS core services: EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, VPC, IAM, CloudWatch
Microsoft Azure: Virtual Machines, Blob Storage, Azure SQL, Functions, Entra ID, Monitor
Google Cloud: Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud SQL, Cloud Functions, IAM, Operations
Mapping equivalent services across providers; CLI and infrastructure as code (Terraform) for each
Deploying the same application to two providers and comparing

syllabus.title: Service management
topics: Service level agreements, availability targets and credits; reading a provider's SLA
ITIL-aligned service management in the cloud: change, incident, problem, capacity
Backup, disaster recovery and multi-region design; business continuity
Capstone: a documented, secured, cost-estimated cloud deployment with monitoring and an SLA

courses.title: Compiler Construction
topics: Lexical analysis
Parsing: top-down and bottom-up
Abstract syntax trees
Semantic analysis and symbol tables
Intermediate code
Optimisation
Code generation
courses.description: Building a working compiler for a small language, phase by phase: lexing, parsing, syntax trees, semantic analysis, intermediate code, optimisation and code generation for a real or virtual machine. Taught to the depth of a leading compilers course.
modelledOn: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
Appel, Modern Compiler Implementation in Java/C/ML
Cooper and Torczon, Engineering a Compiler
Nystrom, Crafting Interpreters
outcomes: Specify tokens with regular expressions and build a lexer by hand and with a generator.
Write grammars, eliminate ambiguity and left recursion, and build recursive-descent, LL(1) and LR parsers.
Construct abstract syntax trees and perform semantic analysis with symbol tables and type checking.
Translate to intermediate representations such as three-address code and SSA.
Apply local and global optimisations driven by dataflow analysis.
Generate code with instruction selection, register allocation and runtime support, and test the compiler end to end.

syllabus.title: Overview of compilation
topics: Compilers, interpreters, JIT compilers and transpilers; the phases and their data structures
The source language for the course (a small C-like or Pascal-like language) and the target (RISC-V, x86 or a VM)
Bootstrapping, cross-compilation, the toolchain (assembler, linker, loader)
Project setup: test suite, driver, error reporting conventions

syllabus.title: Lexical analysis
topics: Tokens, lexemes, patterns; keywords, identifiers, literals, comments, whitespace
Regular expressions to NFA (Thompson), NFA to DFA (subset construction), DFA minimisation
Hand-written scanners versus generators (lex/flex, ANTLR); longest match and lookahead
Error recovery in the lexer; Unicode and source positions for error messages

syllabus.title: Parsing: top-down
topics: Context-free grammars, derivations, parse trees, ambiguity; precedence and associativity in grammars
Eliminating left recursion and left factoring; FIRST and FOLLOW sets
Recursive-descent parsing; predictive LL(1) table-driven parsing
Error recovery: panic mode, synchronising tokens; good error messages
Pratt parsing for expressions

syllabus.title: Parsing: bottom-up
topics: Shift-reduce parsing, handles, conflicts
LR(0) items and automaton, SLR, LR(1), LALR(1) table construction
Parser generators (yacc/bison, ANTLR); resolving conflicts with precedence declarations
Comparing LL and LR; generalised and PEG parsing in brief

syllabus.title: Abstract syntax trees
topics: Concrete versus abstract syntax; designing AST node classes
Building the AST during parsing; semantic actions and syntax-directed translation
Tree traversal with the visitor pattern; pretty printing and AST dumps for debugging
Attribute grammars: synthesised and inherited attributes

syllabus.title: Semantic analysis and symbol tables
topics: Scopes, declarations, name resolution; symbol table design with nested scopes
Type systems: type expressions, equivalence, coercion, overloading; type checking expressions, statements and functions
Semantic checks: declared before use, break inside loop, return paths, constant expressions
Type inference in brief; error reporting and recovery

syllabus.title: Intermediate code and runtime environments
topics: Three-address code, quadruples, control-flow graphs; translating expressions, control flow (short-circuit booleans), arrays and records
Static single assignment form and its construction
Runtime organisation: activation records, calling conventions, stack frames, parameter passing, nested functions
Heap management and garbage collection basics; exceptions

syllabus.title: Optimisation
topics: Local optimisations: constant folding, algebraic simplification, common subexpression elimination, copy propagation, dead code
Dataflow analysis: reaching definitions, live variables, available expressions; the iterative framework
Global optimisations: global CSE, loop-invariant code motion, strength reduction, induction variables
Peephole optimisation; inlining; introduction to LLVM passes

syllabus.title: Code generation
topics: Instruction selection: tree pattern matching, simple macro expansion
Register allocation: liveness, interference graphs, graph colouring, spilling; linear scan
Instruction scheduling and target-specific details; generating assembly and linking with a runtime
End-to-end: compiling and running test programs; performance comparison against a reference compiler

courses.title: Data Mining and Warehousing
topics: Data warehousing and modelling
Schemas for multidimensional data
Warehouse implementation and data mining architecture
Data preprocessing
Association analysis
Classification and prediction, bias and variance
Clustering analysis
courses.description: Designing data warehouses that answer business questions and mining them for patterns: multidimensional modelling, warehouse implementation, data preprocessing, association analysis, classification and prediction with attention to bias and variance, and clustering, each applied to real datasets. Taught to the depth of a leading data mining course.
modelledOn: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques
Tan, Steinbach, Karpatne and Kumar, Introduction to Data Mining
Kimball and Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit
Witten, Frank, Hall and Pal, Data Mining: Practical Machine Learning Tools and Techniques
outcomes: Design a data warehouse with dimensional models and explain its architecture and ETL processes.
Choose and implement star, snowflake and fact-constellation schemas and OLAP operations.
Implement a warehouse and connect a data mining architecture to it.
Clean, integrate, reduce, transform and discretise data for mining.
Mine frequent itemsets and association rules and evaluate their interestingness.
Build, evaluate and compare classifiers, predictors and clustering methods, and explain bias and variance.

syllabus.title: Data warehousing and modelling
topics: Operational systems versus decision support; the data warehouse definition: subject-oriented, integrated, time-variant, non-volatile
Warehouse architecture: sources, staging, ETL/ELT, the warehouse, data marts, metadata, presentation tools
Dimensional modelling: facts, measures, grain, dimensions, hierarchies; slowly changing dimensions
Requirements gathering with business users: a retail chain, a telecom, a university registry

syllabus.title: Schemas for multidimensional data
topics: Data cubes, dimensions and measures; the lattice of cuboids
Star, snowflake and fact constellation schemas; conformed dimensions; surrogate keys
OLAP operations: roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot; ROLAP, MOLAP, HOLAP
SQL extensions for analytics: GROUP BY CUBE and ROLLUP, window functions, materialised views

syllabus.title: Warehouse implementation and data mining architecture
topics: Building the warehouse in PostgreSQL or a cloud warehouse; loading with ETL tools or Python; indexing (bitmap, join indexes); partitioning
Cube computation and materialisation strategies; query processing and performance
Metadata and data quality management; warehouse operations and refresh
The data mining process (KDD, CRISP-DM); architecture: data sources, warehouse server, mining engine, pattern evaluation, GUI
Tools: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, mlxtend), R, Weka, Orange

syllabus.title: Data preprocessing
topics: Data types and statistics; visualising and summarising data; measuring similarity and dissimilarity
Data cleaning: missing values, noise (binning, regression, outlier detection), inconsistencies
Data integration: entity identification, redundancy and correlation analysis, conflict resolution
Data reduction: sampling, dimensionality reduction (PCA, attribute selection), numerosity reduction, compression
Transformation: normalisation (min-max, z-score), discretisation (binning, entropy-based), concept hierarchies

syllabus.title: Association analysis
topics: Market basket analysis; itemsets, support, confidence, lift, conviction
Apriori: candidate generation, pruning, rule generation; efficiency improvements
FP-growth and the FP-tree; closed and maximal itemsets
Multilevel and multidimensional associations; sequential patterns in brief
Interestingness measures and avoiding misleading rules; mining a supermarket or mobile-money dataset

syllabus.title: Classification and prediction; bias and variance
topics: Decision tree induction (ID3, C4.5, CART), attribute selection measures, pruning; rule-based classifiers
Bayesian classification, k-nearest neighbours, support vector machines, neural networks, ensembles (bagging, boosting, random forests)
Prediction: linear and nonlinear regression
Evaluation: holdout, cross-validation, bootstrap; confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, ROC; comparing classifiers statistically
Bias and variance: decomposition, learning curves, underfitting and overfitting, model complexity, regularisation
Class imbalance and cost-sensitive learning

syllabus.title: Clustering analysis
topics: Clustering requirements and types of data; partitioning methods: k-means, k-medoids (PAM, CLARA)
Hierarchical methods: agglomerative, divisive, BIRCH; density-based: DBSCAN, OPTICS; grid-based: STING
Model-based clustering (EM); clustering high-dimensional data; constraint-based clustering
Evaluating clusters: silhouette, cohesion and separation; outlier analysis

syllabus.title: Applications, trends and capstone
topics: Mining text, web, time series and graphs in brief; recommender systems
Privacy-preserving data mining and the ethics of profiling; the Data Protection Act
Capstone: build a warehouse for a dataset, run OLAP reports and apply association, classification and clustering with a written interpretation
Presentation to a non-technical audience

courses.title: Internet of Things
topics: IoT, sensing, actuation, networking basics
Communication protocols
Sensor networks and machine-to-machine
Interoperability
Arduino programming with sensors and actuators
Python and Raspberry Pi
SDN for IoT
Data handling, analytics, cloud
Sensor-cloud and fog computing
Smart cities, homes, connected vehicles, smart grid, industrial IoT
Case studies: agriculture, healthcare, activity monitoring
courses.description: Connecting the physical world to the Internet: sensing and actuation, IoT communication protocols, sensor networks and machine-to-machine systems, interoperability, Arduino and Raspberry Pi programming, software-defined networking, data handling and cloud, fog and sensor-cloud computing, and the application domains from smart cities to agriculture and health. Taught to the depth of a leading Internet of Things course.
modelledOn: Bahga and Madisetti, Internet of Things: A Hands-On Approach
Buyya and Dastjerdi, Internet of Things: Principles and Paradigms
Hanes, Salgueiro, Grossetete, Barton and Henry, IoT Fundamentals: Networking Technologies, Protocols, and Use Cases
Raj and Raman, The Internet of Things: Enabling Technologies, Platforms, and Use Cases
outcomes: Describe the IoT architecture from sensing and actuation through networking to applications.
Select and use IoT protocols such as MQTT, CoAP, HTTP, Zigbee, BLE, LoRaWAN and cellular IoT.
Design wireless sensor networks and machine-to-machine systems and address interoperability.
Program Arduino and Raspberry Pi devices with sensors and actuators and connect them to a cloud service.
Explain software-defined networking, fog and sensor-cloud computing in IoT deployments.
Build and evaluate an end-to-end IoT application in a domain such as agriculture, health or smart cities, with attention to security and privacy.

syllabus.title: IoT, sensing, actuation and networking basics
topics: Definition and history of the IoT; things, gateways, platforms, applications; reference architectures (ITU-T, IoT-A)
Sensors (temperature, humidity, light, motion, gas, GPS) and actuators (relays, motors, valves); signal conditioning and ADC
Networking basics for IoT: IP, addressing, IPv6 and 6LoWPAN, constrained devices and networks
Characteristics: scale, heterogeneity, constrained resources, intermittent connectivity, data volume
Lab kit: Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, sensors; simulators (Wokwi, Tinkercad)

syllabus.title: Communication protocols
topics: Physical and link layers: IEEE 802.15.4, Zigbee, Thread, Bluetooth Low Energy, Wi-Fi, LoRa/LoRaWAN, Sigfox, NB-IoT and LTE-M, RFID and NFC
Network and transport: 6LoWPAN, RPL, UDP versus TCP for IoT
Application protocols: MQTT (publish-subscribe, QoS, retained messages), CoAP, HTTP/REST, AMQP, WebSockets
Choosing a protocol for range, power, data rate and cost; running an MQTT broker and clients
Security in protocols: DTLS, TLS, device authentication

syllabus.title: Sensor networks and machine-to-machine
topics: Wireless sensor networks: topologies, routing, clustering, energy-aware design, localisation and time synchronisation
Machine-to-machine communication; oneM2M and ETSI M2M architecture
Edge devices, gateways and protocol translation
Reliability and fault tolerance in sensor networks

syllabus.title: Interoperability
topics: Levels of interoperability: device, network, syntactic, semantic, platform
Standards and data models: IPSO, OMA LwM2M, W3C Web of Things, Matter
Data formats: JSON, CBOR, SenML; ontologies (SSN/SOSA)
Integrating devices from different vendors through a gateway

syllabus.title: Arduino programming with sensors and actuators
topics: Arduino and ESP32 programming model: setup and loop, digital and analog I/O, PWM, interrupts, timers
Reading sensors over analog, I2C and SPI; driving actuators and displays
Wi-Fi connectivity and sending telemetry over MQTT and HTTP; over-the-air updates
Power management and battery and solar operation
Mini-project: a soil-moisture monitor that publishes readings

syllabus.title: Python and Raspberry Pi
topics: Raspberry Pi setup, Linux basics, GPIO with Python (gpiozero, RPi.GPIO), camera and USB devices
Raspberry Pi as a gateway: MQTT broker, local database, dashboard (Node-RED, Grafana)
Edge processing: filtering, aggregation, simple machine learning on the Pi
Remote access and device management

syllabus.title: SDN for IoT
topics: Software-defined networking: control and data plane separation, OpenFlow, controllers
SDN benefits for IoT: traffic management, security policies, mobility, scalability
Network function virtualisation; SDN in wireless sensor networks and 5G
Simulating an SDN-managed IoT network with Mininet

syllabus.title: Data handling, analytics and cloud
topics: IoT data characteristics; ingestion, time-series databases, storage and retention
Cloud IoT platforms: AWS IoT Core, Azure IoT Hub, Google Cloud IoT, ThingsBoard, open-source alternatives
Device registration, provisioning, digital twins, rules engines, alerts
Analytics and visualisation: dashboards, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance; machine learning at the edge

syllabus.title: Sensor-cloud and fog computing
topics: Sensor-cloud architecture: virtual sensors, sensors as a service
Fog and edge computing: motivation (latency, bandwidth, privacy), architecture, placement of computation
Offloading and orchestration between device, fog and cloud
Designing a fog layer for a campus or farm deployment with intermittent Internet

syllabus.title: Applications and case studies
topics: Smart cities (traffic, lighting, waste), smart homes, connected vehicles, smart grid and prepaid metering, industrial IoT and Industry 4.0
Case studies: precision agriculture and irrigation in Ghana, healthcare and remote patient monitoring, activity and fall monitoring
Security, privacy and safety of IoT systems: botnets (Mirai), device hardening, data protection
Capstone: an end-to-end IoT system from sensor to cloud dashboard, with a cost and power budget

courses.title: Legal and Ethical Issues in Computing
topics: Introduction to IT law
E-commerce legal issues
ICT crime
Intellectual property
IT contracts
Information privacy and Internet governance
Data protection and freedom of information
Data Protection Act 843, GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, POPIA
Work and wealth
Professional ethics and social issues
courses.description: The law and ethics that govern computing professionals and the systems they build: IT law, e-commerce, cybercrime, intellectual property, contracts, privacy and Internet governance, data protection regimes compared across Ghana, Europe, the Americas and Southern Africa, the effects of computing on work and wealth, and professional ethics. Taught to the depth of a leading computer ethics and cyberlaw course.
modelledOn: Quinn, Ethics for the Information Age
Baase and Henry, A Gift of Fire: Social, Legal, and Ethical Issues for Computing Technology
Lloyd, Information Technology Law
ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct; IEEE Code of Ethics
outcomes: Explain the sources and structure of IT law in Ghana and how it interacts with international law.
Identify the legal requirements of e-commerce, electronic contracts, electronic signatures and consumer protection.
Classify ICT crimes and explain the relevant offences, investigation powers and penalties.
Apply intellectual property law to software, data, content and trademarks, including licensing and open source.
Compare data protection regimes (Ghana's Act 843, GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, POPIA) and design compliant data handling.
Analyse ethical dilemmas in computing with established ethical theories and professional codes.

syllabus.title: Introduction to IT law
topics: Sources of law in Ghana: the Constitution, statutes, common law, customary law; courts and jurisdiction
Why the Internet challenges law: territoriality, anonymity, speed, intermediaries
Key Ghanaian statutes: Electronic Transactions Act 2008 (Act 772), Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843), Cybersecurity Act 2020 (Act 1038), Electronic Communications Act 2008
Regulators: NCA, Data Protection Commission, Cyber Security Authority, NITA

syllabus.title: E-commerce legal issues
topics: Electronic contracts: offer, acceptance, click-wrap and browse-wrap, timing, mistakes, automated agents
Electronic signatures and records; certification authorities; evidential weight
Consumer protection online: disclosure, cooling-off, unfair terms, dispute resolution; payment regulation and mobile money rules
Online marketplaces and intermediary liability; advertising and spam; taxation of digital services (the e-levy debate)

syllabus.title: ICT crime
topics: Categories: unauthorised access, data interference, system interference, misuse of devices, computer-related fraud and forgery, identity theft, child sexual abuse material, cyberstalking, hate speech
Ghana's Cybersecurity Act and the Electronic Transactions Act offences; the Budapest Convention and the Malabo Convention
Investigation powers, interception, digital evidence and admissibility; international cooperation
Case studies: sakawa and romance fraud, SIM-box fraud, mobile-money fraud, ransomware
Cybersecurity obligations on organisations and critical information infrastructure

syllabus.title: Intellectual property
topics: Copyright: subsistence, ownership, duration, infringement, fair use and fair dealing; software and databases as works; Ghana's Copyright Act 2005
Patents and software patents; trade secrets and confidentiality; trademarks and domain names (UDRP)
Licensing: proprietary EULAs, open-source licences (GPL, BSD, Apache) and their obligations; Creative Commons
Digital rights management, piracy, and enforcement; ARIPO and international treaties (Berne, TRIPS)
Ownership of code written by employees, contractors and students; AI-generated works

syllabus.title: IT contracts
topics: Software development, licensing, SaaS and cloud contracts; outsourcing and service level agreements
Key clauses: scope, acceptance, warranties, liability caps, indemnities, IP ownership, termination, dispute resolution
Agile contracts and change control; escrow; government procurement of IT in Ghana
Reading and negotiating a real contract

syllabus.title: Information privacy and Internet governance
topics: Privacy as a right: constitutional and international foundations; surveillance, profiling, facial recognition
Internet governance: ICANN, IETF, ITU, multistakeholder model; net neutrality; Internet shutdowns and content regulation in Africa
Freedom of expression online, defamation, platform liability and content moderation
Lawful interception, data retention and the balance with security

syllabus.title: Data protection and freedom of information
topics: Ghana's Data Protection Act 843: principles, data controllers and processors, registration, data subject rights, the Commission, enforcement
GDPR: lawful bases, consent, rights, DPOs, DPIAs, breach notification, international transfers, fines
CCPA/CPRA, PIPEDA and POPIA compared: scope, rights, enforcement; the African Union data policy framework
Freedom of information: Ghana's Right to Information Act 2019 and access to public records
Designing a compliant system: privacy by design, data minimisation, retention, security, breach response; writing a privacy notice

syllabus.title: Work and wealth
topics: Automation, AI and employment; the gig economy and platform work; telework
The digital divide within Ghana and globally; digital inclusion and accessibility obligations
Wealth concentration, big tech and competition law; data as an asset
Environmental effects: energy, e-waste, and responsible disposal

syllabus.title: Professional ethics and social issues
topics: Ethical theories: utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics, social contract; applying them to cases
Professional codes: ACM, IEEE, BCS; whistleblowing, conflicts of interest, competence, honesty
Ethics of AI and algorithms: bias, transparency, accountability, autonomous systems
Case analyses: Therac-25, Volkswagen emissions, Cambridge Analytica, a Ghanaian data breach
Capstone: a policy brief or ethical analysis presented and defended

courses.title: Malware Analysis and Reverse Engineering
topics: Types of malware
Safe analysis environments
Static analysis
Dynamic analysis
Reading assembly and binaries
Mobile malware
Writing detection signatures
courses.description: Analysing malicious software to understand what it does and how to detect it: malware types, building a safe analysis environment, static and dynamic analysis, reading assembly and binaries, mobile malware, and writing detection signatures. Practised only on isolated, disposable virtual machines and a simulated network in the browser, so that live samples are detonated and reversed without any risk to real systems.
modelledOn: Sikorski and Honig, Practical Malware Analysis
Ligh, Case, Levy and Walters, The Art of Memory Forensics
Yosifovich, Ionescu, Russinovich and Solomon, Windows Internals
GIAC Reverse Engineering Malware (GREM) objectives
outcomes: Classify malware by type and behaviour and describe its goals and propagation.
Build and operate a safe, isolated analysis lab that contains a live sample.
Perform static analysis to characterise a binary without running it.
Perform dynamic analysis to observe a sample's behaviour and network activity.
Read assembly and disassembled binaries to reconstruct a program's logic.
Analyse mobile malware and write signatures and indicators that detect a family.

syllabus.title: Types of malware
topics: Taxonomy: viruses, worms, trojans, backdoors, rootkits, ransomware, spyware, bankers and botnets
The malware lifecycle: delivery, execution, persistence, command and control, actions on objectives
Monetisation: ransomware, banking trojans and mobile-money-stealing malware in West Africa
Notable families and campaigns and what each teaches about technique
The analyst's goals: triage, detection, attribution and remediation

syllabus.title: Safe analysis environments
topics: Isolation first: disposable virtual machines, snapshots and a sandboxed, air-gapped simulated network
Preventing escape and accidental spread; handling and storing samples safely
A fake internet: simulated DNS, web and command-and-control services for containment
Building a repeatable analysis workflow and evidence log
Legal and ethical handling of live malicious code

syllabus.title: Static analysis
topics: Fingerprinting a sample: hashes, file type and antivirus consensus
Strings, imports and exports; what the import table reveals about capability
The portable executable format: headers, sections, entry point and resources
Packing and obfuscation: detecting a packer and the limits of static analysis
Extracting indicators without execution

syllabus.title: Dynamic analysis
topics: Detonating a sample under instrumentation on an isolated virtual machine
Monitoring processes, files, registry and services to see persistence and droppers
Observing network behaviour against the simulated internet; extracting the command-and-control protocol
Automated sandboxes and their evasion; detecting analysis-aware malware
Building a behavioural report and a timeline of actions

syllabus.title: Reading assembly and binaries
topics: x86 and x64 registers, memory, the stack and the calling conventions
Common instructions and how C constructs compile to assembly
Disassembly and decompilation with an interactive disassembler; functions, cross-references and graphs
Recognising loops, switches, structures and API calls in disassembly
Identifying encryption, encoding and the sample's core logic

syllabus.title: Unpacking and anti-analysis
topics: Anti-debugging, anti-virtual-machine and timing checks and how to bypass them
Unpacking: finding the original entry point and dumping the unpacked image
Debugging a sample: breakpoints, stepping and patching to reach hidden behaviour
Decoding obfuscated strings and configuration
Documenting the de-obfuscation so a colleague can reproduce it

syllabus.title: Mobile malware
topics: The Android application package and permission model; sideloading risk on budget phones
Static analysis of an app: manifest, permissions and decompiled code
Dynamic analysis in an emulator; intercepting a mobile-money-stealing overlay or SMS interceptor
Fake banking and mobile-money apps as a regional threat
Indicators and defences for mobile platforms

syllabus.title: Writing detection signatures
topics: From analysis to detection: turning findings into reliable indicators
Writing YARA rules on strings and byte patterns; avoiding over- and under-matching
Network and host indicators and mapping behaviour to MITRE ATT&CK techniques
Testing a signature for false positives against benign software
Sharing indicators responsibly with a community or regulator

syllabus.title: A full malware investigation
topics: Combining static, dynamic and code analysis into one assessment of an unknown sample
Determining capability, persistence, command and control and impact
Writing an analysis report with indicators and remediation guidance
Capstone: fully reverse a provided sample and deliver detection signatures and a report

courses.title: MLOps and Model Deployment
topics: The machine learning life cycle
Experiment tracking and versioning
Packaging and serving models
Deployment on cloud and on device
Monitoring and drift
Automated retraining pipelines
Cost, latency and offline inference
courses.description: Taking machine learning from notebook to production: the model life cycle, data and experiment versioning, packaging and serving models behind APIs, deployment to the cloud and to phones and edge devices, monitoring for drift, automated retraining pipelines, and the cost and latency trade-offs of online and offline inference. Practised end to end in browser notebooks, simulated terminals and a simulated cloud console, taught to the depth of a strong final-year MLOps course and the machine learning engineering certifications.
modelledOn: Huyen, Designing Machine Learning Systems
Lakshmanan, Robinson and Munn, Machine Learning Design Patterns
Treveil et al., Introducing MLOps
Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer and AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate objectives
outcomes: Describe the machine learning life cycle and design a system that connects data, training, deployment and feedback.
Version data, code and models and track experiments so that any result can be reproduced.
Package models in containers and serve them through batch, online and streaming interfaces with tested APIs.
Deploy models to cloud platforms and to low-cost phones and edge devices, choosing compression techniques to meet latency and size budgets.
Monitor deployed models for data and concept drift and build automated, gated retraining pipelines.
Estimate and reduce the cost and latency of inference and design for intermittent connectivity and offline use.

syllabus.title: The machine learning life cycle
topics: Why most models never reach production; technical debt in ML systems; the gap between research and engineering
Life cycle stages: problem framing, data collection, training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, feedback
Roles and maturity levels: data scientist, ML engineer, platform team; MLOps maturity models
Framing business metrics against model metrics: a fraud detector for a mobile money operator

syllabus.title: Experiment tracking and versioning
topics: Reproducibility: random seeds, environment pinning, deterministic training, lock files
Data versioning with DVC and content-addressed storage; dataset snapshots and lineage
Experiment tracking with MLflow: parameters, metrics, artefacts, comparing runs
Model registries: model versions, stages, approvals and model cards
Feature stores: offline and online features, point-in-time correctness and training-serving skew

syllabus.title: Packaging and serving models
topics: Serialising models: pickle and its risks, ONNX, TorchScript, SavedModel
Serving a model behind a REST API with FastAPI; input validation, schemas and error handling
Containerising the model server with Docker; health checks, configuration and image size
Batch, online and streaming inference; dedicated serving frameworks and model servers
Testing ML code: unit tests for features, model behaviour tests, contract tests for the API

syllabus.title: Deployment on cloud and on device
topics: Cloud deployment options: virtual machines, managed endpoints, Kubernetes, serverless functions
Release strategies: shadow deployment, canary releases, blue-green, A/B tests and interleaving
Model compression: quantisation, pruning, knowledge distillation; measuring accuracy loss
On-device inference with TensorFlow Lite and ONNX Runtime on low-cost Android phones; WebAssembly and WebGPU in the browser
A crop disease classifier that works offline on a farmer's phone and syncs results when connectivity returns

syllabus.title: Automated retraining pipelines
topics: CI/CD for ML: continuous integration of code and data, continuous training, continuous delivery of models
Pipeline orchestration: directed acyclic graphs, Airflow, Kubeflow Pipelines; idempotent steps and caching
Triggers for retraining: schedules, data volume, performance drops; validation gates and human approval
Data validation: schema checks, expectations, anomaly detection on incoming data
Rollback and model governance: audit trails, reproducible builds and sign-off

syllabus.title: Monitoring and drift
topics: What to monitor: system metrics, prediction distributions, input features, delayed ground truth
Data drift, concept drift and label shift; seasonal effects such as harvest cycles and festive spending
Detecting drift: population stability index, Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, Jensen-Shannon divergence, windowed statistics
Observability stack for models: logging predictions, dashboards with Prometheus and Grafana, alerting thresholds
Feedback loops and fairness monitoring across regions, languages and user groups

syllabus.title: Cost, latency and offline inference
topics: Latency budgets: p50, p95 and p99; batching, caching and hardware choice between CPU and GPU
Estimating inference cost per thousand predictions in dollars and cedis; autoscaling and scale to zero
Designing for unreliable networks and power: offline-first apps, store-and-forward, USSD and SMS fallbacks
Serving large models economically: distillation, quantised models, retrieval to shrink prompts

syllabus.title: Responsible operation and capstone
topics: Security of ML systems: model theft, data poisoning, adversarial inputs, supply-chain risks in model files
Privacy and compliance: personal data in training sets, retention and the Data Protection Act
Incident response for models: runbooks, kill switches and fallbacks to rules
Capstone: a versioned, containerised, monitored model with an automated retraining pipeline and a cost report

courses.title: Mobile Application Development
topics: Characteristics and history of mobile application frameworks
Android framework overview
Application models
User-interface design for mobile
Managing application data
Integrating cloud services
Networking, OS and hardware integration
Enterprise requirements: performance, scalability, modifiability, availability, security
Testing
Publishing, deployment, maintenance
courses.description: Building production-quality mobile applications: the history and characteristics of mobile frameworks, the Android framework and application models, mobile UI design, local data, cloud integration, networking and hardware, enterprise requirements, testing, and publishing to the store, with a complete app shipped by the end. Taught to the depth of a leading mobile development course.
modelledOn: Android Developers documentation and the Modern Android Development guides
Phillips, Stewart, Marsicano and Gardner, Android Programming: The Big Nerd Ranch Guide
Google Material Design guidelines
Apple Human Interface Guidelines and Flutter documentation for cross-platform comparison
outcomes: Compare native, cross-platform and web approaches to mobile development and choose for a given product.
Build Android apps with activities, fragments, navigation, lifecycle-aware components and Jetpack libraries.
Design mobile interfaces that follow platform guidelines and work on small, slow and offline devices.
Store data locally with preferences, files and a database and synchronise with cloud services.
Use networking, sensors, location, camera and background work correctly and efficiently.
Meet enterprise requirements for performance, scalability, modifiability, availability and security, test the app, and publish and maintain it.

syllabus.title: Characteristics and history of mobile application frameworks
topics: From J2ME and Symbian to iOS and Android; the app store model
Constraints: battery, memory, screen, touch, connectivity, interruptions, fragmentation
Native (Kotlin/Android, Swift/iOS), cross-platform (Flutter, React Native, Kotlin Multiplatform), progressive web apps; trade-offs
Mobile in Ghana: Android dominance, low-end devices, data cost, USSD and SMS fallbacks

syllabus.title: Android framework overview
topics: Android architecture: Linux kernel, ART, framework, apps; the SDK, Android Studio, emulators and real devices
Kotlin essentials for Android: null safety, lambdas, coroutines
Project structure, Gradle, the manifest, resources and configuration qualifiers
Activities and their lifecycle; intents and intent filters; permissions model
Debugging, logging and the profiler

syllabus.title: Application models
topics: Components: activities, services, broadcast receivers, content providers; tasks and the back stack
Architecture: MVVM with ViewModel and LiveData/StateFlow; repository pattern; dependency injection (Hilt)
Fragments and the Navigation component; single-activity apps
Process lifecycle, configuration changes and saving state

syllabus.title: User-interface design for mobile
topics: Layouts: ConstraintLayout and Jetpack Compose; lists with RecyclerView and LazyColumn
Material Design: components, theming, typography, dark mode; adaptive layouts for phones and tablets
Input, gestures, animation, accessibility (TalkBack, content descriptions, touch targets)
Localisation (Twi, Ga, Ewe, French), right-to-left support, offline and error states
Designing for low-end devices and slow networks

syllabus.title: Managing application data
topics: SharedPreferences and DataStore; internal and external storage; scoped storage
SQLite with Room: entities, DAOs, migrations, queries as Flows
Content providers and sharing data between apps
Caching strategies and offline-first design

syllabus.title: Integrating cloud services
topics: Firebase or Supabase: authentication, realtime database or Postgres, storage, push notifications, analytics, crash reporting
Synchronisation and conflict resolution; background sync with WorkManager
Payments: mobile money APIs and in-app billing
Backend-as-a-service versus a custom REST or GraphQL API

syllabus.title: Networking, OS and hardware integration
topics: HTTP with Retrofit/OkHttp or Ktor; JSON parsing; handling slow and failing networks; image loading
Coroutines and threading; services, foreground services and WorkManager; notifications
Location and maps, camera and media, sensors, Bluetooth and NFC; runtime permissions
Battery and data efficiency; Doze and app standby

syllabus.title: Enterprise requirements
topics: Performance: startup time, jank, memory leaks, profiling tools, baseline profiles
Scalability and modifiability: modular architecture, feature modules, clean architecture, API versioning
Availability: offline operation, retry and backoff, graceful degradation
Security: secure storage (Keystore), certificate pinning, obfuscation, OWASP Mobile Top Ten, data protection compliance

syllabus.title: Testing
topics: Unit tests with JUnit and mocking; testing ViewModels and repositories; coroutine tests
Instrumented and UI tests with Espresso and Compose testing; screenshot tests
Test pyramid for mobile; device farms and emulator matrices; CI for Android
Beta testing with internal and closed tracks; collecting feedback

syllabus.title: Publishing, deployment and maintenance
topics: App signing, Play Console, store listing, content ratings, privacy policy and data safety forms; iOS App Store comparison
Release management: versioning, staged rollouts, feature flags, in-app updates
Monitoring crashes, ANRs, performance and reviews; analytics and A/B tests
Maintenance: dependency updates, OS version migrations, deprecations
Capstone: a complete app for a local need (market prices, clinic appointments, transport) published to a test track

courses.title: Reinforcement Learning
topics: Agents, environments and rewards
Markov decision processes
Dynamic programming
Monte Carlo and temporal-difference learning
Q-learning
Policy gradient methods
Deep reinforcement learning
courses.description: Learning to act from reward: agents and environments, multi-armed bandits, Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo and temporal-difference methods, Q-learning, policy gradients and deep reinforcement learning. Every algorithm is derived, implemented and watched learning in simulated grid worlds and control environments in the browser, taught to the depth of a strong final-year reinforcement learning course.
modelledOn: Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
Szepesvári, Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning
Bertsekas, Reinforcement Learning and Optimal Control
Lattimore and Szepesvári, Bandit Algorithms
outcomes: Formulate sequential decision problems as bandits or Markov decision processes with suitable states, actions and rewards.
Derive the Bellman equations and solve known MDPs with policy evaluation, policy iteration and value iteration.
Implement Monte Carlo, temporal-difference and Q-learning methods and analyse their bias, variance and convergence.
Apply function approximation and policy gradient methods, including actor-critic algorithms, to large and continuous problems.
Train and debug deep reinforcement learning agents and evaluate them with reproducible experiments.
Assess the risks of reward misspecification and unsafe exploration when applying reinforcement learning to real systems.

syllabus.title: Agents, environments and rewards
topics: The reinforcement learning problem: agent, environment, state, action, reward, return; how it differs from supervised learning
Episodic and continuing tasks; discounting; the reward hypothesis and reward design
Environments as code: the Gymnasium interface, grid worlds, cart-pole, mountain car
Examples: game playing, robotics, recommender systems, irrigation scheduling and traffic signal control

syllabus.title: Multi-armed bandits
topics: The exploration-exploitation dilemma; action-value estimates and incremental updates
Epsilon-greedy, optimistic initial values, upper confidence bound and Thompson sampling
Regret and its bounds; non-stationary bandits and constant step sizes
Contextual bandits: choosing which SMS reminder or promotion to send a mobile money customer

syllabus.title: Markov decision processes
topics: The Markov property; transition dynamics and reward functions; finite MDPs
Policies, state-value and action-value functions
The Bellman expectation and optimality equations derived; optimal policies
Partially observable problems and belief states in brief

syllabus.title: Dynamic programming
topics: Iterative policy evaluation; the contraction mapping argument for convergence
The policy improvement theorem; policy iteration
Value iteration; asynchronous and generalised policy iteration
The curse of dimensionality and why model-free methods are needed; an inventory MDP for a community pharmacy

syllabus.title: Monte Carlo and temporal-difference learning
topics: Monte Carlo prediction: first-visit and every-visit; Monte Carlo control with exploring starts
On-policy and off-policy learning; ordinary and weighted importance sampling
TD(0) prediction and bootstrapping; the bias-variance trade-off between Monte Carlo and TD
n-step methods, eligibility traces and TD(lambda)
SARSA and expected SARSA for on-policy control; the cliff-walking comparison

syllabus.title: Q-learning and function approximation
topics: Q-learning as off-policy TD control; convergence conditions; maximisation bias and double Q-learning
Model-based planning: Dyna-Q, prioritised sweeping, Monte Carlo tree search in brief
Value function approximation: linear features, tile coding, semi-gradient methods
The deadly triad of function approximation, bootstrapping and off-policy learning; divergence examples
Least-squares TD and fitted Q iteration

syllabus.title: Policy gradient methods
topics: Parameterised policies: softmax and Gaussian; the policy gradient theorem derived
REINFORCE; baselines and variance reduction
Actor-critic methods; advantage estimation and generalised advantage estimation
Trust regions and proximal policy optimisation; natural gradients in brief
Continuous control: deterministic policy gradients, DDPG, TD3 and soft actor-critic

syllabus.title: Deep reinforcement learning
topics: Deep Q-networks: experience replay, target networks, learning from pixels
DQN improvements: double DQN, duelling networks, prioritised replay, distributional methods
Engineering deep RL: hyperparameters, seeds, reward scaling, debugging learning curves, reproducibility
Exploration in hard problems: intrinsic motivation, curiosity and count-based bonuses
Offline reinforcement learning from logged data; reinforcement learning from human feedback for language models

syllabus.title: Reinforcement learning in the real world
topics: Multi-agent reinforcement learning and self-play in brief
Reward misspecification, reward hacking and safe exploration
Simulation-to-reality transfer; recognising when reinforcement learning is the wrong tool
Capstone: an agent for a simulated problem such as microgrid battery scheduling or traffic lights at an Accra junction, with an experiment report

courses.title: Responsible AI
topics: Harms from AI systems
Fairness and bias
Transparency and explainability
Privacy and data rights
Safety and robustness
AI governance and regulation
AI for African contexts
courses.description: How to build and govern artificial intelligence that is fair, transparent, private, safe and accountable: the harms AI systems cause, fairness and bias, transparency and explainability, privacy and data rights, safety and robustness, governance and regulation, and what responsible AI means for African contexts. Taught through browser-based exercises that audit real datasets and models for bias, probe them for failures and apply mitigations, grounding each principle in hands-on measurement rather than theory alone.
modelledOn: Barocas, Hardt and Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning
O'Neil, Weapons of Math Destruction
NIST AI Risk Management Framework
ISO/IEC 42001 Artificial Intelligence Management System
outcomes: Identify and categorise the harms an AI system can cause across its lifecycle.
Measure bias and apply fairness definitions, recognising the trade-offs between them.
Explain model behaviour with interpretability methods and produce transparency documentation.
Protect privacy and uphold data rights when collecting and using data.
Assess and improve the safety and robustness of a model against failures and attacks.
Apply governance frameworks and regulation and adapt responsible-AI practice to African contexts.

syllabus.title: Harms from AI systems
topics: A taxonomy of harms: allocative, representational, quality-of-service, and harms to autonomy and dignity
Where harm enters the lifecycle: problem framing, data, model, deployment and feedback loops
Case studies: biased hiring and credit scoring, flawed facial recognition, content-moderation failures
Harms with regional weight: credit scoring for the unbanked and mobile-money risk models
Stakeholders and the diffusion of responsibility; who bears the cost

syllabus.title: Fairness and bias
topics: Sources of bias: historical, representation, measurement, aggregation and deployment bias
Group fairness definitions: demographic parity, equalised odds, predictive parity
Individual and counterfactual fairness; the impossibility results that force trade-offs
Measuring disparity and auditing a model on a held-out dataset in the browser
Mitigations at pre-processing, in-processing and post-processing stages
Choosing protected attributes sensitively where ethnicity, language and region are involved

syllabus.title: Transparency and explainability
topics: Transparency versus explainability versus interpretability
Intrinsically interpretable models versus post-hoc explanation
Local explanations: feature attribution, LIME and Shapley-value methods
Global explanations, partial-dependence and the limits and misuse of explanations
Documentation: model cards, datasheets for datasets and system fact sheets
Explaining a decision to an affected user such as a declined loan applicant

syllabus.title: Privacy and data rights
topics: Personal data, consent, purpose limitation and data minimisation
Ghana's Data Protection Act 843 and the role of the Data Protection Commission
Re-identification risk and the failure of naive anonymisation
Privacy-preserving techniques: k-anonymity, differential privacy and federated learning in brief
Data collection ethics for low-resource languages and communities; informed consent in practice

syllabus.title: Safety and robustness
topics: Distribution shift and why accuracy on a test set overstates real-world reliability
Adversarial examples and data poisoning; probing a model's brittleness in the browser
Uncertainty estimation, calibration and knowing when to abstain
Robustness to missing data, noisy inputs and intermittent connectivity
Monitoring, drift detection and safe rollback after deployment

syllabus.title: AI governance and regulation
topics: Risk-based governance: the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and an AI management system
The emerging regulatory landscape and risk tiers; sectoral rules for finance and health
Impact assessments, audits and accountability structures within an organisation
Procurement and third-party model risk; responsibility across a supply chain
Standards, voluntary codes and the limits of self-regulation

syllabus.title: AI for African contexts
topics: Data scarcity and representation for African languages, faces and settings
Infrastructure realities: offline and low-bandwidth deployment, on-device models, power cuts
Data sovereignty, benefit sharing and avoiding extractive data practices
Continental and national policy: the African Union's AI stance and local strategy
Building appropriate, locally governed AI rather than importing ill-fitting systems

syllabus.title: A responsible-AI assessment
topics: Combining fairness, transparency, privacy and safety into one evaluation of a system
Producing an impact assessment and a mitigation and monitoring plan
Communicating findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders
Capstone: audit a provided model and dataset and deliver a responsible-AI report with fixes

courses.title: Site Reliability Engineering
topics: Reliability goals and error budgets
Monitoring and alerting
Incident response
Postmortems
Capacity planning
Load balancing and failover
Automation and toil reduction
courses.description: Running production services reliably at scale: reliability goals expressed as service level indicators, objectives and error budgets, monitoring and alerting, incident response and blameless postmortems, capacity planning, load balancing and failover, and automation that removes toil. Practised through simulated outages, on-call rotations and failover drills in browser-based consoles and terminals, taught to the depth of a strong final-year reliability engineering course.
modelledOn: Beyer, Jones, Petoff and Murphy, Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems
Beyer, Murphy, Rensin, Kawahara and Thorne, The Site Reliability Workbook
Nygard, Release It! Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software
Allspaw, The Art of Capacity Planning
outcomes: Define service level indicators and objectives that reflect user experience and manage releases with error budgets.
Design monitoring and alerting that pages humans only for urgent, actionable, user-visible problems.
Lead and take part in incident response using clear roles, communication and mitigation-first practices.
Write blameless postmortems that identify contributing factors and drive lasting improvements.
Forecast demand, plan capacity and design load balancing, redundancy and failover for target availability.
Measure and reduce toil through automation, safe release engineering and controlled chaos experiments.

syllabus.title: Reliability goals and error budgets
topics: What SRE is: software engineering applied to operations; how it relates to DevOps and traditional operations
Availability, latency, durability and correctness; the cost of each additional nine
Service level indicators, objectives and agreements; choosing SLIs from user journeys
Error budgets and error budget policies; balancing feature velocity against reliability
SLOs for a mobile money transfer service and a national exam results portal on release day

syllabus.title: Monitoring and alerting
topics: White-box and black-box monitoring; the four golden signals; the USE and RED methods
Metrics, logs and traces; time series, labels and cardinality; Prometheus and Grafana
Alerting on symptoms not causes; burn-rate alerts on SLOs; reducing alert fatigue
Synthetic probes and real user monitoring; monitoring from networks in different African countries
Dashboards that answer questions; runbooks linked from every alert

syllabus.title: Incident response
topics: On-call: rotations, handovers, escalation policies, sustainable load and compensation
Incident command: incident commander, operations lead, communications lead, scribe
Mitigate first: rollbacks, feature flags, traffic draining, graceful degradation
Communication during incidents: status pages, stakeholder updates, customer messages
Simulated incidents: a database failover, a bad deploy and an upstream payment provider outage

syllabus.title: Postmortems
topics: Blameless culture and why blame hides information
Writing a postmortem: timeline, impact, detection, response, contributing factors, action items
Analysis techniques: five whys and its limits, causal diagrams, systems thinking about complex failures
Tracking action items to completion; learning from public postmortems of major outages

syllabus.title: Capacity planning
topics: Demand forecasting: organic growth, seasonality, events such as month-end salaries and festive seasons
Load testing and finding the saturation point; queueing theory basics and Little's law
Headroom, N+1 and N+2 redundancy; provisioning lead times for cloud and on-premises hardware
Autoscaling policies and their failure modes; cost as a capacity constraint
Planning around unreliable power and connectivity: generators, UPS, multiple internet providers

syllabus.title: Load balancing and failover
topics: Layer 4 and layer 7 load balancing; algorithms: round robin, least connections, consistent hashing
Health checks, connection draining, overload protection, load shedding and rate limiting
Resilience patterns: timeouts, retries with jitter, circuit breakers, bulkheads; cascading failures
DNS and global load balancing; active-active and active-passive multi-region designs
Database replication and failover; recovery time and recovery point objectives; disaster recovery drills

syllabus.title: Automation and toil reduction
topics: Defining and measuring toil; the toil budget
Automation maturity: from runbooks to scripts to self-healing systems; when not to automate
Release engineering: CI/CD, canary releases, progressive delivery, automated rollback
Configuration as code and infrastructure as code as reliability tools

syllabus.title: Reliability practice and capstone
topics: Chaos engineering: hypotheses, blast radius, game days
Production readiness reviews and launch checklists
Organising SRE: embedded, centralised and consulting models; reliability in small teams
Capstone: define SLOs, build monitoring, run an incident drill and write the postmortem for a simulated service
